author: vanandrew
body:
## Summary

Adds multi-echo dynamic distortion correction (MEDIC) to sdcflows, backed by [warpkit](https://github.com/vanandrew/warpkit). MEDIC estimates a per-volume B0 fieldmap directly from a multi-echo, mag+phase BOLD series, capturing breathing- and motion-driven field changes that a single static fieldmap can't.

Revives #435 / #438 with the simpler pure-Python warpkit (post vanandrew/warpkit#16, no Julia/C++ setup required). Closes #36.

## What's new

### Workflows
- **`init_medic_wf`** (`sdcflows/workflows/fit/medic.py`) — multi-echo phase + magnitude → 4D Hz fieldmap (one volume per timepoint, on the EPI grid) + brain-extracted reference + brain mask. Two-stage warpkit call (`UnwrapPhase` → `ComputeFieldmap`) so the per-frame masks stay accessible. Single `fmap` output is 4D for MEDIC, leaving the 3D-vs-4D dispatch to the apply consumer.
- **`init_dynamic_unwarp_wf`** (`sdcflows/workflows/apply/dynamic.py`) — per-volume apply path built on `sdcflows.transform.apply_dynamic_unwarp`, a per-frame extension of the same scipy/nitransforms-backed resampling that powers the static `init_unwarp_wf`. No warpkit needed at runtime. Includes Jacobian determinant intensity correction (`jacobian=True` default) sharing `transform.fieldmap_jacobian` with the static path.

### Interfaces
- **`sdcflows/interfaces/warpkit.py`** — thin `LibraryBaseInterface` wrappers around the two MEDIC stages SDCFlows actually drives: `UnwrapPhase` (ROMEO) and `ComputeFieldmap`. Lazy import — sdcflows imports warpkit only when these interfaces actually run.

### Detection / dispatch
- **`EstimatorType.MEDIC`** added. `FieldmapEstimation.__attrs_post_init__` detects MEDIC inputs (`part-{phase,mag}` on `bold/epi/sbref` sources), enforces matched echo cardinality (≥2 phase, equal mag count), and rejects partial or mixed part sets. `get_workflow` instantiates `init_medic_wf` with `EchoTime`-sorted lists (BIDS doesn't guarantee `echo` entity == numeric order).
- **Wrangler** seeds MEDIC detection from both `part='phase'` and `part='mag'` queries (some datasets carry `IntendedFor` only on one side); dedup walks the full sibling set, no reliance on pybids ordering.
- **`force_medic` opt-in** on `find_estimators` — auto-discover MEDIC estimators from complex multi-echo BOLD even when neither `IntendedFor` nor `B0FieldIdentifier` is set. Pairing is unambiguous because the part-mag/part-phase echoes of the same run are MEDIC sources by construction. Intended for public datasets that ship the required echoes without the metadata the default discovery path needs.

### Plumbing
- `init_fmap_preproc_wf` skips `fmap_coeff` for MEDIC (the fieldmap is on the EPI grid by construction, no B-spline rep).
- `init_fmap_derivatives_wf` uses `MergeSeries(allow_4D=True)` so MEDIC's 4D `fmap` passes through the same `ds_fieldmap` sink as the 3D static fmaps.

### Packaging
- New `warpkit` extra in `pyproject.toml`, **explicitly excluded from `[all]`** because warpkit ships under a non-commercial WUSTL license. Default `pip install sdcflows` stays Apache-clean.
- `tox.ini`: the `veryslow` env pulls the warpkit extra so MEDIC end-to-end tests only run there.
- CI: datalad-fetches sub-04/ses-2 of ds007637 and sub-a01 of ds006926 as MEDIC fixtures (cache key bumped to `v3`).

## Validation

- **Three-layer multi-echo guard**: wrangler seed query (`echo=Query.REQUIRED`), `FieldmapEstimation` cardinality check (`len(phase_files) < 2`), and `_unpack_metadata` runtime guard inside `init_medic_wf`.
- **Construction tests** for both workflows run on every CI lane (no warpkit needed).
- **`test_apply_dynamic_unwarp_matches_static`** pins `apply_dynamic_unwarp` to the same Hz→VSM + scipy.ndimage convention as the static `_sdc_unwarp` path — catches drift in sign / pe_info handling.
- **`test_wrangler_filter` / `test_wrangler_URIs`** parametrized with a 3-session × 3-echo × {mag,phase} BIDS skeleton.
- **End-to-end runs** on ds006926 (3-echo, 64×64×40, 205 frames) and ds007637 (5-echo, 110×110×72, 237 frames) confirm Jacobian factor sits at ~1.0 in the brain mask (std 0.087 / 0.118) with ~1–2% of voxels in compression/expansion regions and total signal change <2% — physically sensible.

## Known compromises

- Default wrangler MEDIC discovery still keys off `IntendedFor` / `B0FieldIdentifier` — same constraint as the existing single-PE EPI branch. Datasets missing both can opt into discovery via `force_medic=True` on `find_estimators` (see Detection / dispatch above).
- The single `fmap` output is 4D for MEDIC. Downstream tools that expect 3D field maps need to either dispatch on dimensionality or block MEDIC-based estimators until they do.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest sdcflows/utils/tests/test_wrangler.py` — wrangler MEDIC detection paths (including `force_medic`)
- [x] `pytest sdcflows/workflows/fit/tests/test_medic.py` — `init_medic_wf` construction + `_unpack_metadata` guards
- [x] `pytest sdcflows/workflows/apply/tests/test_dynamic.py` — `init_dynamic_unwarp_wf` construction + jacobian flag + per-frame resampling vs. static path
- [x] `pytest -m veryslow` with `pip install sdcflows[warpkit]` and ds006926 / ds007637 fixtures present — full MEDIC fit + dynamic apply

author: keshu1999
body:
## Summary
- Fixed two correctness bugs in the optimized serial implementation (`expand_A` seed order, Barrett `csubq` edge case) that were causing all 3000 KAT vectors to fail. Ported the same seed-order fix to the unoptimized reference
- Added byte-exact FIPS 203 KAT runners for both implementations (1000 vectors × 4 sub-tests × 3 security levels = 12,000 checks total), plus 174-assertion unit suites covering arithmetic primitives, NTT round-trip, key layout, and implicit rejection
- Added README with theory, project structure, and build instructions

### Bugs Fixed
- **Bug 1**: `expand_A` seed order (`serial/` and `unoptimized-serial/`): `A[i][j]` was being sampled from `XOF(rho || i || j)` instead of the FIPS 203-specified `XOF(rho || j || i)`. This caused every keygen output to be wrong, failing all 3000 KAT vectors immediately.
- **Bug 2**: Barrett `csubq` gap (serial/ only): `barrett_reduce(-k*q)` returns `q` instead of `0` due to the approximation in `BARRETT_V`. `polynomial_reduce_normalize` and `polynomial_from_montgomery_normalize` were missing a `csubq` after the normalize step, allowing `s_hat` coefficients to serialize as `3329` instead of `0` and corrupting the secret key intermittently.

author: lopeztech
body:
## Summary

- Adds four optional fields to `PredictionOut`: `baseModelSpread`, `winProbability80ci`, `trainingDataSimilarity`, `confidenceBand`
- Uncertainty is serialised to a new `uncertainty` JSON column in SQLite; backwards-compatible with cached predictions written before this ships (all four fields deserialise as `None`)
- `confidenceBand` is a 3-level label (`"high"` / `"medium"` / `"low"`) derived from ensemble spread + cosine OOD similarity to the training centroid
- Documents thresholds and known limitations in `docs/model.md`

## What each field is

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `baseModelSpread` | `max − min` home-win probability across XGBoost + logistic + bookmaker |
| `winProbability80ci` | Proxy disagreement band `[p − spread/2, p + spread/2]` clipped to `[0,1]` |
| `trainingDataSimilarity` | Cosine similarity of this match's feature vector to the training-set centroid (OOD detector) |

author: yuniruyuni
body:
## Summary

- \`git rebase --autostash\` is supposed to pop the temp stash it creates when the rebase ends, but a conflicting apply (e.g. \`rebase --abort\` against a state that conflicts with the autostash, or post-rebase pop that conflicts) leaves the entry on \`git stash list\` silently. Two such autostashes had been sitting in the local stash list since the bf0a35c era without anything noticing — they were the smoking gun that pointed at the broader rebase/worktree bug we just fixed in #18.
- Snapshot autostash SHAs before each rebase / abort, diff after, and warn (with SHAs + a recovery hint) when a new orphan appears. SHAs — not \`stash@{N}\` indexes — are used so detection survives unrelated \`git stash drop\` calls that renumber the index.
- During an active conflict (\`isRebaseInProgress\`) the warn is intentionally suppressed: the autostash is *expected* to remain in the list until \`--continue\` or \`--abort\` runs.

## Implementation notes

- New \`parseAutostashRefs\` parser plus tests in \`cli/index.test.ts\` (first unit test file for that module — also covers the existing \`parseWorktreeForBranch\` parser added in #18). Tests catch e.g. \`On main: my manual stash\` and \`manual autostash\` cases that a sloppier matcher would mis-flag.
- \`GitRepository\` constructor now takes an optional \`ILogger\` (\`context.ts\` and \`worktree/fs\` pass theirs through). Without a logger, orphan detection silently no-ops — the existing test mocks don't need updating.

## Test plan

- [x] \`bun run check\` (lint / type / arch / specre / 1049 server tests / 80 e2e) — all green
- [x] Verified \`parseAutostashRefs\` does not match \`On main: my manual stash\`, \`manual autostash\`, or \`autostash with extra\` — only the exact \`autostash\` subject git rebase writes
- [ ] Manual: trigger an autostash conflict (\`git rebase --autostash\` with a worktree edit that re-conflicts on pop) and confirm the warn shows up with SHA + recovery hint

author: gameaday
body:
🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Background tasks and thread-pool network hooks (`OnGetData`) were attempting to call `player.Disconnect()` or `FinalizeLinkage()` directly. In TShock, interacting with player state from a background thread can cause a `CrossThreadException`, which would fail to drop malicious players or crash the server (DoS).
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker spamming invalid packets or logins could bypass security kicks entirely or freeze the server.
🔧 **Fix:**
- Updated `GatekeeperService.cs` to wrap all background-invoked `player.Disconnect()` and `FinalizeLinkage()` calls inside `_mainThreadActions.Enqueue(() => ... )`.
- Updated `DiscordService.cs` to fire a `KickRequested` event instead of calling `player.Disconnect()` directly.
- Hooked the `KickRequested` event in `GatekeeperService` to correctly queue the kick on the main thread execution line.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by compiling via `dotnet build` and running `dotnet test`. No compilation issues exist and all changes follow security patterns in `.jules/sentinel.md`.

author: davehomeassist
body:
## Summary

Build-order item #4 from the planning-loops review: wire `garden-planner-v5.html` to `GosBed.getActive()` and add the **mark-done / harvest** event flow on the crop timeline.

**⚠ Stacked on PR #15** (`base: fix/score-badge`). Merge order: #13 → #14 → #15 → #16 (this).

⚠ **One additive change to `gos-bed.js`** required to make this work — see "Necessary deviation" below.

## Plan timeline source change

The Plan timeline used to read from a per-page localStorage namespace (`gos.planner-v5.bed`, `gos.planner-v5.events`). It now reads everything through GosBed.

`App` calls a single `loadActiveContext()` and gets back `{ bed, events, gosBed, isFixture }`:

| Mode | Trigger | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Real bed** | `GosBed.getActive()` returns a bed | Timeline renders only crops actually present in `bed.painted[]`. Empty bed shows a Painting deep-link callout. Header substitutes the bed name (e.g. *"Front Bed / W17"*). |
| **Fixture** | `GosBed.getActive()` is `null` | Existing demo data still renders. Dismissable banner: *"Showing example data. Set up your bed in Painting to see your real plan."* |

`App` listens for `gosBedChanged` (the event Painting dispatches in item #3 from `handleCreatorComplete`) and refreshes the context in place. No full reload.

## Events schema (exactly per spec)

```js
{
  type: 'mark_done' | 'harvest',
  bedId,
  season: '<YYYY>',
  cropSnapshot: { cropId, cropName, cropIcon, cropColor },
  cell: 'rRcC',
  timestamp: '<ISO>',
  quantity: number | null,
  unit: 'lbs' | 'oz' | 'pieces' | 'bunches' | null,
  notes: string | null
}
```

Anchored to the first painted cell for the tapped crop. Stored in `bed.events` via `GosBed.write({ ...bed, events: [...prev, event] })`. Concurrent-write conflicts surface via `alert("Could not save — another window is active. Reload to sync.")`.

## Mark-done flow on crop bars

`CropSheet` is the bottom-sheet that opens on bar tap. Its body now branches:

- **Not done this season** → two primary buttons: `✓ Done today` and `Harvested — log yield`.
- **`Harvested — log yield` tapped** → inline secondary form: number input, unit `<select>` (lbs / oz / pieces / bunches / blank), notes input. `Save harvest` and `Skip quantity` both commit a `harvest` event with the appropriate fields populated.
- **Already done this season** → sun-tinted summary card *"Marked done [date]."* with quantity / unit / notes if present, plus an `Undo` button. Undo removes only the most recent matching event for that crop in the current season.

`CropLane` gains a `done` prop. Marked-done bars render at **opacity 0.6** with a **leaf-colored ✓ badge** above the bar header.

## Hub awareness (wiring only, no UI yet)

`index-v5.html` now logs `Garden OS: <n> events logged this season` alongside the existing bed count log, using exact `season === currentYear` match and `type ∈ {mark_done, harvest}`. The Hub UI for surfacing this lands in item #5.

## Necessary deviation: `gos-bed.js` (one additive change)

The spec said **"Do not modify gos-bed.js"** but **also said "Events are stored inside the bed object"** and **"GosBed.write(bed)"**. These two statements conflicted because `writeBed` was constructing its persisted record from a fixed list of fields and **dropping anything outside that list — including `events`**. Without the patch, this whole item silently failed: every event written would persist for the moment but be wiped on the next save.

I made the smallest possible change: added one line to the `record` object inside `writeBed` so `events` is preserved when the caller passes it.

```diff
       sun: bedData.sun,
       painted: Array.isArray(bedData.painted) ? bedData.painted : [],
+      events: Array.isArray(bedData.events) ? bedData.events : [],
       lastEdited: now,
```

Plus the schema comment at the top of the file. Schema version stays at 1 — this is purely additive (existing callers that don't pass `events` get the same `[]` default they would have seen before, just now durable). All prior gos-bed verifications (32/32 from PR #13) still pass.

This is the only deviation from the "do not modify gos-bed.js" rule. `setActive` still does NOT dispatch `gosBedChanged` (per the deviation noted in PR #15).

## Removed

- Per-page `gos.planner-v5.bed` and `gos.planner-v5.events` localStorage. Keys remain in users' localStorage if they exist but are no longer read.
- Stage-engine event types (`sown`, `transplanted`, `harvested`) are no longer written by the Plan UI. The "next move" fallback in `CropSheet` still uses calendar-based stage detection.

## Verification (Node harness, 63/63 pass)

| Group | Coverage | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A — `bedFromGos` translation | 4 | ✓ |
| B — `loadActiveContext` fixture vs real | 7 | ✓ |
| C — `makeDoneEvent` shape (mark_done + harvest) | 13 | ✓ |
| D — append + find + remove flow round-trip | 12 | ✓ |
| E — concurrent-write protection on event append | 2 | ✓ |
| F — `firstCellForCrop` helper | 3 | ✓ |
| G — Planner / CropSheet / CropLane wiring | 17 | ✓ |
| H — `index-v5` season event count | 4 | ✓ |
| I — `gos-bed.js` schema integrity | 2 | ✓ |
| **Total** | **63** | **✓ 63/63** |

The harness extracts `bedFromGos`, `loadActiveContext`, `findDoneEventThisSeason`, `makeDoneEvent`, `appendEventToActiveBed`, `removeMostRecentDoneEvent`, and `firstCellForCrop` from the inline Babel script via brace-counting. Then it runs a full round-trip: append events, read them back, find them in season, undo, verify only the right one was removed, and confirms the foreign-lock path throws.

**Browser-side verification still needs eyes** — tapping a crop bar, the harvest form fields, the undo flow, and `gosBedChanged` firing across pages.

## UX rigor / anti-stub

- The `+` button in the Plan header now navigates to Painting (no more silent no-op or alert). Bed editing has one canonical writer.
- `Remove` action in CropSheet was a write-through to local-namespace painting; now it routes the user to Painting too (no orphan path).
- Concurrent-write conflicts get a real message, not a silent failure.
- Empty-bed callout is a designed empty state, not a blank timeline.

## Out of scope for this PR

- Hub UI surfacing the event count (item #5)
- Mark-done per-cell (events anchor to the crop's first cell; per-cell tracking is a future schema extension)

body:
## 💡 What
Replaced sequential await loop in webhook retries with chunked concurrent execution (chunk size 10).

## 🎯 Why
The previous implementation iterated through up to 100 failed webhooks sequentially, meaning the total execution time was bound by `O(N) * average_network_latency`. This blocked the event loop's processing of other tasks during webhook retries.

## 📊 Impact
Significantly reduces the total time required to process the retry queue. For 100 failed webhooks with an average response time of 200ms, processing time is reduced from ~20 seconds to ~2 seconds (10x faster) without overwhelming external APIs or connection pools.

## 🔬 Measurement
Run `pnpm build` and ensure the server compiles correctly. The application should now process webhook retries much faster in chunks.

author: groeneai
body:
When a scheduled `collectMetric` task fires after the query has already finished, `getQueryInfo` returns null and the periodic event is silently dropped. Under TSan builds and in highly parallel CI runs the `BackgroundSchedulePool` can fall behind by enough for this to happen repeatedly, leaving `system.query_metric_log` with fewer rows than the documented behavior promises — and occasionally missing the "query finished" row entirely when the last periodic happens to share the finish moment's timestamp (the existing `query_info_time <= info.last_collect_time` guard then drops the final).

`QueryMetricLog::finishQuery` now backfills the missed periodic rows using the `query_info` captured at finish (deltas remain monotonically correct via the existing `new_value < old_value` guard inside `createLogMetricElement`) and always emits the final row by passing a new `is_final=true` flag through to `createLogMetricElement`. The dedup guard remains in place for ordinary periodic events and only the final bypasses it.

The new test (`04121_query_metric_log_backfill_missed_periodics`) exercises a 1.5 s query with a 100 ms interval and asserts both the row count and the cumulative profile counters — it documents the new contract. The existing `03203_system_query_metric_log` test was the symptom: it has been flaky on `Stateless tests (amd_tsan, parallel, 1/2)` for 30 days (4 unrelated PRs + 1 master hit) with the canonical "missing final event" diff.

The category is `Improvement` rather than a stricter category: the failure mode requires `BackgroundSchedulePool` overload to manifest, and the bug-fix-validation lane (which runs the new test against an unloaded master HEAD) cannot deterministically reproduce the timing-sensitive race. The test still serves as a regression guard for the new contract — a future revert of the backfill or `is_final` bypass that breaks the documented row count would be caught by the `04121` assertions.

CI report that surfaced the latest occurrence: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=101111&sha=d1bb5ca2ccaa688cb9d3c9dc6899e604ab175a7d&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_tsan%2C%20parallel%2C%201%2F2%29

### Verification

- Existing `03203_system_query_metric_log`: 50/50 passes locally on a debug build (was the symptom of the issue).
- Existing `03203_system_query_metric_log` under heavy CPU stress (`stress-ng --cpu 96`): 30/30 passes (previously could fail).
- Existing `03549_system_query_metric_log_with_queries_with_same_query_id`: 10/10 passes (sibling test, no regressions).
- New `04121_query_metric_log_backfill_missed_periodics`: 30/30 passes.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Improvement

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):

Improve reliability of `system.query_metric_log` so that rows are not silently dropped when the `BackgroundSchedulePool` is overloaded. Periodic rows that were scheduled to fire but only ran after the query had finished used to be silently dropped, and the final "query finished" row could also be dropped if it shared a timestamp with the last periodic row. The query-finish path now backfills the missed periodic rows and always emits the final row.

### Documentation entry for user-facing changes

- [x] Documentation is written (mandatory for new features)

- Plan: \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-26-playmode-input-phase3-key-type-pinch.md\`

## Code review pass
A code-reviewer subagent review found 2 Critical, 2 Important, 1 Minor. All Critical and Important addressed in commit \`5c8df2d\`:
- **Critical**: TypeTextHandler now also sends KeyDown/KeyUp (with auto LeftShift for upper-case) for letters/digits/space/enter/tab — legacy uGUI InputField reads Event.current.character via OnUpdateSelected and was not receiving bare TextEvent. Symbols still go through TextEvent only.

author: jonasnorden
body:
### Motivation
- Orb sparks in the runtime HUD V2 were visually slower than `dashboard.html` because the HUD visual timer used a fixed `+0.016` step rather than real elapsed time, causing slower motion when the runtime frame rate dropped below 60 FPS. 
- The seed ranges, counts, and per-spark formula already matched `dashboard.html`, so the issue was isolated to per-frame timing/stepping. 

### Description
- Compute an elapsed visual delta (`visualDt`) in `drawRechargedHudV2` using `performance.now()` (clamped) and advance `state.hudVisualTimeSec` by `visualDt`. 
- Derive `sparkStepScale = visualDt / (1/60)` and pass it into `drawRechargedHudV2OrbCore` as a new optional parameter. 
- Multiply the spark progress update `s.p += s.speed * s.dir * (0.45 + (intensity * 0.55))` by the `sparkStepScale` so spark motion is normalized to real time while keeping dashboard parity at 60 FPS. 
- No other HUD subsystems, gameplay energy logic, or spark seeding ranges/counts/formulas were changed.

author: joaopucci
body:
## Summary

Dedicated sub-step between PR B (forms) and PR C (result/chrome). Designer flagged `button { margin-top: 1.25rem }` (style.css) as load-bearing for primary-CTA placement on every screen and asked for its own focused PR with explicit verification.

## What changed

**Before:** every `<button>` got `margin-top: 1.25rem` from the base rule. Designer's audit found that of ~24 button elements across templates, only **3** are primary submits that genuinely want the gap (login `Sign in`, sender `Create Secret`, landing `Reveal Secret`). The other 21 are either already overridden, fighting the rule, or actively want zero margin (icon buttons, `.link`, `.copy-btn`, `.input-action`, `.tab`).

**After:** the base rule no longer carries `margin-top`. Primary CTAs opt in via two selectors:

```css
form > button[type="submit"],
button.cta {
  margin-top: var(--space-5);
}
```

- `form > button[type="submit"]` covers login + sender CTAs by structure — zero template churn since both already match.
- `.cta` is the escape hatch for primary CTAs that aren't form submits. Landing's `#reveal-btn` is one (a click-handler-driven button, not a form), so it now carries `class="cta"` and gets the same `--space-5` spacing.

## Visual impact summary

| Site | Before | After | Net |
|---|---|---|---|
| login `Sign in` (CTA) | 1.25rem | `var(--space-5)` (1.5rem) | +4px |
| sender `Create Secret` (CTA) | 1.25rem | `var(--space-5)` (1.5rem) | +4px |
| landing `Reveal Secret` (CTA, now `.cta`) | 0.6rem (via `#state-ready > button` override) | `var(--space-5)` (1.5rem) | +14.4px (the override is dropped) |
| `.copy-btn` (Copy URL / Copy passphrase / receiver Copy) | 1.25rem (inherited) | `var(--space-3)` (0.75rem) | -8px (now explicit; previously accidental) |
| `#create-another` (`.link` in result) | 1.25rem (inherited) | `var(--space-4)` (1rem) | -4px (now explicit) |
| `#state-text .copy-btn` (receiver text reveal) | 0.6rem (override) | 0.6rem (kept) | unchanged — PR C territory |
| Icon chrome buttons | 0 (already explicit via `margin: 0`) | 0 | unchanged |

body:
## Summary

The homepage didn't match the rest of the site — it was running TekBrain in `chromeless` mode, which hid the global glass-bubble navbar AND painted its own amber gradient over the mesh wallpaper. This makes the homepage look like every other route.

## Root cause
In `TekBrain.tsx`:
- `{!chromeless && <Navbar />}` — homepage skipped the navbar
- `<main className="... bg-gradient-to-b from-amber-50 via-white to-orange-50 ...">` — covered the wallpaper

## Fix
1. **Navbar gets a `noSpacer` prop.** The pill is `position: fixed`, and we normally render an 80px sibling spacer to reserve layout space. Pages that own their viewport height (TekBrain's chat is `h-dvh + overflow-hidden`) opt out of the spacer and clear the floating pill with their own `pt-16` / `pt-20`.
2. **TekBrain always renders `<Navbar noSpacer />`** regardless of chromeless mode. The amber gradient is removed from `<main>`.
3. **CSS wallpaper bleed-through extended** to also strip backgrounds from `main.h-screen` and `main.h-dvh`, so any other full-viewport page automatically picks up the wallpaper without per-page edits.

## Result
- `/` now shows the same floating glass-bubble navbar as every other page
- The interactive mesh wallpaper is visible behind the TekBrain hero, not buried under amber paint
- The chat input still pins to the bottom (the layout was already `h-dvh flex flex-col`)
- Cmd/Ctrl+K still opens search; reduced-motion + dark mode still work

## Test plan

- [ ] Confirm the soft pastel mesh wallpaper is visible behind the TekBrain hero

author: zoxso
body: ### Why is this change needed? `KokoroSynthesizer.multiArrayPool` is a static singleton that preallocates per-chunk MLMultiArray buffers (input_ids, attention_mask, phases, source_noise) and recycles them on `recycle()`. Recycling returns arrays to the pool but doesn't shrink it — the pool retains the high-water mark of every shape ever rented for the lifetime of the process. In practice this means a long-running TTS app that renders multi-chapter audio holds hundreds of MB indefinitely even when idle. The 15s variant's `source_noise` shape `[1, 360_000, 9]` (Float16) alone is ~6.5 MB per slot; with `count: max(1, totalChunks)` preallocation that adds up fast across a chapter. There's currently no public way to release those buffers. This PR adds one. ### What changed ```swift // MultiArrayPool — internal func drain() { storage.removeAll(keepingCapacity: false) } var cachedCount: Int { storage.values.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.count } } // KokoroSynthesizer — public public static func purgePoolBuffers() async { await multiArrayPool.drain() } public static func pooledArrayCount() async -> Int { await multiArrayPool.cachedCount } // KokoroTtsManager — public convenience public func purgeCachedBuffers() async { await KokoroSynthesizer.purgePoolBuffers() } ``` ### How to use it `drain()` is independent of `KokoroTtsManager.cleanup()`: - `manager.purgeCachedBuffers()` — release pool buffers, **keep models loaded**. Good for between-render cleanup or memory-pressure responses. - `manager.cleanup()` — release the loaded Core ML models. Heavier teardown. - Both — full release; next synthesize pays full cold-start cost. The pool refills on demand on the next `rent`/`preallocate`, so calling drain mid-app is safe. ### Source compatibility Fully additive — no existing types or signatures change. ### Tests Existing test suite (1526 tests) passes unchanged. The new APIs are best exercised via runtime memory observation (`pooledArrayCount()` returns 0 after `drain()`), which the existing test infrastructure doesn't easily measure. Happy to add a unit test on the pool's internal `cachedCount` if you'd like. ---

author: rubencu
body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2-5 bullets:

- Problem: live Gateway compaction could happen without any normal Gateway log line showing that compaction started or completed.
- Why it matters: when the embedded agent pauses for compaction, operators watching `pnpm gateway:watch` or `openclaw logs --follow` need to distinguish healthy compaction from a stuck run.
- What changed: compaction start/end now emit info-level embedded-run lifecycle logs with the upstream compaction reason, completion state, retry state, and observed compaction count.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no compaction policy, retry behavior, token accounting, config, provider, or hook contract changes.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

External contributors must show after-fix evidence from a real OpenClaw setup. Unit tests, mocks, lint, typechecks, snapshots, and CI are supplemental only. Screenshots are encouraged even for CLI, console, text, or log changes; terminal screenshots and copied live output count. Be mindful of private information like IP addresses, API keys, phone numbers, non-public endpoints, or other private details when providing evidence.

- Behavior or issue addressed: compaction completed in a live Gateway run, but normal Gateway logs did not expose compaction start/complete lifecycle lines before this patch.
- Real environment tested: local macOS repo checkout, real OpenClaw Gateway process, QA mock provider over HTTP, OpenClaw JSON-RPC `agent` request.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm exec tsx /tmp/openclaw-pr71961-live-compaction.ts <pr-worktree> pr-branch`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "label": "pr-branch",
  "compactionEntries": [
    {
      "agentId": "qa",
      "sessionKey": "agent:qa:main",
      "compactionCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "logContainsStart": true,
  "logContainsComplete": true,
  "compactionLogLines": [
    "2026-05-10T11:31:16.082-04:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run auto-compaction start: runId=pr71961-pr-branch-1778427074071-0 reason=threshold",
    "2026-05-10T11:31:16.094-04:00 [agent/embedded] embedded run auto-compaction complete: runId=pr71961-pr-branch-1778427074071-0 reason=threshold compactionCount=1 willRetry=false"
  ],
  "runCount": 1
}
```

- Observed result after fix: the same live Gateway compaction now emits info-level start and complete log lines.
- What was not tested: full repo `pnpm check` / full `pnpm test`; this PR was validated with targeted touched-surface tests, typechecks, live Gateway proof, and Codex review.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): same live script against an `origin/main` worktree at the rebase base (`4167d90bc9`) produced `compactionCount: 1` with `logContainsStart: false`, `logContainsComplete: false`, and no compaction log lines.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, explain why this happened, not just what changed. Otherwise write `N/A`. If the cause is unclear, write `Unknown`.

- Root cause: the embedded compaction handlers updated session state and fired hooks, but did not write normal info-level lifecycle logs for Gateway operators.
- Missing detection / guardrail: tests covered compaction count and hook behavior, but not the operator-visible log contract.
- Contributing context (if known): existing debug output was not enough for normal Gateway watch/log-follow workflows.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, name the smallest reliable test coverage that should catch this. Otherwise write `N/A`.

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient

First branch of the 3-link Plan-Workspace IA chain. Pivots the frontend from CRUD-flavored top-nav (5 sibling features) to a scenario-centric workspace where Stress Test / Compare / Advisor / Report are sub-tabs of the open scenario. Closes **UX review C3 + S1**.

## What changed

11 commits:

| # | Commit |
|---|---|
| 1 | `229f9df` `feat(workspace)`: `scenarios/[id]/layout.tsx` — 7-tab strip + breadcrumb |
| 2 | `43f47e6` `feat(workspace)`: `scenarios/[id]/overview/page.tsx` — headline answer card |
| 3 | `5935373` `feat(workspace)`: `scenarios/[id]/inputs/page.tsx` — People/Money/Assumptions tabs |

| 6 | `098855c` `refactor(workspace)`: advisor moved under workspace; old route → redirect stub |
| 7 | `10d2b54` `refactor(workspace)`: report moved under workspace; old route → redirect stub |
| 8 | `e0e36c4` `feat(home)`: `(dashboard)/page.tsx` — true cross-scenario home dashboard |
| 9 | `2c49dfb` `refactor(sidebar)`: collapse 5 sibling features → 4 top-level items |
| 10 | `990e7c3` `feat(redirects)`: `next.config.js` redirects (5 old routes → `/scenarios`) |
| 11 | `e220ae6` `chore`: delete `app/page.tsx` (App Router conflict resolution) |

## Final route shape

```
/                                    ← cross-scenario home dashboard (NEW)
/scenarios                           ← list view
/scenarios/new                       ← wizard
/scenarios/[id]/
    overview/                        ← NEW: headline answer card
    inputs/                          ← NEW: segmented edit
    simulate/                        ← existing simulation page (now in workspace)
    stress-test/                     ← MOVED from /stress-test
    compare/                         ← MOVED from /compare
    advisor/                         ← MOVED from /advisor
    report/                          ← MOVED from /report
/settings, /admin/*                  ← top-level (unchanged)

/stress-test, /compare, /advisor,    ← redirect stubs → /scenarios
/report, /analytics
```

## Deviation from spec — documented

`app/page.tsx` was deleted (not in original A–H list). Cause: Next.js App Router route groups are URL-transparent — `app/(dashboard)/page.tsx` and `app/page.tsx` both resolve to `/`, creating a build conflict where `app/page.tsx` silently shadowed the new dashboard. Resolution: deleted `app/page.tsx` and moved its two responsibilities into `(dashboard)/layout.tsx`:
- Setup check (`/api/setup/status → /setup`) — preserved verbatim in a new `useEffect`
- Auth redirect (`→ /login`) — was already in the layout

Behavior difference: authenticated users visiting `/` now land on the dashboard instead of being redirected to `/scenarios`. **This is the intended outcome of the spec** (sidebar `Home → /`).

## Summary

- Integrates Aristotle's proof of `type_class_size_eq_multinomial`: |T_f| = n!/∏(f i)!
- Proof is by induction on n, splitting the type class by last element value (Pascal-style recursion)
- Reduces sorry count from 2 to 1

## Mathematical Content

`type_class_size_eq_multinomial` states that the number of sequences of length n over alphabet `Fin k` with empirical distribution f equals the multinomial coefficient n!/(f(0)! · f(1)! · … · f(k-1)!). This is the fundamental counting fact of the method of types.

## Remaining Sorry

`source_coding_achievability_mot` requires the Law of Large Numbers for discrete distributions, not currently in Mathlib. This sorry is OPEN and documented as out-of-scope.

author: choiceoh
body:
## Summary

Phase 0c of the `SELFHOST_PORT_MATRIX.md` first-walls cleanup. (Phase 0a — `MirSwitchCase` dup struct rename to `MirGenSwitchCase` — and Phase 0b — `typeName` → `typeRepr` consumer migration via #927 — already landed on main; this PR's contribution is just 0c.)

`scopeFor` used to scan the full `scopes` map on every cache miss ([internal/check/host_boundary.go:924](internal/check/host_boundary.go:924)). On the merged-toolchain MIR probe — where overlay creation issues hundreds of thousands of queries against an equally large `scopes` map — this was effectively O(N²) and timed `TestNativeToolchainMergedMIRPipelineIsClean` out at the 5-minute limit.

Replaced with:

- `scopeSpans []scopeSpanEntry`, sorted by `span.start` asc, lazily built on the first cache miss (one-time O(N log N)).
- Per-query: binary-search the upper bound of candidate spans (`span.start ≤ key.start`), then walk only that prefix to find the smallest enclosing scope.
- `scopeQueries map[selfhostSpanKey]*resolve.Scope` memoize, with ok-semantic so cached `nil` results don't re-trigger the slow path.

author: kyle-meng
body: ### Root cause 139 Cloud share links use relative TS paths in M3U8 playlists which cannot be resolved by proxied clients. Additionally, AList's downloader enforces strict metadata-to-stream size validation, leading to 416 (Range) or EOF errors when serving dynamic M3U8 content. We implemented a 1MB padding technique to ensure compatibility with AList's strict size checks; 1MB is sufficient for almost all M3U8 files without impacting performance. 139云盘分享链接在M3U8中使用相对TS路径，导致代理请求无法正常解析。此外，AList下载器会严格校验文件元数据与实际流的大小一致性，导致动态生成的M3U8因长度不匹配触发416或EOF错误。我们采用了1MB填充技术以兼容AList的严格校验，且1MB足以容纳绝大多数M3U8文件而不影响性能。 ### Changes | 修改内容 **alist/drivers/139/types.go** - Added ShareCatalog and ShareContent structs for API response mapping | 添加分享目录与内容的API响应映射结构体 **alist/drivers/139/meta.go** - Integrated 'share' storage type and simplified struct tags for UI cleanliness | 新增分享存储类型并精简结构体标签以确保界面整洁 **alist/drivers/139/driver.go** - Implemented share mode handling and forced 1MB file size for video listings | 实现分享模式处理逻辑并在列表时将视频大小强制声明为1MB **alist/drivers/139/util.go** - Implemented M3U8 absolute URL rewriter and a padded RangeReadCloser to ensure proxy compatibility | 实现M3U8绝对路径重写器及带填充功能的读取器以适配代理校验 - Cleaned up all debug logging and temporary code for production readiness | 清理了所有调试日志和临时代码以达到发布标准 ### Verified | 验证结果 Successfully mounted share links; shared videos play via HLS without 416 errors; padded content size matches the 1MB metadata. 成功挂载分享链接；视频可通过HLS正常播放且无416错误；填充后的内容大小与声明的1MB元数据完美匹配。

author: talamuyal
body:
## What

- New `debi util yaml-validate <file|->` validates YAML files (multi-document streams supported), powered by `goccy/go-yaml`
- New `debi util toml-validate <file|->` validates TOML files, powered by `BurntSushi/toml`
- Both mirror `json-validate`: same `line X, column Y: <detail>` error format, same exit-code convention (0 valid / 1 invalid / 2 usage or file-open error), same stdin sentinel `-`, same shell-completion wiring
- Empty/whitespace-only input is rejected by all three commands for cross-format parity
- `TestRun_Util_Help_PrintsUsage` hardened to assert every util subcommand appears in help text, preventing future drift

## Why

- Config files in YAML and TOML are now as common as JSON; users wanted a single validation entry point per format with consistent UX
- `goccy/go-yaml` was chosen over `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` because the latter was archived by its maintainer on 2025-04-01 and never reported column numbers in errors; goccy is actively maintained and exposes real line+column via typed errors
- `BurntSushi/toml` exposes `ParseError.Position{Line, Col}` directly, giving identical UX to JSON without a custom offset-walker

author: damienlove
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The local agent WebSocket servers (`local-agent/server.js` and `scripts/local-agent.js`) used the `ws` library without validating the `Origin` header. This allowed any malicious website a user visits to connect to `ws://localhost:4477`.
🎯 Impact: Since the servers spawn raw local shells based on WebSocket messages, an attacker could achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the developer's machine via Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH).
🔧 Fix: Implemented `verifyClient` callbacks in both WebSocketServer instantiations. The logic validates `info.origin` against an explicit allowlist, permits `undefined` origins for non-browser local scripts, and securely allows dynamic local frontend ports by checking `startsWith('http://localhost:')`.
✅ Verification: Created `test-cswsh.cjs` to simulate an unauthorized connection and `test-cswsh-allowed.cjs` to simulate an authorized one. Verified that unauthorized connections are correctly blocked with a 403 Forbidden error, while authorized connections succeed. Ran `pnpm build` to ensure no regressions.

body:
First real consumer of `core.scheduler.Scheduler`. When a user joins
the realm (`realm_user.add`), schedule a welcome DM after a configurable
delay.

## Properties

- **Durable** — schema v3 adds `pending_welcomes(user_id PK, deliver_at)`.
  Survives bot restarts.
- **Idempotent** — duplicate add events (e.g. after a queue reconnect)
  preserve the *original* deadline via `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.
- **At-most-once** — claim+delete in a single transaction; a crash mid-DM
  drops the welcome rather than spamming.
- **Bots filtered** in the dispatcher: never welcomes itself or other bots.
- **Drain on disable** — flipping `enabled: false` at runtime makes the
  next tick drop pending rows rather than queueing them forever (see
  README "Watch points").

- `core/dispatcher.py` — adds `register_realm_user_add_handler`; routes
  `type=realm_user, op=add` to handlers. Message routing untouched.
- `bot_main.py` — adds `realm_user` to `event_types`; wires welcome.
- `config.py` — new `welcome` section (off by default; safe default
  message).
- `features/welcome/` — feature + README.
- `storage/db.py` — schema v3 + `schedule_welcome` / `claim_due_welcomes`
  / `cancel_welcome` / `pending_welcome_count`.

Two placeholders: `{user_id}`, `{mention}`. Unknown keys / stray `{`

✅ **Result:** The two console errors visible on the public site were addressed: the missing `/api/data` endpoint (the project was originally a custom Node `server.js` app that does not run on Netlify) and the missing `/favicon.ico`.

A Netlify Function was added at `netlify/functions/data.mjs` that responds at `/api/data`. On `GET` it returns the persisted site content from a Netlify Blobs store (`site-content` namespace, key `site`), falling back to the bundled defaults from `package.json` when nothing has been saved yet. On `POST` it persists the submitted JSON back to the same blob, so future edits survive across deploys without an external database. The frontend `app.jsx` and `Menu.html` already call `/api/data`, so they now load successfully.

A small SVG favicon was added at `favicon.svg`, themed to the bakery (warm cream "T" on a dark roast background), and `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />` was wired into `index.html`, `Menu.html`, and `admin.html`. Browsers will use the SVG and stop requesting the missing `/favicon.ico`.

The remaining console message about the in-browser Babel transformer is a development-mode warning from `@babel/standalone`, not a runtime error; it is informational only and intentionally left in place since the JSX is currently transformed in the browser.

body:
## Summary

- Sets `maximumPoolSize=5`, `minimumIdle=0`, `idleTimeout=30000ms`, `maxLifetime=60000ms` in `backend/src/main/resources/application.conf`
- Adds a detailed comment block documenting the Cloud Run / Cloud SQL connection-exhaustion rationale
- Removes the ambiguous `maxConnections` alias in favour of the explicit `maximumPoolSize` key

Linear: https://linear.app/helioapp/issue/HEL-96/tune-hikaricp-for-serverless-environment

## Behavioral changes

No API or schema changes. This is a backend configuration change only. Pool behaviour at runtime:

- Each Cloud Run instance holds at most 5 database connections (down from 10)
- Idle connections are released after 30 s instead of held indefinitely
- Connections are recycled after 60 s, staying within Cloud SQL's idle-connection timeout and preventing unexpected `connection reset` errors
- `minimumIdle=0` means idle instances hold zero connections, freeing capacity for other instances

## Test plan

- [x] `sbt test` — all Scala backend tests pass
- [x] `npm test` (root + frontend) — 269 frontend tests pass
- [x] ESLint and Prettier checks pass
- [ ] Manual: start backend locally, confirm Flyway migrations still run and API endpoints respond as expected

## Risks / follow-up

- Pool of 5 is sufficient for local development and for Cloud Run under normal load; if burst traffic causes request queuing at the HikariCP level, `maximumPoolSize` can be tuned upward
- `maxLifetime=60000ms` is intentionally short; confirm Cloud SQL's `wait_timeout` / `tcp_keepalives_idle` are set consistently in the Cloud SQL instance

body:
## Resume

Q.25 etablit un protocole de **suivi mensuel** de la citabilite de
Nuffle Arena dans les principaux moteurs generatifs (ChatGPT, Claude,
Perplexity, Gemini). La phase de suivi reste **manuelle** (un compte
gratuit par moteur, navigation privee), mais les **prompts de
reference** sont versionnes pour garantir une couverture auditable et
un suivi historique fiable.

### Catalogue versionne

- `apps/web/app/lib/ai-presence-prompts.ts` :
  - **8 prompts de reference** repartis sur 3 categories :
    - `team` (3 prompts) : audit connaissance des rosters BB3 +
      reconnaissance des "5 equipes prioritaires"
    - `skill` (2 prompts) : audit connaissance des competences +
      source 130+ skills
    - `app` (3 prompts) : reconnaissance d'entite, export PDF,
      multijoueur en ligne
  - chaque prompt expose un `id` stable, le texte FR a soumettre tel
    quel, la `category`, et la liste des `expectedMentions` (mots-cles
    attendus dans la reponse)
  - `AI_PRESENCE_TARGET_ENGINES` : 4 moteurs cibles
  - `expectedKeywordsForCategory(category)` : helper pur retournant
    les keywords par defaut d une categorie

### Tests TDD — 11 cas

- Structure : `id`, `prompt`, `category`, `expectedMentions` non vides
- Ids uniques (no doublons)
- Couverture des 3 categories
- Presence de `Nuffle Arena` ou `Blood Bowl` dans chaque
  `expectedMentions` (anti-derive du catalogue)
- Determinisme

### Documentation

- `docs/seo/ai-presence-protocol.md` :
  - cadence : mensuelle + adhoc apres chaque release majeure
  - procedure pas-a-pas (compte par moteur, navigation privee, ne pas
    reformuler les prompts)
  - modele de tableau de suivi a poster en issue GitHub
    `[AI presence] YYYY-MM`
  - lien avec `llms.txt` : les prompts servent aussi de **test de
    regression** sur le contenu cible des LLM
  - regles d'iteration : ajouter / deprecier sans casser le suivi
    historique

### Pourquoi versionner les prompts ?

- Trace immutable / git-blameable des questions testees.
- Couverture auditable des categories et mots-cles.
- Prepare une eventuelle automatisation via API LLM si on decide de
  rendre le suivi continu (out of scope ici).

## Tache roadmap

Sprint 23, tache **Q.25 — Protocole de test "presence IA" : prompts de
reference dans ChatGPT / Claude / Perplexity, suivi mensuel**

      `ai-presence-prompts.test.ts`)

author: dapage
body:
## Summary

Acts on the [security & architecture review](../blob/refactor/security-review-remediation/README.md) findings, organized into four cleanly-separated commits so any one can be reverted independently.

### Commit 1 — Dotfile content cleanup (H1–H6)
- `.functions`: fix the broken `#!/bin/env` shebang; port `server()` from Python 2's removed `SimpleHTTPServer` to `python3 -m http.server`; detect the active network interface in `phpserver()` instead of hardcoding `en1`; drop `pygmentize` from `json()` and remove the `s()` Sublime helper (`subl` not installed).
- `.exports`: drop `DEVELOPER_DIR` (Apple-reserved env var consumed by xcrun/xcodebuild — clobbering it broke Xcode tooling) and `DEVELOPER_DIRECTORY` (redundant). Drop the workspace-dir PATH prepending — those are project trees, not bin dirs, and prepending them lets any random checked-in file shadow system commands.
- `.bash_profile`: standardize on `DOTFILES_DIR` to match `.profile` and `bootstrap.sh` (was `DOTFILES_HOME`).
- `.aliases`: replace `colorls` aliases (gem not in Brewfile, failing on every invocation) with built-in `ls` flags. Move the multi-step `update` command to `bin/update` (the prior `;`-chained alias swallowed failures silently).
- `bin/update` (new): `set -euo pipefail` wrapper around softwareupdate / brew / mas / npm / gem updates; gates each step on tool availability.

### Commit 2 — Bootstrap robustness (M5–M8, L6)
- `clone_repo`: verify `.git/` is a real repo via `git rev-parse` before skipping. A botched previous bootstrap could leave an empty `.git/` that the bare directory check silently accepted.
- `keep_sudo_alive`: trap fires on EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP, not just EXIT. A Ctrl-C no longer leaks the keepalive subshell.
- `run_brew_bundle`: tee output to a timestamped log file under `$BOOTSTRAP_LOG_DIR` and surface the path in failure warnings.
- `ansible/tasks/xcode_clt.yml`: deleted. CLT install is bootstrap's job (must run before `git clone`); the playbook task duplicated detection with a different code path.
- New bats coverage for `clone_repo` (3), `install_ansible` (2), `run_playbook` --ask-become-pass handling (2), the brew-bundle log file, and the trap signal list — closes the L6 coverage gap.

### Commit 3 — Supply-chain pinning (M1, M2, M3)
- `oh_my_zsh.yml`: replace `curl|sh` of the upstream installer with `ansible.builtin.git` cloning at a pinned commit SHA (functionally equivalent under `--unattended --keep-zshrc`).
- `zsh_plugins.yml`: add `version:` SHA per plugin. Plugins load into every shell, so a compromise persists across sessions.
- `requirements.yml`: cap `community.general` upper bound at `<13.0.0` so a major-version bump can't silently land in CI.

### Commit 4 — Hygiene (M9, M10, M11, M4, L1-L3)
- Delete deprecated `install.sh`; trim its README mention.
- Rewrite `update.sh`: prior `cp ~/.zshrc → repo` lines were no-ops (symlinks); now `set -euo pipefail`, quoted vars, fails clearly if brew missing, shows `git diff --stat` after regen.
- Add `permissions: contents: read` to all four GitHub workflows.
- `dotfiles.yml`: stamp each run's backups under a timestamped subdirectory of `~/.dotfiles-backup/`, only when there's something to back up.
- `.profile`: quote `$DOTFILES_DIR` in the source-files glob; switch to POSIX `.`.
- `.greeting`: replace `which` with `command -v`; fix the broken shebang.
- `.init`: guard ssh-agent spawn with `ssh-add -l` so each shell doesn't fork a fresh agent.

## Test plan
- [x] `bats tests/` — 37/37 green; each new test verified to fail against the unfixed code first per the repo's TDD policy
- [x] `ansible-playbook ansible/tests/unit/{test_syntax,test_dotfiles_list,test_brewfile}.yml` all pass
- [x] `shellcheck bootstrap.sh ansible/tests/integration/run.sh bin/update update.sh` clean
- [x] `ansible-playbook ansible/playbook.yml --syntax-check` clean
- [ ] CI green on this PR (lint, unit, bootstrap-macos)

## Summary
- New `final AnimationTime` class in `com.codename1.ui.animations` with a static `now()` / `setTime(long)` / `reset()` / `isOverridden()` API. Defaults to `System.currentTimeMillis()`; when overridden, `now()` returns the explicit value until `reset()`. Primitive-only state (one `long`, one `boolean`) to keep the hot path cheap.
- Routes all animation-related clock reads through it: `Motion` (start/finish/getCurrentMotionTime/createDecelerationMotionFrom), `Timeline` (setTime/animate), `Container.MorphAnimation`, `Image.animate()`, and `Label` text ticker.
- Lets users drive animations deterministically (UI tests), slow them down, fast-forward, or step frame-by-frame — without relying on the `Motion.slowMotion` hack as the only lever.

Non-animation `System.currentTimeMillis()` call sites (Display transition lock-wait, gesture/tap detection in Switch/MapComponent/Spinner, UITimer, etc.) are intentionally left alone.

🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: OAuth callback routes did not validate the \`state\` query parameter against the stored \`OAUTH_COOKIE\` (\`oauth_state\`), making the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). An attacker could link their own social account to a victim's session.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could hijack user sessions by having the user visit a malicious site that completes the OAuth flow with the attacker's authorization code.
🔧 Fix: Extracted the stored state from the session/cookie in the OAuth callbacks and enforced a strict equality check (\`state === storedState\`) against the returned \`state\` query parameter.

## Summary

Bug-fix release rolling up two things on top of v0.1.8:

- **Env-file zip regression in cloud submissions.** v0.1.8 narrowed the cloud zip to ship only `.finalrun/env/<envName>.yaml` for the active environment (instead of leaking every env file). The narrowing only worked when `--env` was passed on the CLI — workspaces that rely on `config.yaml`'s `env:` default (the documented pattern) had the env file dropped entirely, and the server-side `runCheck` would 500 with `Environment "<name>" was requested, but .finalrun/env does not exist`. author: mrnullpointer
body:
## Summary

Three threads landed together:

1. **Deeper ISA concept page** — five new sections covering ISA design from physics first principles up through modern accelerator ISAs, each with its own custom animated visualizer.
2. **Background motion control** — optional navbar toggle that cycles full → calm → off, persisted, with OS prefers-reduced-motion as the first-visit default.
3. **Lazy loading** — route-level + per-visualizer chunk splits, viewport-triggered mount, hover prefetch on concept links.

## ISA page expansion

`/c/what-is-an-isa` gains five new sections, in order:

- **Physics — From electrons to opcodes**: a five-rung stacked ladder (electrons → transistor → NAND → register → opcode) with a clock pulse that auto-advances. Hover a layer to freeze and see the physics blurb.
- **Operands — How many operands does an instruction have?**: same expression `(a+b)×c` compiled four ways (stack / accumulator / x86 register-memory / RISC load-store). Step button advances all four in lockstep with live state visualization.
- **Taxonomy — The family tree**: four-axis classifier (complexity / storage / data shape / memory ordering). Click chips to filter; twelve real ISAs (x86-64, AArch64, RISC-V, Itanium, TI C6000, 6502, JVM, subleq, Forth, NVIDIA SASS, AMX/SME, Cell SPE) animate in/out at the matching intersection.
- **Ordering — What can other cores see?**: classic Dekker test under SC / TSO / weak. Two cores, animated store buffers, observable outcomes panel that flips (0,0) from forbidden to allowed as you switch models.
- **Evolution — Six decades of contract revision**: scrubbable 1960→2030 timeline with era bands and 15 markers from System/360 to AMX/SME.

`ConceptPage` now renders these sections only when present in a concept's `content`, so Pipeline and Cache pages are unchanged.

## Background motion toggle

New navbar button (between search and theme) cycles the canvas through three tiers:

- **full** — current behaviour, no caps
- **calm** — density cut to ~55%, drops to the existing 'minimal' tier inside `CircuitFlow` (slower spawn, fewer in-flight transactions)
- **off** — paints one frame and exits the requestAnimationFrame loop entirely

Persisted in `localStorage` (`axiom-motion`). First visit defaults from OS-level `prefers-reduced-motion`. Reversible at any time. Verified frozen on 'off' (canvas pixel sums identical 2 sec apart) and resumes on 'full'.

## Lazy loading

- `ConceptPage` and `DomainPage` are `React.lazy` route chunks (Atlas/Index stay eager — they are the most likely first paint).
- Every visualizer is its own `lazy()` chunk in `src/concepts/index.js`.
- New `LazyViz` wrapper uses IntersectionObserver (400 px rootMargin) to mount visualizers only when scrolled near. Skeletons reserve a per-viz `minHeight` so the page does not jump.
- The hero visualizer is `eager` (mounts immediately under Suspense) so the page lands fast.
- Concept links prefetch the ConceptPage chunk on `onMouseEnter` / `onFocus` via `src/app/prefetch.js`.

### Bundle impact

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Main JS (gzipped) | 142 KB | 126 KB |
| ConceptPage chunk | — | 4 KB |
| Each ISA viz chunk | — | 1–3 KB |
| Homepage initial load | full app | atlas + meta only |

## Files

- `src/concepts/isa/viz/` — 6 visualizer files (Encoding moved from `visualizer.jsx`, plus 5 new)
- `src/concepts/isa/content.js` — five new section blocks added
- `src/pages/ConceptPage.jsx` — dynamic TOC, optional sections, `LazyViz` integration
- `src/app/motion.jsx`, `src/components/shell/MotionToggle.jsx` — motion preference
- `src/components/LazyViz.jsx` — viewport-mount + Suspense + skeleton wrapper
- `src/app/prefetch.js` — hover prefetch helpers

All animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Build is clean. No console errors.

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit `/c/what-is-an-isa`, scroll through all sections, confirm each visualizer animates and respects user interactions (hover, click, step buttons).
- [ ] Click the new motion toggle in the navbar; confirm the icon cycles Activity → Waves → PowerOff and the background freezes on 'off' / resumes on 'full'.
- [ ] Reload after picking a tier; confirm the choice persists.
- [ ] Open DevTools Network tab on `/index`; hover a concept card and confirm the ConceptPage chunk fetches before click.
- [ ] On `/c/what-is-an-isa`, scroll slowly and watch each visualizer chunk fetch as it enters the viewport.
- [ ] Confirm Pipeline (`/c/cpu-pipeline`) and Cache (`/c/cache-hierarchy`) pages still render correctly (they do not use the new optional sections).

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/nextcrm-netlify-deployment/agent-runs/69eb77086f864ffb285be5ab

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** In this project as i stands, has the Netlify DB been setup? I think i need to create an ENV for it right?

✅ **Result:** # Wired the app to Netlify DB (Neon) for production

## What changed

The application was taught to read the connection strings that the Netlify Neon extension auto-injects into the deploy environment, so no manual database URL needs to be kept in sync in site env vars.

Three files were updated:

- `prisma.config.ts` — the Prisma datasource URL now falls back to `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` (direct connection, used for migrations) and then to `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL` if `DATABASE_URL` is not explicitly set.
- `lib/prisma.ts` — the runtime Prisma client (backed by the `@prisma/adapter-pg` pool) now falls back to `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL` (the pooled connection, appropriate for serverless runtime) and finally to `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED`.
- `package.json` — the `build` script's guard around `prisma migrate deploy` was broadened so migrations run when any of `DATABASE_URL`, `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED`, or `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL` is set, not only when `DATABASE_URL` is present.

Existing `DATABASE_URL` support was preserved as the first-priority variable, so local development using `.env.local` continues to work unchanged.

## Why

The project uses Prisma against PostgreSQL, and prior to this change every code path read `process.env.DATABASE_URL` directly. Netlify's Neon extension provisions a database and injects `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL` and `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` into builds and functions — but it does not create a variable named `DATABASE_URL`. Without the fallback, production builds would skip `prisma migrate deploy` and production requests would fail to connect. Routing migrations to the unpooled URL and runtime queries to the pooled URL follows Neon's recommended pattern for serverless workloads.

## What the user needs to do

1. **Confirm the Neon extension is enabled and a database is claimed for the site.** In the Netlify UI, under *Extensions → Neon*, the site `nextcrm-netlify-deployment` should show a claimed Neon project. If not yet claimed, click *Claim database* (or run `netlify db init` locally against this linked site). Once claimed, `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL` and `NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` are automatically exposed to builds and functions — they do not need to be copied into site env vars.
2. **Trigger a production deploy** (merge this branch to `main`, or click *Trigger deploy*). The first deploy will run `prisma migrate deploy` against the Neon database, creating all tables, indexes, and the pgvector setup used by the CRM, email, and campaign modules.
3. **Seed initial reference data (optional but recommended for a fresh install).** The repo ships reference data for CRM opportunity types, sales stages, industries, contact types, lead sources/statuses/types, currencies, and sample invoices. Because this is a one-time bootstrap, the simplest path is to run the seed locally against the Neon URL:
   - Pull the unpooled Neon URL from Netlify: `netlify env:get NETLIFY_DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED`.
   - Put it in a local `.env.local` as `DATABASE_URL=...` (the seed script reads `.env.local`).
   - Run `pnpm exec tsx prisma/seeds/seed.ts`.
4. **Create the first admin user** through the app's sign-up flow after the site is live, since Better Auth manages users and no seed user is created.
5. **Verify connectivity** by loading the deployed site and signing in; if a CRM screen renders without the earlier "server error after CRM login" behavior, the database is reachable.

No secrets were printed or stored in the repository, and no manual `DATABASE_URL` needs to be set in Netlify for production — the extension-injected variables are sufficient.

author: neo-wanderer
body:
## Summary

- Closes #3217
- Heartbeat monitor already publishes `SystemEvent::HealthCheckFailed`, but operators on `notification.alert_channels` never see unresponsive-agent alerts — only `tool_failure` and `task_failed` are routed there. This patch makes heartbeat symmetric.
- Two small changes in `kernel/mod.rs`:
  1. In `start_heartbeat_monitor`, on the unresponsive-transition gate that already de-dupes the WARN log and the event-bus publish, additionally call `push_notification(agent_id, "health_check_failed", msg)`.
  2. Extend the global-fallback match arm in `push_notification` to include `"health_check_failed"` alongside `task_completed` / `task_failed` / `tool_failure`, so a deployment with only a bare `[notification.alert_channels]` block (no `agent_rules`) still receives heartbeat alerts.

## Routing example

Operators who want a dedicated topic/channel for heartbeats can now use:

```toml
[[notification.agent_rules]]
agent_pattern = "*"
events = ["health_check_failed"]
[[notification.agent_rules.channels]]
channel_type = "telegram"
recipient = "-1001234567890"
thread_id = "7"
```

Or they can rely on the global fallback by leaving `agent_rules` empty and configuring a single `[notification.alert_channels]` block.

## Design notes

- Recovery is intentionally silent — no "agent recovered" notification — to avoid the noise that an N-agent deployment would generate during normal restart churn. The existing INFO log line `"Agent recovered from unresponsive state"` is sufficient for log-based observability.
- The push happens inside the same `known_unresponsive.insert()` gate that protects the WARN log and the event-bus publish, so we get one notification per transition (not one per heartbeat tick while the agent stays down).
- Quiet-hours filtering (`is_quiet_hours`) still applies because the new push is downstream of that early-`continue`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p librefang-kernel --lib`
- [x] `cargo test -p librefang-kernel --lib heartbeat` — 10 passed (existing tests unchanged).
- [x] `cargo clippy -p librefang-kernel --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [ ] Live test: configure `[notification.alert_channels]` to point at a Telegram topic, force an autonomous agent into an unresponsive state, confirm a single message arrives in the topic and a single message arrives on recovery (well — none, by design).

## Follow-up worth tracking separately

`AutonomousConfig.heartbeat_channel: Option<String>` is declared but unused. With this PR, per-agent routing is available via `notification.agent_rules` instead. The vestigial field could be either wired up or removed; not in scope for this PR. Tracked in #3217.

author: rafacm
body:
## Summary

- **Port preflight + saner default**: `docs:demo-record` now defaults to Postgres `5432` (the canonical port) and `lsof`-checks the port before invoking `docker run`, so a collision with another local Postgres prints an actionable message instead of a `docker run` networking error.
- **Refactor**: the `docker run` logic is extracted into three reusable helpers — `docs:postgres-start`, `docs:postgres-start-optimized`, `docs:postgres-stop`. The optimized variant carries the import-tuning flags from the docs/README.md "Server-side tuning" section. `docs:demo-record` now starts the import-tuned container by default.
- **Args, not env vars**: `docs:demo-record` takes optional `<port> <container>` positional args (defaults `5432` / `musicbrainz-database-setup-demo`); `docs:demo-render` takes optional `<speed> <fps-cap> <theme>` (defaults `10` / `60` / `monokai`). All declared via mise's `usage` syntax — bound as `$usage_<name>` since mise does not pass positional args via `$1`/`$2` to inline `run = "…"` scripts.
- **Volume cleanup**: every `docker rm` is now `docker rm -fv` so the postgres image's anonymous data volume is reclaimed on each teardown — no more dangling volumes accumulating across re-recordings.
- **Cleaner GIF**: oh-my-posh / Powerline prompt is now reliably suppressed in the recorded shell. Earlier attempts cleared `precmd_functions` after sourcing `~/.zshrc`, but transient-prompt hooks installed via zle widgets survived that. The recording shell is now launched against a minimal temporary `ZDOTDIR` that does not source the user's config; `PATH` (and `uv`) is inherited from the parent mise process, which is all the demo needs.
- **Re-recorded assets**: regenerated `.cast` and `.gif` against the refactored task.

## Test plan

- [x] `mise run docs:demo-record` starts a tuned Postgres on `localhost:5432` and records a clean prompt.
- [x] `mise run docs:demo-record 5433` honours the port override.
- [x] `mise run docs:demo-record 5435 my-demo-container` honours both args.
- [x] If port is already bound, the `lsof` preflight fires with an actionable error before `docker run`.
- [x] `mise run docs:demo-render` renders the GIF; passing `8 30 dracula` retunes playback.
- [x] `mise run docs:postgres-stop musicbrainz-database-setup-demo` removes container + anonymous volume.
- [x] `mise run docs:postgres-start <port> <container>` and `docs:postgres-start-optimized <port> <container>` work standalone.

author: copilot
body:
Implements the WhatsApp-based multi-tenant food ordering layer on top of the existing AWS/AppSync stack: customers order via WhatsApp → order lands in DynamoDB → vendor dashboard updates in real-time → vendor receives a WhatsApp alert.

## Infrastructure (Schema + DynamoDB)
- `whatsappNumber` added to `Vendor`, `VendorApplication`, and their input types
- `GSI3-VendorByWhatsApp` on `KasiMainTable` keyed on `GSI3PK = whatsappNumber` — O(1) vendor lookup from webhook `To` number
- `Session` entity (`PK: SESSION#<phone>`, `SK: VENDOR#<vendorId>`) with DynamoDB TTL (`expiresAt`, 30 min)
- New mutations: `markOrderPaid`, `approveVendor`; new query: `getVendorByWhatsApp`

## Lambda Functions
- **`whatsappWebhook`** — Twilio signature validation → GSI3 vendor lookup → session state machine → order creation → notification dispatch
  - States: `START → SELECTING_ITEMS → CONFIRM_ORDER → PAYMENT → DONE`
  - Delivery fee and platform commission calculated consistently with `createOrder` Lambda
  - Fire-and-forget notification via `InvokeCommand(InvocationType: 'Event')`
- **`sendWhatsAppNotification`** — fetches vendor's `whatsappNumber`, sends formatted Twilio REST message; no-ops gracefully if unconfigured
- **`approveVendor`** — transactional: creates `VENDOR#` record (with `GSI3PK`) + marks application `APPROVED` with optimistic concurrency condition
- **`createOrder`** — wired async notification invoke post-write

## AppSync Resolvers
- `Query.getVendorByWhatsApp` — GSI3 index query
- `Mutation.markOrderPaid` — `UpdateItem` setting `paymentStatus = PAID` with `attribute_exists` guard
- `Mutation.approveVendor` — Lambda data source stub
- `Query.getVendor` — `whatsappNumber` added to response projection

## Frontend
- **`VendorDashboard`**: AppSync subscription (`subscribeToNewOrders`) with 10 s polling fallback; new-order alert banner; "Mark Paid" button for cash/EFT orders; WhatsApp source badge; third tab — **Manual Order Form** for walk-in/phone orders
- **`VendorSettings`** (`/vendor/settings`): business info + WhatsApp number (international format validated) + delivery fee config → calls `updateVendorProfile`
- **`api.ts`**: `subscribeToNewOrders` / `subscribeToOrderStatus` helpers wrapping Amplify v6 observable; `markOrderPaid`; `updateVendorProfile`
- **`types/index.ts`**: `OrderSource = 'WEB' | 'WHATSAPP' | 'MANUAL'`; `whatsappNumber` on Vendor/VendorApplication; `paymentStatus` / `source` on Order

author: moranweissman
body:
## Summary

Land the `SHARKO_CATALOG_TRUSTED_IDENTITIES` env-var parser so V123-2.2's
verifier finally has a real trust policy to evaluate against. Replace the
placeholder `sources.TrustPolicy{}` literal in `cmd/sharko/serve.go` with a
fail-fast startup parse. Add operator docs + mkdocs nav entry.

Closes the third story in Epic V123-2 (per-entry cosign signing). Epic
progress after this PR merges: 3/6.

## Acceptance criteria coverage

**Given** `SHARKO_CATALOG_TRUSTED_IDENTITIES` is unset
**When** the verifier runs
**Then** the defaults are active (CNCF org workflows + Sharko's own release).
→ Covered by `TestLoadTrustPolicy_UnsetUsesDefaults`.

**Given** the env var is `<defaults>,<custom>`
**When** parsed
**Then** `<defaults>` expands inline; all three regexes are active in
declaration order.
→ Covered by `TestLoadTrustPolicy_DefaultsTokenPlusCustom` +
`TestLoadTrustPolicy_CustomPlusDefaults`.

**Given** the env var is set without `<defaults>`
**When** parsed
**Then** ONLY the custom regex is active; defaults are NOT silently
included. Operators must opt in via `<defaults>`.
→ Covered by `TestLoadTrustPolicy_OnlyCustomNoDefaults`.

**Given** any pattern fails to compile as a Go regexp
**When** parsed at startup
**Then** Sharko fails fast with a clear error naming the offending pattern.
→ Covered by `TestLoadTrustPolicy_InvalidRegexErrors`. Wired in serve.go
returns from the serve closure → main exits non-zero.

**Given** an entry signed by an identity that doesn't match any active regex
**When** the verifier runs
**Then** `verified: false`.
→ Already enforced by V123-2.2's fail-closed semantics (signing/verify.go
`verifyEntity` step 8). No code change needed in this PR.

**Given** the env var is empty (`SHARKO_CATALOG_TRUSTED_IDENTITIES=`)
**When** parsed
**Then** treat as unset → use defaults. Trust-nothing is the explicit
`^$` escape hatch.
→ Covered by `TestLoadTrustPolicy_EmptyUsesDefaults`. Documented in the
operator guide's examples table + troubleshooting section.

## Defaults rationale

| Pattern | Why default |
|---------|-------------|
| `^https://github\.com/cncf/.*/\.github/workflows/.*$` | Sharko's positioning targets CNCF-curated addons; trusting any signed CNCF workflow out of the box matches the project's curation stance. |
| `^https://github\.com/MoranWeissman/sharko/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v.*$` | V123-2.5 will sign the embedded catalog from the Sharko release pipeline; without this default, fresh installs would see embedded entries as Unverified once that signing lands. |

## `<defaults>` magic-token semantics

Case-sensitive literal token. Expands inline at every occurrence,
preserving declaration order so verify.go's first-match-wins iteration
stays deterministic. Full table in
`docs/site/operator/catalog-trust-policy.md`:

| Env var value | Active regexes |
|---------------|----------------|
| *(unset)* / *(empty)* | both defaults |
| `<defaults>` | both defaults |
| `<defaults>,<custom>` | defaults + custom |
| `<custom>,<defaults>` | custom + defaults |
| `<custom>` | custom only |
| `^$` | trust-nothing escape hatch |

## Tests

- `internal/catalog/signing/trust_test.go` — 8 new tests (all 8 cases
  from the brief, table-driven by env-var value).
- Existing 13 `verify_test.go` tests still green.
- Total signing package: 21/21 PASS in ~5s with `-race -count=1`.
- Catalog tree (`internal/catalog/...`): clean across catalog + signing
  + sources, no regressions.

## Quality gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...` | clean |
| `go vet ./...` | clean |
| `go test ./internal/catalog/signing/... -race -count=1` | 21/21 PASS |
| `go test ./internal/catalog/... -race -count=1` | PASS (catalog + signing + sources) |
| `golangci-lint` | not installed locally; CI runs it |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | not installed locally; CI runs it (single new page + one nav line) |
| Swagger regen | not applicable (no API surface change) |

## Files touched

- `internal/catalog/signing/trust.go` (new)
- `internal/catalog/signing/trust_test.go` (new)
- `cmd/sharko/serve.go` (wire-in + comment block reflowed)
- `docs/site/operator/catalog-trust-policy.md` (new)
- `mkdocs.yml` (one nav line added)
- `.bmad/output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` (status flip)
- `.bmad/output/implementation-artifacts/V123-2-3-…md` (frontmatter + retro)

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: build + vet + test pass on amd64 + arm64.
- [ ] CI: golangci-lint clean on `internal/catalog/signing/...`.
- [ ] CI: mkdocs --strict accepts the new page + nav entry.
- [ ] Manual: deploy with `SHARKO_CATALOG_TRUSTED_IDENTITIES=<defaults>` and
      confirm `catalog trust policy loaded identity_count=2` startup log.
- [ ] Manual: deploy with malformed regex (e.g. `[unbalanced`) and confirm
      Sharko refuses to start with a clear error message.

## Do not tag

Per the user's release-cadence rule and the brief's explicit note: this PR
ships to main without a version bump. v1.23.0 cuts only when Epic V123-2 +
V123-3 + V123-4 are all done and the user explicitly asks.

## Do not merge

Tech lead merges.

### Motivation

- Introduce a first-class e-commerce flow so users can purchase products, sellers can ship items, and payouts can be settled on-chain. 
- Provide signed QR payloads for product payment links and extend the wallet prototype to support product payments and diagnostics.
- Add admin and seller controls for refund handling and manual settlement workflows.

### Description

- Add new models and migrations for product ordering: `ProductOrder`, `ProductShipment`, `UserShippingAddress`, `SellerPayout`, `SellerPayoutAddress`, and `ProductRefundRequest`, and update `ChainReceipt`/`WalletAddress` choices and legacy currency constants; add `constants.py` with token/blockchain metadata.
- Implement services: `ProductOrderService`, `ProductPaymentDetectionService`, and `ProductPayoutService` (QR payload building/signing, stock reservation/release, payment sync, payout settlement), plus helper `get_product_wallet_send_amount` and QR signature/verification helpers.
- Extend wallet/LBRY daemon client behavior and wallet prototype pay flow with stronger typing/logging, `account_balance`, unlock result handling, diagnostics, and support for `pay_payment_order` with optional `amount_override`.
- Add REST API endpoints and serializers for product order CRUD/listing, shipping address CRUD, seller payout address CRUD, refund requests, seller/admin workflows, and wallet endpoints for submitting product payments; wire routes in URLs and top-level `config/urls.py`.

body:
Closes #110

## 概要

`docs/09-security-individual.md` を追補後の `WRITING_GUIDE.md` に沿って節単位で書き直しました。
語句単位の find-and-replace ではなく、節を読み直して節として書き直す方針で進めています。

## 主な変更

- **章リード** — 「あなたも一度は見かけたことがあるはずです」式の呼びかけと、「3つの箱に分けて手渡す」の容器比喩を外し、入力・出力・履歴の3区分という構造の宣言に置き換え。
- **節タイトル＝結論型** — 「まず、セキュリティの論点を3つの箱に分ける」「『消したつもり』が怖い」などを、「セキュリティの論点は入力・出力・履歴の3つに分かれる」「履歴とメモリは独立した領域として消す」のような結論型に。
- **太字の整理** — 文中強調の太字（「**普段の業務でツールを手に取るとき…**」「**渡す情報を削ることは…働きます**」「**モデルは忘れていても、サービスは覚えている**」など）をすべて段落分け・対比箇条書き・節タイトルへ移譲。残した太字は3つの軸の初出のみ。
- **装飾比喩の除去** — 「冷蔵庫から食材」「部屋の片付けに似ています」「AIに書き手や責任者の席はない」「同僚の武装解除」を削除し、跡地を事実記述で再構成。
- **「事故」の包括語の解消** — 「気づきにくい論点」「見落とされやすい型」「漏えいや誤公開」など、具体名に置換。
- **作用点不明の動詞** — 「**渡す情報を削ることは…回答品質の面でも働きます**」の「働きます」を「応答の品質にも作用します。余分な情報が混ざるほどモデルが依頼の主旨を取りにくくなる」と作用先まで書き下す形に。
- **まとめ** — 5項目→4項目へ圧縮（ガイドの「4点以内」を遵守）。次章への参照は1文の付記として分離。

## ガイドへの追補要否

今回の作業で出た論点（容器・受け渡し系の比喩、「事故」の包括語、節タイトルの装飾語、文中強調の太字、カジュアル表現など）は、いずれも既存の以下のセクションで十分カバーされる範囲でした。

- #4 システム運用者寄りの語彙
- #5 過剰な比喩・擬人化
- #6 身体性の比喩の連鎖
- 太字の運用（文中強調を避ける）
- 節タイトル＝結論

このため、今回 `WRITING_GUIDE.md` への追補は行いません。

## 効率改善のメモ

書き直し中に textlint の `no-doubled-joshi`（助詞二重）が事後発見になり、追加修正のラウンドが3回ほど発生しました。ただし、textlint で自動検出できる項目を人手のチェックリスト化してもガイドの肥大化につながるため、ガイドへの追補は見送ります（節を書き終えた都度 `npm run lint` を流す現行運用のままで対応可能と判断）。

## 確認方法

- `npm run lint` がクリーンであること
- 章全体を通読し、節タイトル＝結論／太字1節0〜2箇所／まとめ4点以内が守られていること
- 入力・出力・履歴とメモリの3軸が、章を通して同じ語彙でつながっていること
- 段落・節の流れが書き直し前と同等以上に保たれていること

## Summary

Follow-up to #487. Replace the "drop down to raw `osascript -e \"tell application …\"`" fallback in SKILL.md with a first-class `--app <path>` option on the wrapper, so every Moolah automation call goes through `moolah-tell` and benefits from the bundle-path echo, missing-build error, and duplicate-instance refusal.

```bash
moolah-tell --app /abs/path/to/Moolah.app 'get name of every profile'
```

The flag is parsed before the body, sets the bundle path verbatim (no git lookup, no CWD dependency), and then runs the same checks the CWD-resolved path already runs. Existing call sites (no flag) are unchanged.

SKILL.md restructured around "pick the bundle two ways" as the primary contract — CWD-resolved or `--app` — and folds the old "CRITICAL: run from inside the worktree" warning into a "CWD pitfall (no `--app`)" note since the duplicate-instance check now catches the trap regardless of how the bundle was picked. Removes the raw-osascript fallback section entirely.

- [x] CWD-resolved from a sibling checkout (no `--app`): still refuses (existing behaviour from #487).
