## Summary

Implements the full ImagetoPDF pipeline: extract text from images via Tesseract OCR, compile results into a PDF, and optionally email the PDF.

**New files:**
- `requirements.txt` — Python dependencies (`pytesseract`, `Pillow`, `fpdf2`)
- `config.py` — SMTP configuration via environment variables (`SENDER_EMAIL`, `SENDER_PASSWORD`, `RECIPIENT_EMAIL`, `SMTP_SERVER`, `SMTP_PORT`)
- `ocr_extractor.py` — Wraps `pytesseract.image_to_string()` with graceful error handling per image
- `pdf_generator.py` — Generates a multi-page PDF using `fpdf2`, one page per image with filename header and extracted text body. Handles non-Latin characters with `errors='replace'`
- `email_sender.py` — Sends the generated PDF as an email attachment via SMTP/TLS
- `main.py` — CLI entry point using `argparse` with `--output`, `--email`, and `--no-email` flags

**Updated:**
- `README.md` — Full documentation with prerequisites, installation, configuration (env vars, Gmail App Passwords), usage examples, and project structure

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human
- [ ] Install Tesseract OCR on your system (`sudo apt install tesseract-ocr` / `brew install tesseract`) and run `pip install -r requirements.txt`
- [ ] Test basic OCR + PDF generation: `python main.py <some_image>.png --no-email` — verify `output.pdf` contains extracted text
- [ ] Test email sending (requires `SENDER_EMAIL`, `SENDER_PASSWORD` env vars): `python main.py <image>.png --email your@email.com`
- [ ] Verify graceful handling of unreadable/corrupt image files

### Notes
- `pytesseract` is a wrapper around the Tesseract binary — it must be installed separately on the host system.
- For Gmail SMTP, users need a 16-character App Password (not their regular password) if 2FA is enabled.
- The PDF uses the built-in `Helvetica` font with `latin-1` encoding fallback (`errors='replace'`) to handle unexpected OCR characters without crashing.

author: pengdingkang
body:
Closes #150

## Problem
Songs that have been downloaded (shown with a checkmark in the Songs list) still play via streaming instead of using the local cached file, even when the cached quality meets or exceeds the current stream quality setting.

## Fix
`DefaultPlaybackManager` now checks for cached songs before building stream URLs. If a cached file exists and its quality is at least as good as the current stream quality, the local file is used for playback.

### Changes

**`CachedSongRepository` / `DefaultCachedSongRepository`**
- `getPlayableCachedSong(serverId, songId, preferredQuality)` — single song lookup with quality + file existence check
- `getPlayableCachedSongs(serverId, preferredQuality)` — batch lookup returning `Map<songId, CachedSong>` for queue building
- `CachedSong.canPlayAt()` — checks `File(localPath).isFile` and `quality.isAtLeast(preferredQuality)`
- `StreamQuality.isAtLeast()` — ordinal comparison (ORIGINAL=0 is highest)

**`DefaultPlaybackManager`**
- Inject `CachedSongRepository`
- `Song.toPreferredMediaItem()` — prefers cached file, falls back to stream
- `PlaybackRequest.toPreferredMediaItemOrNull()` — for prefetch/quality upgrade of next track
- All playback entry points (`play`, `playNext`, `addToQueue`, `addSongToQueue`) now check cache first
- Prefetch logic also checks for cached versions
- Extract `PlaybackRequest.toLogicalMediaItem()` to eliminate duplicated MediaItem builder code

### Quality comparison logic
`StreamQuality` enum ordinal: ORIGINAL(0) > 320kbps(1) > ... > 96kbps(6). A cached song is playable if its ordinal ≤ the preferred quality's ordinal (i.e., same or better quality).

body:
## Summary
- Integrates the real Phase 7 image detector using `prithivMLmods/Deep-Fake-Detector-v2-Model` converted to signed dynamic-range TFLite.
- Adds `data-detection-ml` and `feature-detect-image`, then wires image inference into `ProvenancePipeline` after C2PA/SynthID.
- Recalibrates image uncertainty gating so the final golden-set eval produces useful verdicts instead of all-uncertain output.
- Fixes the physical-device GPU delegate path for Play Services LiteRT by using `InterpreterApi.Options.addDelegateFactory(GpuDelegateFactory())`.

## Final Eval
500-image golden-set eval on `veritas_play_avd` using emulator `CPU_XNNPACK`:

- Binary accuracy: `0.896`
- False-positive rate: `0.064`
- False-negative rate: `0.144`
- Uncertain rate: `0.190`
- p95 latency: `1075 ms`

Full report: `docs/phase_reports/phase_7.md`

## Physical GPU Smoke
Physical-device smoke test passed on Google Pixel 8, Android API 36:

```text
Phase7ImageDetectorTest: score=0.2700992, interval=ConfidenceInterval(low=0.13009919, high=0.4100992), fallback=GPU, subScores={vit_model=0.31776375, exif_ela=0.0}, reasons=[CODEC_CONSISTENT]
```

## D-042 Finding
The first Pixel 8 run exposed a real Play Services LiteRT integration bug. The device had `tflite_gpu_dynamite` installed, but the app still fell back to `CPU_XNNPACK`. Logcat showed Play Services rejecting an instantiated `GpuDelegate`:

```text
IllegalArgumentException: Instantiated delegates (other than NnApiDelegate) are not allowed when using TF Lite from Google Play Services. Please use InterpreterApi.Options.addDelegateFactory() with an appropriate DelegateFactory instead.
```

Fix: `DelegateChain` now uses `addDelegateFactory(GpuDelegateFactory())`, after which the Pixel 8 smoke test reported `fallback=GPU`.

## Known Deferred Item
APK size is `183.25 MB`, primarily due to the `87.8 MB` image model. This is documented in D-041 and deferred to Phase 13 signed model delivery infrastructure using Play Asset Delivery. Phase 13 must reduce the installed APK below `100 MB`.

author: singchia
body:
## Summary

First slice of **0.4 — Application**. Adds the eight app-layer packet body codecs that ride inside the conn-layer 14-byte header. Wire format byte-for-byte compatible with Go v1.3.0-rc.2.

| Type                      | Body layout                                                              |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `StreamPayload`           | `session_id(8) + raw bytes`                                              |
| `MessagePayload`          | `session_id(8) + MessageData JSON`                                       |
| `MessageAckPayload`       | `session_id(8) + MessageData JSON`                                       |
| `RequestPayload`          | type alias of `MessagePayload` (type byte `0x71`)                        |
| `ResponsePayload`         | type alias of `MessageAckPayload` (type byte `0x72`)                     |
| `RequestCancelPayload`    | `session_id(8) + cancel_type(2)`                                         |
| `RegisterPayload`         | `session_id(8) + method bytes`                                           |
| `RegisterAckPayload`      | `session_id(8) + RegisterData JSON { error? }`                           |

### Notable design

- **`MessageData`** carries the full set of Go fields: `key`/`value`/`custom` (base64 in JSON), `topic`, `error`, `timeout` (`i64` nanoseconds), `deadline` + nested `context.deadline` (RFC3339 strings). All fields are `skip_serializing_if=Default-empty` so the wire stays compact when unused.
- **`RequestCancelType`** strict enum: `Canceled(1)` / `DeadlineExceeded(2)`. `from_u16` returns `Error::UnknownCancelType` for anything else.
- **`Request` / `Response` are type aliases**, not separate structs — they share the wire layout with `Message` / `MessageAck`. The packet type byte (`0x71` / `0x72`) is what differentiates them at the dispatcher.
- **`app` module structure** now mirrors `conn` / `mux`: `error.rs` + `packet/{mod, data}.rs`. `app` Cargo.toml gains `serde` / `serde_json` / `base64`. Tests opt into `unwrap`/`expect` via `#![cfg_attr(test, allow(...))]`.

## Tests (14 new, 105 workspace-wide)

- `message_payload_round_trip` — full data with timeout / deadline / context
- `message_payload_empty_data` / `message_ack_payload_round_trip`
- `request_payload_is_message_payload_alias` — type alias substitution
- `stream_payload_round_trip` (data + empty)
- `request_cancel_round_trip` — both variants
- `request_cancel_unknown_type_errors` — `from_u16(99)` → `UnknownCancelType(99)`

author: truhojunbot-tech
body:
## Summary

Closes #103. The CLI \`_wait\` loop used \`_pane_looks_idle\` (a last-line scan for prompt characters) which silently failed against Claude Code's multi-line footer. When the pane showed

    ✻ Cooked for 5m 4s
    ❯
     ⏵⏵ bypass permissions on (shift+tab to cycle)

the LAST line was the bypass-permissions banner, not \`❯\`, so the scan returned False and the wrapper waited the full \`--timeout\` instead of intervening early.

Same fragility class as #84 — text-matching against agent UI strings. Apply the same fix the watchdog adopted in #84-v2: pane content diff.

## Behavior

| Idle duration | Before | After |
|---------------|--------|-------|
| < 2 min | (silent) | (silent) |
| ≥ 2 min | (silent — wrapper waiting until --timeout) | warning: \"no activity for Ns, auto-fail in Ms\" |
| ≥ 5 min | wait for full --timeout, then auto-fail | \`_auto_submit_failed\` with \`watchdog timeout\` summary → fallback policy reroutes |

The auto-fail summary is shaped to match the failover patterns from #85 / #87, so a CLI-side stall directly drives the same rate-limit fallback chain that handles in-flight stream timeouts and watchdog auto-fails.

## Implementation

- \`_pane_changed(pane_target)\` — captures the pane, compares to previous snapshot, returns True iff different. First-call semantics: returns False (no baseline), mirroring \`agent_crew.server._pane_is_busy\`. Subprocess failures also return False so a transient probe error never triggers a false auto-fail.
- \`_PANE_CONTENT_LAST\` per-pane cache; \`_reset_pane_content_cache\` test-only entry point. \`_wait\` resets on entry so consecutive \`crew run\`s don't carry stale snapshots between tasks.
- The polling loop drives off \`_pane_changed\` with explicit thresholds (2 min warn, 5 min auto-fail). The pre-existing deadline-extension path (#92) also moves to \`_pane_changed\`, priming explicitly when the main loop never reached the 30s grace.
- \`_pane_looks_idle\` kept and exercised by a test that pins its known weakness — useful documentation for why we don't rely on it.

## Tests

\`tests/unit/test_cli_idle_detection.py\` (10):
- \`_pane_looks_idle\`: zsh prompt / Completed → idle; multi-line footer (the #103 case) → not idle (the regression we route around)
- \`_pane_changed\`: first call False; unchanged → False; changed → True; past-tense glyph stable across 4 ticks → False; per-pane state independent; subprocess failure → False; reset cache restarts baseline

Full suite: 302/302 passing.

author: gaojian-0106
body:
## Summary

`OPENROUTER_DEFAULT` in `scripts/lib/providers.py` is set to `google/gemini-flash-2.0`, which is not a valid OpenRouter model ID (the segments are reversed). This causes **every** rerank and FunJudge call to fail with HTTP 400 when `LAST30DAYS_REASONING_PROVIDER=openrouter` unless the user has explicitly pinned `LAST30DAYS_RERANK_MODEL` themselves.

## Symptom

```
[Rerank] LLM reranking failed, using local fallback: HTTPError: HTTP 400: Bad Request
[FunJudge] LLM scoring failed: HTTPError: HTTP 400: Bad Request
```

OpenRouter's response body confirms:
```json
{"error":{"message":"google/gemini-flash-2.0 is not a valid model ID","code":400}}
```

Every ranked-evidence cluster ends up tagged `Why: fallback-local-score`.

## Root Cause

`scripts/lib/providers.py:22`:
```python
OPENROUTER_DEFAULT = "google/gemini-flash-2.0"   # segments reversed
```

The valid OpenRouter format is `google/gemini-{VERSION}-flash[-VARIANT]`, e.g. `google/gemini-2.0-flash-001`. `google/gemini-flash-2.0` is not listed.

`LAST30DAYS_PLANNER_MODEL` masks this for the planner because most users pin it, but `LAST30DAYS_RERANK_MODEL` is rarely pinned, so rerank/FunJudge always hit the bad default.

## Fix

Switch to `google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview`.

Rationale for this specific replacement: `providers.py:12` already declares
```python
GEMINI_FLASH_LITE = "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview"
```
as the default for the native Gemini provider (`_MODEL_DEFAULTS["gemini"]`). Aligning the OpenRouter default to the same model keeps both code paths consistent and prevents future divergence whenever this constant is updated.

Alternative considered: minimal-change `google/gemini-2.0-flash-001` (the closest valid ID to the original typo). Happy to switch if you prefer the more conservative fix.

## Validation

After the fix, ran `last30days "Claude Opus 4.7" --quick`:

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `[Rerank] LLM reranking failed` log lines | 1 per run | 0 |
| `[FunJudge] LLM scoring failed` log lines | 1 per run | 0 |
| `Why: fallback-local-score` markers in output | all clusters | 0 |
| LLM-generated `Why:` reasoning lines | 0 | 11 |

Sample of restored LLM-rerank reasoning:
> "Directly addresses benchmark performance comparisons against competitors..."
> "Provides specific technical specifications regarding image resolution capabilities..."

## Diff

```diff
- OPENROUTER_DEFAULT = "google/gemini-flash-2.0"
+ OPENROUTER_DEFAULT = "google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview"
```

One line, restores broken default and aligns OpenRouter with the existing native-Gemini default.

author: noeljackson
body:
**Draft.** Surfacing the design conversation @justinsb opened on #459 about Pod-spec mutation. Not ready to merge — see dependencies below.

## Summary

When a `SandboxClaim`'s `workspaceResources` change while the sandbox is running, patch the Pod's workspace container resources in place rather than waiting for a Pod recreate. Targets K8s 1.27+ with `InPlacePodVerticalScaling`; on older clusters or when the patch fails, falls back to the drift-recreate path from #690.

## Why a draft

This carries the broader sig-apps design question @justinsb raised on #459: in-place mutation of Pod spec on a running Pod is the controversial half of what the original `b2348b0` commit bundled. Pod recreation on template change is uncontroversial (Deployment / StatefulSet / DaemonSet pattern, landing in #690); in-place resize without restart needs explicit sig-apps direction.

## Dependencies

This PR is stacked on top of two others; the diff currently includes their commits so it builds and tests pass standalone:

1. **#459** — adds `SandboxClaim.Spec.WorkspaceResources`. Without this PR's API there's nothing to resize.
2. **#690** — adds the drift-recreate fallback in `controllers/sandbox_controller.go`. Without it, an in-place resize that fails (older kubelet, ephemeral storage drift, anything else) silently leaves the pod mis-sized. With #690, the next reconcile sees the template-hash mismatch and recreates.

Once both have merged, I'll rebase this PR onto upstream main so the diff shows only the resize-specific changes.

## Approach

- New `reconcileWorkspaceResources` invoked from `getOrCreateSandbox` whenever a sandbox already exists for a claim. Patches running Pod resources in place using `client.StrategicMergeFrom`.
- New `buildResizePatch` helper computes the minimal patch by comparing both Requests and Limits against the desired `WorkspaceResources`.
- After patching the Pod, also patches `Sandbox.Spec.PodTemplate` so the new sizing survives a future Pod recreate. Without this the resize is silently best-effort.

## Copilot's four substantive critiques from the original `b2348b0` review have separate fix commits

The PR is structured as: original commits (#459, #690, base resize) + four small Copilot-fix commits that you can review independently:

1. `fix: only swallow IsNotFound in reconcileWorkspaceResources` — the original returned nil on any Get error, hiding RBAC/transient failures.
2. `fix: buildResizePatch compares both Requests and Limits` — the original early-returned when limits matched, ignoring drifted requests.
3. `fix: persist in-place resize back to Sandbox.Spec.PodTemplate` — the original only patched the Pod; a future recreate would revert.
4. `fix: surface reconcileWorkspaceResources errors to the reconciler` — the original logged-and-continued, masking transient failures.

Plus `test: add buildResizePatch regression tests` covering #2.

## Sig-apps thread

/cc @justinsb @janetkuo @soltysh — picking up the design question from https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/pull/459#issuecomment-4226028651 about in-place Pod-spec mutation. Specifically:

- Is delete-and-recreate (#690) the right default everywhere, with in-place resize as an opt-in optimization on supported clusters?
- Or should Sandbox treat in-place resize as primary semantics and document delete-and-recreate as the fallback?
- Are there other Pod-spec fields beyond resources that we should consider for in-place mutation now (KEP-0174 only enables resources; image is mutable too but for "reasons"), or should those wait?

The current implementation models option 1 — drift-recreate is the default; in-place resize is an optimization that runs before recreate would be triggered. Open to direction.

## Outstanding before un-drafting

- [ ] sig-apps direction on the design question above
- [ ] #459 and #690 merge so this PR can rebase to a clean diff
- [ ] Heavier integration tests for `reconcileWorkspaceResources` (persistence to `Sandbox.Spec`, IsNotFound handling, error propagation) — only the pure `buildResizePatch` is unit-tested today

Refs: #459, #487 (closed predecessor), #491, #690.

body:
This PR introduces a major upgrade to the WalkBuddy ML testing pipeline, shifting it from a binary pass/fail architecture to a fully diagnostic evaluation suite. It implements structured error categorization and global ML metrics tracking to provide actionable insights into model performance and threshold tuning.

Key Changes:

- Core ML Metrics Integration: The pipeline now dynamically tracks True Positives (TP), False Positives (FP), and False Negatives (FN) across the entire test suite, outputting global Precision, Recall, and F1 Scores.

- Object-Level Error Intelligence (evaluate_case.py): Replaced flat failure strings with structured error dictionaries. Failures are now categorically tracked as:

    - Low Confidence Drop (with raw confidence score attached)

    - False Negative (completely undetected)

    - False Positive (hallucinations/background noise)

    - Direction Error

    - Logic/Count Error

- Automated Diagnostic Engine (run_test_suite.py): The test suite now generates a contextual intelligence report upon completion. It pinpoints the most common failure mode, identifies the specific object classes causing the issues, and suggests actionable tuning strategies (e.g., threshold adjustments vs. model retraining).

Testing Notes:

Verified that updating the confidence threshold argument dynamically shifts the Precision/Recall tradeoff.

All testing artifacts are successfully ignored by Git, keeping the branch completely clean.

Reviewers can test the diagnostic engine by running python run_test_suite.py --confidence 0.75 to observe the automated drop-off analysis.

author: davior
body:
## Summary
Implements a provider router that manages multiple live flight data providers with automatic failover on rate-limit or authentication errors. Adds real-time usage tracking, persistent request logging, and a new provider status UI component.

## Key Changes

### Backend
- **ProviderRouter** (`provider_router.py`): New service that wraps multiple `LiveFlightProvider` instances and automatically switches to the next available provider when rate-limit or authentication errors occur. Implements the `LiveFlightProvider` protocol for drop-in compatibility.
- **ProviderUsageTracker** (`provider_usage_tracker.py`): Tracks per-provider request counts and errors using an in-memory sliding-window deque for fast real-time counts, with persistence to a new `provider_request_log` database table.
- **Provider Configuration**: 
  - New `providers.json` config file (with fallback search paths) that defines multiple providers with capabilities and rate limits
  - Updated `live_flight_provider_factory.py` to load and instantiate providers from config, with backwards-compatible fallback to `LIVE_FLIGHT_PROVIDER` env var
  - New `PROVIDERS_CONFIG_PATH` setting in `config.py`
- **Database**: New `ProviderRequestLog` model and migration to persist provider request history
- **API Endpoint**: New `/flights/provider-status` endpoint that returns health, usage, and capability info for all configured providers
- **Capability Tracking**: Added `supports_trajectory` field to `LiveFlightCapabilities` across all providers

### Frontend
- **ProviderStatusDot** (`ProviderStatusDot.vue`): New floating UI component showing active provider health status with a dropdown panel displaying:
  - All configured providers with health indicators
  - Request usage (current/max in period)
  - Rate-limit status and expiration times
  - Supported features (time-shift, trajectory)
- **Flights Store**: Added `providerStatus` state and `loadProviderStatus()` action
- **API Client**: New `fetchProviderStatus()` function
- **FloatingControls**: Integrated ProviderStatusDot component
- **Type Definitions**: Added `ApiProviderStatus` and `ApiProviderInfo` types

## Implementation Details
- Failover is triggered only on `rate_limited` or `authentication_failed` error codes; other errors are propagated to the client
- Rate-limited providers have a cooldown period (configurable per provider) before they can be retried
- Higher-priority providers (earlier in config) are automatically restored when their cooldown expires
- Request tracking uses a bounded deque (100k entries) for memory efficiency while maintaining detailed database history
- The router maintains backwards compatibility: if no `providers.json` is found, it falls back to single-provider mode using the env var

## Summary
- Fix production cost-leak: gpt-5.4 calls hit api.openai.com/v1 PAYG ($0.10/call) even after `/login oauth openai` registered Codex Plus subscription. Router never consulted PlanRegistry.
- Adopt openai/codex CLI default semantic (SUBSCRIPTION/OAuth wins, with `forced_login_method` escape hatch).
- Refresh model registry — verified 2026-04-26 against developers.openai.com / platform.claude.com / docs.z.ai. Drop sub-5.3 OpenAI IDs, add gpt-5.5 (OAuth-only), fix 6-month-stale GLM pricing.
- 10 invariant tests + 4 fixture updates.

## Why
v0.51 incident continuation. After v0.52.3 fixed billing-fatal retries / parallel approval / drift, the user discovered LLM calls weren't actually using the OAuth subscription they'd just registered. Daemon log confirmed: every "안녕" hit `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` at $0.10/call.

Root cause: `_resolve_provider("gpt-5.4")` is a static map → `"openai"`. The PlanRegistry resolver (`resolve_routing()`) existed and worked correctly but only `mascot.py` (UI) and `glm.py` (GLM-specific) called it. The 4 `call_llm*()` entry points in `core/llm/router.py` bypassed it entirely.

User experience: paid for ChatGPT Plus, paid AGAIN per LLM call. Equivalent footgun documented in Anthropic's Claude Code Help Center ("env-key wins over OAuth subscription") — Codex CLI defaults the OTHER way (subscription wins) per `forced_login_method` unset semantics, openai/codex#2733/#3286.

## Changes
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `core/auth/plans.py` | + `PLAN_KIND_PRIORITY` map (SUBSCRIPTION → OAUTH_BORROWED → CLOUD_PROVIDER → PAYG) |
| `core/llm/registry.py` | + `PROVIDER_EQUIVALENCE` (openai↔openai-codex, glm↔glm-coding) + `equivalent_providers()` helper |
| `core/auth/plan_registry.py` | `resolve_routing()` step 1.5 — equivalence-class scan with kind-priority sort + `_apply_forced_login_method()` |
| `core/config.py` | + `forced_login_method: dict[str, str]` setting (Codex CLI parity escape hatch) |
| `core/llm/router.py` | + `_route_provider(model)` helper. 4 call sites swapped from `_resolve_provider` to `_route_provider` |
| `core/llm/providers/codex.py` | `_resolve_codex_token()` checks ProfileStore for `openai-codex` profile FIRST, then ~/.codex/auth.json fallback |
| `core/config.py` | OPENAI_PRIMARY/CHAIN refreshed to gpt-5.5 generation; CODEX_PRIMARY → gpt-5.5 (OAuth-only) |
| `core/llm/token_tracker.py` | MODEL_PRICING + MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOW refreshed (gpt-5.5 added; sub-5.3 IDs dropped; GLM stale prices fixed) |
| **NEW** `tests/test_routing_policy.py` | 10 invariant cases (equivalence-class, kind priority, explicit-override precedence, escape hatch, router wiring source-level) |
| `tests/test_codex_provider.py`, `test_llm_client.py`, `test_model_escalation.py` | 4 fixtures updated for refreshed model lists |

💡 What: Updated `useParentalStore` selectors in `App`, `NavigationHeader`, `SessionMonitor`, and `useScreenTimeEnforcement` to target specific derived data (`children.length > 0` or specific `activeChild`) instead of subscribing to the entire `children` array. Added performance benchmark tests to document the impact.
🎯 Why: Due to Immer's behavior, whenever a single property of any child is updated (e.g., `totalTimeToday` updating every 10 seconds), the `children` array reference changes. This caused widespread unnecessary React re-renders in components that merely needed to check if the array was empty or needed access to a single child.
📊 Impact: Completely eliminates unnecessary re-renders in the main App shell and critical UI components during active child sessions, improving performance and reducing CPU overhead. 
🔬 Measurement: Run the added benchmarks (`npm run test -- src/performance/zustand_children_hasChildren_opt.test.tsx` and `src/performance/zustand_selector_children_benchmark.test.tsx`) to see the difference between unoptimized and optimized behavior.

## Summary

- Adds `docs/specs/2026-04-26-state-management-model-design.md` as the canonical state-management contract: rule, decision tree, refactor scope, and follow-up plan. Each agent session loads a short `## State Management` section in `CLAUDE.md` that mirrors the rule and links here.
- Aligns six lock-based hotspots from the audit. `SearchIndexHandle` becomes a bespoke `SearchActor` (full migration). The rest collapse multi-lock atomicity smells into single guards and carry a `// state: lock-ok` comment naming the constraint, with the deeper refactors tracked as follow-up entries (F1–F8) in the spec.
- Restores `docs/specs/` and `docs/plans/` as the only canonical doc directories; deletes the orphaned `docs/superpowers/`.
- Two rounds of multi-agent deep review applied inline (commits `7a7653e` round-1 and `e311c1c` round-2). 18 issues fixed in-PR, 4 new follow-ups (F5–F8) tracked.

## Refactor map (matches spec § 1–6)

| § | What | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crates/client/src/search/handle.rs` | Bespoke `SearchActor` owning index + config + recents + status; async API; web call sites use `spawn_local`. |
| 2 | `crates/client/src/nickname.rs` `MemNicknameStore` | Collapse `RwLock<HashMap>` + `RwLock<u64>` → `Mutex<MemNicknameInner { map, version }>`; lock-ok annotation, F1 follow-up. |
| 3 | `crates/client/src/trust.rs` `InMemoryTrustStore` | Already single guard; lock-ok annotation, F1 follow-up. |
| 4 | `crates/client/src/lib.rs` `topics` + `join_links` | Annotate, F4 follow-up (~25 sync call sites + generic `N::Topic`, deferred). |
| 5 | `crates/client/src/state.rs:180` `message_db` | Delete the dead field + `MessageDb` + `StoredMessage` + `open_message_db` (PersistenceActor owns persistence). |
| 6 | `crates/web/src/{trust_store,profile/nickname_store,state_bridge}.rs` | Collapse `WebNicknameStore` lock pair; annotate the rest, F1 + F2 follow-up. |

## Why no hard CI gate

Spec rejected a grep-based or custom-clippy gate: the iroh boundary and a handful of legitimate cases would generate false positives, and allowlist comments degrade into noise. Agent-context awareness via the `## State Management` block in `CLAUDE.md` is the chosen enforcement mechanism. F3 in the spec keeps the door open if drift recurs.

## Follow-up work (tracked in spec § Follow-up)

Each entry has a `Trigger:` line in the spec naming the dedicated PR title to open.

- **F1.** Eliminate `NicknameStore` and `TrustStore` traits in favour of `NicknameActor` + `TrustActor`. ~25 sync call sites in web; estimated ~600 lines.
- **F2.** Re-evaluate `state_bridge.rs` cache shape (Leptos `Resource` vs `StateActor`) once F1 lands.
- **F3.** Custom clippy lint or grep gate, only if drift recurs after F1.
- **F4.** Migrate `ClientHandle.topics` + `join_links` into actors. Generic over `N::Topic`; touches `MutationContext` + `ListenerContext` + ~25 sync sites across `listeners.rs`, `mutations.rs`, `joining.rs`, `lib.rs`, `connect.rs`.
- **F5.** SearchActor head-of-line + rebuild-storm fix. Rebuild blocks Query in FIFO order; the rebuild Effect has no debounce. Fix is chunked-Rebuild + `Debounce<Rebuild>` wrap. (User-visible search-as-you-type latency.)
- **F6.** Browser-tier coverage for `SearchIndexHandle` consumers. The new `spawn_local` + Effect path has no wasm-pack test.
- **F7.** Sealed `ClientSpawner` to narrow the `system()` API surface, rather than exposing the full `SystemHandle` to external consumers.
- **F8.** Search-query debouncing-flicker fix via generation tag or Leptos `Resource` migration.

## Review history

- Round 1 — three parallel agents (SearchActor refactor, collapsed-lock annotations, spec/docs/dead-code) flagged 15 issues; all fixed inline in `7a7653e`.
- Round 2 — two fresh agents (verification + wider-scope sweep) verified all round-1 fixes clean and surfaced 8 new findings; 3 inline-fixed, 5 tracked as F5–F8 in `e311c1c`.
- Cumulative: 0 Critical / 0 High / 0 Medium remaining in-PR; all Medium-severity findings either fixed or tracked.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete infrastructure-as-code deployment module for DynamoUI Canvas on GCP, along with database schema, configuration, and containerized services for both backend and frontend components.

## Key Changes

### Infrastructure & Deployment
- **Terraform module** (`infra/modules/dynamoui/`) — Self-contained GCP deployment provisioning:
  - Cloud SQL database and user for Canvas
  - GCS bucket for canvas-output with versioning and 90-day archive lifecycle
  - Cloud Run services for backend (FastAPI, internal LB) and frontend (nginx, public)
  - Cloud Run Job for database migrations and optional scaffold resync
  - Secret Manager secrets for database credentials and LLM API key
  - Service account with least-privilege IAM roles
  - Optional Serverless VPC Access connector
  - Comprehensive variables and outputs for flexible configuration

- **Cloud Build pipeline** (`cloudbuild.yaml`) — Multi-step CI/CD workflow:
  - Builds and pushes backend Docker image
  - Updates and executes canvas-migrate job with optional resync
  - Deploys backend with traffic routing
  - Deploys frontend with latest tag

### Database & Migrations
- **Canvas database schema** (`alembic/versions/canvas/0001_canvas_schema.py`) — Initial schema with tables:
  - `canvas_sessions` — Session lifecycle tracking
  - `canvas_turns` — Conversation turns with intent parsing
  - `canvas_themes` — Generated CSS themes
  - `canvas_layouts` — Layout configurations
  - `canvas_enriched_skills` — Enriched skill definitions
  - Proper indexing and foreign key constraints

- **Alembic configuration** — Canvas-specific migration setup with environment detection and URL configuration from environment variables

### Application Configuration & Scripts
- **Canvas settings** (`canvas/config.py`) — Pydantic-based configuration:
  - Database connection (Unix socket and TCP support for Cloud SQL Auth Proxy)
  - Output directory management (GCS mount in Cloud Run, local path in dev)
  - Session TTL and resync flag

- **Migration entrypoint** (`scripts/migrate_entrypoint.sh`) — Cloud Run Job entry point:
  - Runs Alembic migrations
  - Optionally scaffolds database and uploads generated skills/patterns to GCS
  - Generates resync manifest

### Containerization
- **Backend Dockerfile** — Multi-stage build:
  - Builder stage with gcc and libpq-dev for compiled dependencies
  - Runtime stage with minimal footprint
  - Includes migration script and Alembic config
  - Runs FastAPI via uvicorn

- **Frontend Dockerfile** — Node.js + nginx:
  - Builds React/Vite application
  - Serves via nginx with environment variable substitution
  - Custom entrypoint for dynamic BACKEND_URL injection

- **nginx configuration** (`dynamoui-frontend/scripts/nginx.conf.template`) — Production-ready setup:
  - SPA routing with fallback to index.html
  - API and WebSocket proxying to backend
  - Security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy)
  - Asset caching with 1-year expiry

### Documentation
- **Module README** — Usage examples, resource overview, and input/output reference

## Notable Implementation Details
- **Flexible VPC connectivity** — Supports both existing VPC connectors and auto-creation
- **Secret management** — All sensitive values (DB passwords, LLM API key) stored in Secret Manager with environment variable injection
- **Unix socket support** — Canvas DB connections via Cloud SQL Auth Proxy Unix domain socket for secure, passwordless authentication
- **Conditional scaffold resync** — `CANVAS_DB_RESYNC` flag enables optional database introspection and skill generation on migration runs
- **Health checks** — Backend includes startup and liveness probes; frontend includes nginx health endpoint
- **Resource optimization** — CPU idle enabled for Cloud Run services, configurable min/max instances, startup CPU boost for backend

## What changed

`POST /vocabulary/export/obsidian` now returns 404 when an explicit `book_id` is provided but the book does not exist in the cache.

## Why

Previously, `_build_and_push_book` checked `if book: check_book_access(book, user)` but silently continued when `get_cached_book` returned `None`. It would push an empty/default markdown file to GitHub and return 200. Users had no indication the book was missing.

The fix adds a book existence check and `check_book_access` call in the outer scope before delegating to `_build_and_push_book` for the explicit single-book export path. The export-all path (no `book_id`) is unaffected — it iterates over book IDs from the user's own vocabulary, which are always valid.

author: decoargen-create
body:
## Problema

El módulo Marketing/Senydrop está en desarrollo y a veces hace falta resetear el state (`?reset=1`, ErrorBoundary "Limpiar todo y reiniciar", DevTools "Clear site data"). Esos caminos hacen `localStorage.clear()` total y se llevaban puesto los datos de Viora — que es la plataforma productiva y **NO** tiene que reiniciarse cuando probás features de dev.

## Solución

Mover el state de Viora a **IndexedDB**. Storage paralelo: un `localStorage.clear()` no lo toca. Solo "Clear site data" de DevTools afecta ambos (ese flow queda como destructivo explícito y consciente).

## Archivos

- `src/vioraStorage.js` — nuevo módulo con `loadVioraState`, `saveVioraState`, `clearVioraState`, `createBackup`, `listBackups`, `restoreBackup`. Usa DB `lab-viora` y object store `state`.
- `src/App.jsx`:
  - `useReducer` arranca con `INITIAL_STATE` y se hidrata async.
  - **Migración automática**: si encuentra el state legacy en `localStorage` (key `viora-state-v2`), lo copia a IndexedDB y limpia la key vieja. Una sola corrida — el user no pierde datos.
  - Persistencia con debounce 200ms a IndexedDB.
  - **Backup automático cada hora** (rotativo, máx 24 snapshots) en IndexedDB como red de seguridad.
  - Loader "Cargando datos…" mientras hidrata (~50ms en máquinas modernas).
  - Botones "Vaciar todos los datos" y "Cargar datos de demo" pasan a IndexedDB.

## Test plan

- [ ] Hacer hard refresh — ver el loader brevemente, después la app con los datos persistidos.
- [ ] `?reset=1` — el localStorage se limpia, Viora sigue intacta.
- [ ] Crear/editar/borrar órdenes → recargar → verificar persistencia.
- [ ] "Vaciar todos los datos" del menú → confirma → recarga vacía. Después se puede recargar demo.

# 🔒 Recon 2.0: Security Analysis Report

This pull request contains a comprehensive security analysis report generated by Recon 2.0.

⚠️ **Note:** No automated fixes were generated. The vulnerabilities found require manual review and remediation.

## 📊 Executive Summary

# Executive Summary

## Overall Security Posture: Critical Risk

Our comprehensive security analysis of the NestJS backend application has identified **29 vulnerabilities** across the codebase, including **5 critical** and **5 high-severity** issues that require immediate attention. The current compliance posture is concerning, with all major frameworks—SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI-DSS—scoring at only **40%**. This indicates significant gaps in security controls that could expose the organization to regulatory penalties and data breach risks.

The critical and high-severity vulnerabilities identified pose substantial risk to the organization's data integrity and operational continuity. These findings typically include issues such as authentication weaknesses, injection vulnerabilities, or insecure data handling patterns common in backend systems. With 10 vulnerabilities in the critical and high categories combined, attackers could potentially exploit these weaknesses to gain unauthorized access, exfiltrate sensitive data, or disrupt business operations.

From a business perspective, the low compliance scores across all four regulatory frameworks represent material risk. Non-compliance with GDPR can result in fines up to 4% of annual global revenue, while HIPAA violations can reach $1.5 million per incident category annually. Beyond financial penalties, a security incident could damage customer trust, disrupt operations, and create significant legal liability. The absence of automated fixes for any identified vulnerabilities indicates that remediation will require dedicated engineering resources.

**Recommendation:** We strongly advise treating this as a priority initiative. Immediately triage and remediate the 5 critical vulnerabilities within the next 7-14 days, followed by high-severity issues within 30 days. Concurrently, engage compliance and engineering teams to develop a 90-day roadmap to elevate all compliance scores above 80%. A follow-up assessment should be scheduled upon completion of critical remediation efforts to validate the improved security posture.

## 🔍 Vulnerabilities Found

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| 🔴 Critical | 5 |
| 🟠 High | 5 |
| 🟡 Medium | 8 |
| 🟢 Low | 11 |
| **Total** | **29** |

## ❓ Why No Automated Fixes?

Automated fixes were not generated for the following reasons:

- Vulnerabilities require manual code review and context-specific fixes
- Fixes may require architectural changes or business logic updates
- Some vulnerabilities are in third-party dependencies (update required)
- Complex security issues that need human judgment

## 📋 Compliance Status

| Framework | Score | Status |
|-----------|-------|--------|
| SOC 2 | 40% | ❌ Critical |
| GDPR | 40% | ❌ Critical |
| HIPAA | 40% | ❌ Critical |
| PCI-DSS | 40% | ❌ Critical |

## 💡 Top Recommendations

1. **Implement Data Encryption at Rest and in Transit** (Priority 1)
   Immediately address SOC 2 and HIPAA encryption requirements. For NestJS: 1) Enable TLS 1.3 for all API endpoints using Helmet middleware, 2) Implement AES-256 encryption for PHI/sensitive data using crypto module or @nestjs/crypto, 3) Configure database-level encryption (e.g., PostgreSQL TDE or MongoDB encrypted storage engine), 4) Store encryption keys in a dedicated secrets manager (AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault). Timeline: 1-2 weeks for critical paths.

2. **Establish Role-Based Access Controls (RBAC) for HIPAA Compliance** (Priority 2)
   Implement comprehensive access controls in NestJS: 1) Use @nestjs/passport with JWT strategy for authentication, 2) Create custom Guards and Decorators for role-based authorization (@Roles decorator), 3) Implement the principle of least privilege - define granular permissions for PHI access, 4) Add audit logging for all PHI access using NestJS interceptors, 5) Integrate with an identity provider (Auth0, Okta) for centralized user management. Timeline: 2-3 weeks.

3. **Remediate Critical and High Vulnerabilities** (Priority 3)
   Address the 10 identified vulnerabilities systematically: 1) Run 'npm audit' and 'yarn audit' to identify dependency vulnerabilities, 2) Update all NestJS core packages (@nestjs/core, @nestjs/common) to latest stable versions, 3) For the 4 manual fixes required, create dedicated tickets with security context, 4) Implement Snyk or Dependabot for continuous vulnerability monitoring, 5) Establish a 48-hour SLA for critical vulnerabilities, 7-day SLA for high. Timeline: 1 week for critical, 2 weeks for high.

4. **Deploy Comprehensive Audit Logging and Monitoring** (Priority 4)
   Essential for both SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance: 1) Implement structured logging using @nestjs/common Logger with Winston or Pino, 2) Log all authentication events, PHI access, and administrative actions, 3) Include correlation IDs across requests using cls-hooked or AsyncLocalStorage, 4) Ship logs to a SIEM solution (Splunk, ELK, or cloud-native options), 5) Create alerts for suspicious patterns (multiple failed logins, unusual data access). Timeline: 2 weeks.

5. **Implement Input Validation and API Security Hardening** (Priority 5)
   Strengthen NestJS API security: 1) Use class-validator and class-transformer for strict DTO validation on all endpoints, 2) Implement rate limiting using @nestjs/throttler to prevent abuse, 3) Add CORS configuration with explicit allowed origins, 4) Enable Helmet middleware for security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.), 5) Implement request sanitization to prevent injection attacks, 6) Add API versioning for controlled deprecation. author: rashidee
body:
## Summary

Today the conductor-* skills record traceability between PRD.md / BUG.md requirement codes (USxxxxxxx, NFRxxxxxx, CSxxxxxxx, RFxxxxxxx, TCxxxxxxx, BUG-XXX) and generated source code **only in transient Markdown tracking files** (`IMPLEMENTATION_MODULE.md`, `BUG_FIX_PLAN.md`, `BUG_MASTER.md`, PRD.md `### Bug` section). `git blame`, IDE symbol search, and downstream audits cannot surface the originating requirement for a given line of code without first opening those tracking files.

This PR makes the **source code itself self-describing**.

### `conductor-feature-develop`

- **Step 3.3** — every newly created source file (entity, repository, service, mapper, controller, view template, listener, scheduled job, configuration class) must begin with a top-of-file doc comment listing the `USxxxxxxx`, `NFRxxxxxx`, `CSxxxxxxx`, `RFxxxxxxx` codes it implements. Comment style follows the language: Javadoc / PHPDoc / JSDoc / `{{-- --}}` / `@* *@` / `<!-- -->` / `#`.
- **Step 3.4** — every Playwright test name must be prefixed with the `TCxxxxxxx` test case code from `TEST_SPEC.md` (e.g., `'TC0000123: User can create an employer'`), and each test must carry a JSDoc traceability comment listing the User Stories, NFRs, and any `[BUG-XXX]` regression coverage.
- **Critical Rule 19** — code-level traceability is MANDATORY.

### `conductor-defect`

- **Step 2.5** — every method / block / template region modified by a fix must carry a `[BUG-XXX]` marker comment using the language's native comment style. If the file already has a top-of-file traceability comment from `conductor-feature-develop`, append the `[BUG-XXX]` code to its `Bug fixes:` line.
- **Critical Rule 15** — code-level bug traceability is MANDATORY.

### Version bump
`marketplace.json` and `plugin.json` bumped 1.1.28 → 1.1.29.

## Test plan

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the messaging and user profile features across both backend and frontend. The main changes include enriching chat message data with sender details, refining the unread message logic, exposing a new API for fetching the current user's profile, and updating frontend components and types to utilize these enhancements.

**Messaging and Chat Improvements:**

- Chat message objects now include `senderName` and `senderAvatar`, both in backend (`messages.interface.ts`) and frontend types, allowing the UI to display richer sender information. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2d9109bbc99b3d15e4f7b1b8356f86b3cc97634d1cadaaa9c5aa5ce9dfd3cdd3R23-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-033dcf2f5d96e933dcd88654e3d01ca2326bdec86d3ba618e9840d428b565599R16-R17)
- When fetching chat history, the backend now queries user details for message senders and includes their name and avatar in each message object. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-68b2dbcf33db3c3f97b3354750437d8f0d8b4ed395d34cc7097952db648ff058R242-R252) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68b2dbcf33db3c3f97b3354750437d8f0d8b4ed395d34cc7097952db648ff058R261-R267)
- The frontend components (`ChatWindow`, candidate messages page) use the new sender fields to display accurate avatars and names, utilizing a `getSenderAvatar` utility for consistency. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d9cf39834109cef0523801cb8f49d9a3d6867c12c3778ff5059b46e1016886R47-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cc09d7dc5cc5c09357cc8cf521ce323c21d04f886c47f3160c303559aa88e7a6L178-R217) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cc09d7dc5cc5c09357cc8cf521ce323c21d04f886c47f3160c303559aa88e7a6L243-R286)

**Unread Message Logic:**

- The unread status logic in the backend has been improved: chats are not marked as unread if the latest message was sent by the current user. This is also covered by new unit tests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-68b2dbcf33db3c3f97b3354750437d8f0d8b4ed395d34cc7097952db648ff058L146-R146) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68b2dbcf33db3c3f97b3354750437d8f0d8b4ed395d34cc7097952db648ff058L155-R158) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c653fc65d8884ee423dca842f8eac8a80a7b087d8132d83aa5320e5af6fe6571L299-R302) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c653fc65d8884ee423dca842f8eac8a80a7b087d8132d83aa5320e5af6fe6571R313-R349)

**User Profile API:**

- A new backend endpoint (`GET /api/user/me`) and corresponding service method allow the frontend to fetch the full authenticated user profile, including avatar and personal details. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c51d721bb87dda9e7e30783e1d4e99888ecfeacbbecb064a98f3c37e4614da36L1-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c51d721bb87dda9e7e30783e1d4e99888ecfeacbbecb064a98f3c37e4614da36R18-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f7cd4c53f61ababff62b471af8286454c1d9cdb0420afc49a072d479cc932486R21-R34) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f7cd4c53f61ababff62b471af8286454c1d9cdb0420afc49a072d479cc932486R68-R108) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-a1e073281968959c3fe0c5d765e2b18c29835a76aa55b714517f427013e91c18L2-R17)
- The frontend now uses this endpoint to obtain the user's avatar for chat contexts, ensuring accuracy even if the avatar changes.

**Frontend State Management and Type Updates:**

- The socket context now tracks the active chat ID, allowing components to stay in sync with the user's current conversation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-574a515cf43cde72dc3cec07502a794f880f29ae32d34cf09b6f73780179835bL3-R12) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-574a515cf43cde72dc3cec07502a794f880f29ae32d34cf09b6f73780179835bR27) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-574a515cf43cde72dc3cec07502a794f880f29ae32d34cf09b6f73780179835bR68-R69)
- Types for chat messages and summaries have been updated to reflect the new sender fields.

**Miscellaneous Improvements:**

- Message lists are now consistently ordered oldest-to-newest for display, and debug logs have been added to help trace message transformation and sorting. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d9cf39834109cef0523801cb8f49d9a3d6867c12c3778ff5059b46e1016886R72) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b1d9cf39834109cef0523801cb8f49d9a3d6867c12c3778ff5059b46e1016886R96-R99) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-cc09d7dc5cc5c09357cc8cf521ce323c21d04f886c47f3160c303559aa88e7a6L266-R314)

These changes collectively enhance the user experience in chat by providing more context for each message, improving notification accuracy, and ensuring user profile data is up-to-date across the application.

author: sho7650
body:
## Summary
Closes the Dependabot CVE backlog (20 vulns: 2 critical, 9 high, 9 moderate) on `main` and unblocks local installs that were failing because `psycopg2==2.8.6` cannot compile against modern Apple clang (`gettimeofday` implicit declaration is now an error in Xcode 15+).

- **Runtime**: `runtime.txt` → `python-3.12.13` (was 3.6.1, EOL Dec 2021); `mise.toml` pins `python = "3.12"` for local/prod parity.
- **Django**: 3.1.2 → **5.2 LTS** (extended support through Apr 2028).
- **Database driver**: `psycopg2==2.8.6` (source build) → `psycopg2-binary>=2.9,<3.0` (prebuilt wheels).
- **Other deps**: `dj-database-url` 2.3, `gunicorn` 23, `whitenoise` 6.8, `asgiref` 3.8, `sqlparse` 0.5; drop pinned `pytz` (Django 4+ uses stdlib `zoneinfo`).
- **Code migrations for Django 5**:
  - `herokuwebinar/urls.py`: `url(r'^…$', …)` → `path('…', …)` (the legacy `url()` was removed in Django 4.0).
  - `herokuwebinar/settings.py`: drop deprecated `USE_L10N`; add `DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD = 'django.db.models.BigAutoField'`; replace `STATICFILES_STORAGE` with the modern `STORAGES` dict.
- **Hygiene**: ignore `.venv/`.

## Verification
- `python manage.py check --deploy` returns no issues (only the expected `SECRET_KEY` length warning when run with a test value).
- `python manage.py check` clean.
- Live `Client().get('/')` returns **200 "Hello world!"** under Django 5.2.13 / Python 3.12.13.
- All packages install from prebuilt wheels — no compiler invocation required.

## Test plan
- [ ] `pip install -r requirements.txt` in a fresh Python 3.12 venv.
- [ ] `python manage.py check --deploy` — expect zero warnings (with a real `SECRET_KEY`).
- [ ] `python manage.py migrate` against a real PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL`.
- [ ] Heroku staging deploy: confirm `python-3.12.13` is picked up and `gunicorn herokuwebinar.wsgi` boots.
- [ ] Confirm `/` still responds 200 in staging and HSTS / `X-Frame-Options` headers are present.

body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements and refactoring to the backend API and some frontend improvements. The main focus is on making the dashboard endpoints more flexible by supporting advanced filtering, switching to the new `vehicle_positions_enriched` data source, and adding new endpoints for summary metrics, routes, and areas. Some frontend updates improve module imports and the header UI.

**Backend API improvements and refactoring:**

*Generalized filtering and query improvements:*
- Added `_build_filter_clauses` and `_build_cache_key` helper functions to support flexible filtering (by date, time, route, direction, speed delta, areas, etc.) across dashboard endpoints, reducing code duplication and improving maintainability.
- All major dashboard endpoints (`speeding-events-today`, `dashboard-stats`, `dashboard-comparison-metrics`) now accept advanced filter parameters and use the new helper functions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1R25-R108) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1L53-R166) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1R210-R301)

*Data source and schema updates:*
- Switched from the old `matched_positions` table to the new `vehicle_positions_enriched` table and updated all queries and field names accordingly (e.g., `road_name` → `way_name`, `maxspeed_kmh` → `speed_limit_kmh`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1L53-R166) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1L86-R178) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1L101-R191) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4a4d9df7259af5b73c5679428eb374cb9c47a91a15ce8ee9d86dc046e69b6ba1L139-R327) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7930a58585f2d7cc53070e280b266e33d8b3e8c5126b63f87676e5dee350372bL31-R36) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7930a58585f2d7cc53070e280b266e33d8b3e8c5126b63f87676e5dee350372bL51-R51) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-7930a58585f2d7cc53070e280b266e33d8b3e8c5126b63f87676e5dee350372bL75-R79)

*New endpoints and caching:*
- Added `/dashboard-summary-metrics` endpoint to provide aggregate speeding event statistics with filtering support.
- Added `/routes` and `/areas` endpoints for populating dropdown filters in the frontend, with in-memory caching for performance. (F8bea9a1L373R373)
- Removed the now-redundant `/routes` endpoint from `map.py`

**Frontend improvements:**

*Module and UI updates:*
- Added `FormsModule` and `MatButtonModule` to Angular app module imports to support forms and button styling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-13b05cc841c9553102bbc2af4d4b7fe4fd9d1df773b08aeddb3840f8f4fac6e2R4-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-13b05cc841c9553102bbc2af4d4b7fe4fd9d1df773b08aeddb3840f8f4fac6e2R41-R42)
- Updated the app header: replaced emoji with a Material icon, simplified branding, and improved semantic structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4b1a7f8e18a71c67ff1b558ed681fac01984b7e242472dbf7f50fc82d49c16a0L2-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4b1a7f8e18a71c67ff1b558ed681fac01984b7e242472dbf7f50fc82d49c16a0L21-R20)
- Disabled Angular CLI analytics for the project.

**Summary of most important changes:**

**Backend API:**

## Add seeded terrain generator in src/sim/terrain.ts

**Category:** `feature` | **Contributor:** uJJZGeu2imjA7Z8Fp-tXL

Closes #113

### Changes
Create src/sim/terrain.ts exporting generateChunk(seed: number, chunkCoord: { x: number; y: number; z: number }) that returns a Chunk filled with stone below a height threshold, a dirt band above the stone, grass as the topmost solid block, and air above. Derive a per-column surface height by combining the seed with the world (x, z) column coordinates via the Mulberry32 PRNG in src/sim/random.ts (e.g. hash seed + column coords into a sub-seed via createRng / hashStringToSeed, then sample one or more octaves of value noise) so the same (seed, chunkCoord) pair yields byte-equal chunks. Use the Chunk type and its setter helpers from src/sim/chunk.ts (created by the existing queued chunk task — this task should not land until that file exists). Add tests/sim/terrain.test.ts covering: (1) determinism — calling generateChunk twice with identical (seed, chunkCoord) produces chunks whose underlying voxel arrays are byte-equal; (2) layer ordering — for each column, every air voxel sits above any solid voxel, the topmost solid voxel is GRASS, the band immediately below grass is DIRT, and everything below the dirt band is STONE; (3) continuity — surface heights for two horizontally adjacent chunk coordinates differ by at most a small bound (e.g. <=2) at the shared boundary columns, so the world looks continuous.

author: lexluthor0304
body:
## Summary
Phase One IQ4 (.iiq) users report the page hanging forever on upload — file is ~170 MB and `libraw-wasm@1.1.2`'s bundled LibRaw doesn't fully support PhaseOne's compressed stream at 100/150 MP. Worker enters a degenerate loop, `await raw.imageData()` never resolves, loading overlay spins forever.

This PR adds two complementary safety nets, both reusing the embedded-preview decoder added in PR #81:

### 1. Proactive shortcut (eliminates the wait)
- `.iiq` + file >100 MB → skip LibRaw entirely → `tryNefJpegPreview` → ~1s image in front of the user
- Opt-in by extension — CR2/NEF/ARW/DNG over 100 MB still go through LibRaw for full 16-bit precision
- User's 170 MB IQ4 file hits this path

### 2. Wall-clock timeout (backstop)
- `raw.open`: 30s default, 60s for >200 MB
- `raw.imageData`: 90s default, 180s for >200 MB
- Timeout → `raw.worker.terminate()` (release WASM heap, ~1-2 GB) → retry via `tryNefJpegPreview`
- If preview also missing → throw tagged `RAW_DECODE_TIMEOUT` → friendly i18n message (zh/en/ja) suggests Adobe DNG Converter / Capture One

Same `tryNefJpegPreview` handles both NEF "snow" (PR #81) and new IIQ timeout. Two error codes distinguish user-facing copy: `RAW_DECODE_GARBLED` vs `RAW_DECODE_TIMEOUT`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build:web` clean
- [x] `garbledCheck.test.mjs` + `image16.test.mjs` regression — both pass
- [ ] Manual: `_DSC3111.NEF` (lossless compressed) → still LibRaw 16-bit path, well under 90s
- [ ] Manual: 170 MB IQ4 IIQ → preview shortcut, ~1s, 8-bit image visible
- [ ] Manual: corrupt RAW or no embedded preview → friendly i18n timeout error after 90s, no permanent hang

## Out of scope (intentional)
- Reflashing libraw-wasm with newer LibRaw (long-term fix; separate effort)
- Progress feedback in overlay
- Worker pool reuse after terminate

author: copilot
body:
Adds `docs/exploit.md` documenting the two-vulnerability attack chain used for bootloader-locked Xiaomi 13 downgrade.

### Vulnerability 1: ABL cmdline parameter injection
- `fastboot oem set-gpu-preemption` doesn't sanitize input — attacker injects `androidboot.selinux=permissive` into kernel cmdline via space-separated append
- Same class as CVE-2016-10277 (Nexus 6 bootloader cmdline injection)

### Vulnerability 2: IMQSNative local privilege escalation
- `miui.mqsas.IMQSNative` transaction code 21 exposes arbitrary command execution as root with no caller validation
- With SELinux permissive (from vuln 1), `dd` writes engineering ABL directly to `abl_a`/`abl_b` partitions

### Anti-Rollback bypass
- Engineering ABL skips rollback index verification in AVB chain
- Allows flashing firmware with lower rollback index than device's recorded maximum

Full attack flow table and references included.

author: nadaverell
body:
## Summary

Six small visual-review fixes, each addressing a real hierarchy or affordance gap surfaced in dark-mode review of the live nonprod cluster.

### Pod drawer pill hierarchy

In `WorkloadView` (the drawer header used everywhere), the kind pill (\"Pod\") and status pill (\"Running\") were both filled, both bordered, both `font-medium`. For healthy resources both render in green hues — collapsing into \"two green pills\" until you read the text. Kind is metadata (the user already clicked the resource); status is the signal.

New `getKindColorOutline` helper in `drawer-components.tsx` strips the fill classes, giving the kind pill an outline-only treatment that retains its color identity in border + text. Status keeps its filled treatment. Clear hierarchy: outline = label, filled = signal.

### Traffic empty states

The \"no traffic observed\" branch previously used a Filter icon — implies the user's filters caused the emptiness, even when nothing was being seen at all. Misleading.

Refactored to the new `EmptyState` primitive (#533) with three branches:
- **Filtered out**: `tone='filtered'` + Filter icon + \"Show all\" CTA
- **Warning** (`flowsData.warning`): `tone='neutral'` + AlertTriangle icon
- **No traffic yet**: `tone='neutral'` + Activity icon + dynamic headline `\"Observing via {sourceName} — no traffic yet\"`

Connection-failed stays custom (no error tone in EmptyState — that scoping was deliberate in #533).

The dynamic headline matters: it puts the connection status (\"yes, we're hooked up and waiting\") in the place the user is actually looking, not just the small corner pill.

### ContextSwitcher dropdown

Three small changes to the dropdown items and group header:

- Region pill moved to the right of each row (`ml-auto`), so the cluster name has uninterrupted left-aligned scan and the region floats as a tag
- Raw kubeconfig context line gets `opacity-70` on top of tertiary — quieter without inventing a new color tier; still copy/pasteable via tooltip
- Group header (\"GKE · blitz-prod-404612\") bumps to `text-[11px] font-semibold` on `bg-theme-elevated/60` with a thin bottom border. Reads as a deliberate section divider instead of a default-looking small grey label.

### Secret Reveal eye icon

Per #533's review: the muted \"Reveal\" buttons read as text. Keeping the deliberate-friction muted-color treatment (the AlertBanner's cautionary tone shouldn't compete with a loud CTA) but adding an Eye / EyeOff icon makes the action scannable as a button, not dead text.

### Certificates list — Domains column

Widened from `w-48` (192px) to `w-56` (224px) to fit typical production FQDNs without ellipsis truncation. Tooltip on hover still handles the long tail.

## Test plan

- [x] `make tsc` clean
- [x] `/visual-test` against live nonprod cluster: all five UI areas verified — context switcher dropdown, traffic \"no traffic yet\" empty state, pod drawer header pill hierarchy, certificates list domains column, secret drawer reveal/hide eye icon toggle
- [x] No console errors during walkthrough

author: thorspb
body:
Two bugs caught by post-cutover live testing.

## 1. Menu profile stuck on "Loading..." — `fetchCurrentUser` wrong endpoint

`/auth/user` returns only `{id}`. Switched to `/user/me` which returns `{id, email, firstName, lastName, fullName, emailVerified}`. Map `fullName` → `name` to match the existing `AuthUser` shape.

Verified live by Playwright test `tests/migration/prod-login.spec.ts` which logged in, navigated to /menu, and confirmed the profile section showed "Loading..." with the body of /user/me being just the id field.

## 2. Google SSO 401 — backend doesn't support GIS popup flow

Lovable used Google Identity Services popup → ID token → POSTed to `/auth/sso` with `platform: 'web'`. Backend's `google-sso.provider.ts` handles `platform=web` by calling `exchangeAuthorizationCode(token)` which expects an OAuth authorization code, not an ID token. Exchange fails → 401.

Fixed by switching Google to the redirect flow that Apple already uses. The `/auth/callback/google` handler from Phase 5 closes the loop.

### Side effects
- Deleted `src/services/googleAuth.ts` (GIS popup loader, unused)
- Frontend no longer needs `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` — Google client ID lives only on the backend
- The Google Cloud Console "Authorized JavaScript origins" requirement for `app.versemate.org` no longer applies (the redirect flow uses Authorized redirect URIs which are already configured for Apple via the same backend endpoint)

## Test plan
- [ ] After merge + deploy: navigate to `/menu` → profile pic + name should render (not stuck on Loading)
- [ ] Click 'Continue with Google' → redirects to backend → Google login → back to app, signed in

author: aminsato
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4282 — joining a QR for an existing seed-phrase vault on a device that already has it threw `DuplicateVaultException` after keygen completed, leaving the *Vault created successfully* screen stuck on an infinite spinner.

- **Primary fix** — `JoinKeygenViewModel` (KEYGEN/KeyImport branch) now compares the QR's `hexChainCode` against existing vaults before doing anything. If a match is found, it skips mediator discovery + keygen entirely and routes to `Route.Home(openVaultId = existingVault.id)`. The non-blank guard prevents matching legacy vaults that have an empty stored chain code.
- **Defence in depth** — `KeygenViewModel.saveVault()` now catches `DuplicateVaultException` on the non-override path (only `KEYGEN`/`KeyImport` can hit it; reshare/migrate use `upsert`). On catch it looks up the existing vault by `pubKeyECDSA`, stops the mediator service, and routes to Home — so the success screen never hangs even if the early `hexChainCode` check ever misses (e.g. the QR carries an empty chain code, or another flow saved the vault concurrently).
[Screen_recording_20260426_050958.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24d7646d-5709-41f4-8b0e-4818fc32e854)

## Why two layers

The early `hexChainCode` check is the user-friendly path: skip the whole join when we already know the vault is here. The save-side catch protects the cases the early check can miss — initiating-device flows, blank/legacy chain codes, races against another save — so we never regress to the original infinite spinner.

## Test plan

- [ ] Device A has Vault X (seed-phrase). Device B has the same Vault X stored. Start join keygen flow on B with A's QR — B should land on Home with Vault X selected, no spinner hang, no error toast.
- [ ] Normal first-time join on a clean device still completes keygen and reaches the backup flow.
- [ ] Reshare / Migrate flows are unaffected (still upsert; never throw `DuplicateVaultException`).
- [ ] Verify on emulator with two debug builds (forward port 18080 + socat per README).

body:
## Problem

When an org goes past their product analytics usage limit, the global red banner explains usage is exceeded but doesn't say _why_ session recording filtering can suddenly look broken. Several session recording filters (event-based filters, autocapture, person/session properties) depend on processed events. When ingestion is throttled by the product analytics quota, recordings still get captured but those filters can silently hide them — confusing users who expected those recordings to show up.

## Changes

- Add an in-context red `LemonBanner` at the top of the session replay filters panel (`ReplayFiltersTab`) in `RecordingsUniversalFiltersEmbed.tsx`.
- Only renders when the org's `product_analytics` product has `percentage_usage > 1`, mirroring the trigger used by the global banner in `billingLogic`.
- New Storybook entry under `Replay/Tabs/Home/Filters Banner` with over-limit and under-limit stories so the banner can be reviewed visually.

Banner copy:

> You're past your usage limit for product analytics. Some session recording filtering relies on the processing of events; recently recorded sessions might not be visible when you filter even though they've been recorded.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Code). No manual browser testing was performed.

- Added a Storybook story (\`ProductAnalyticsOverLimit\` / \`ProductAnalyticsUnderLimit\`) so a human reviewer can verify the banner visually under both states.
- Reviewed the trigger condition against \`billingLogic.tsx\` lines 869-882 to confirm it uses the same \`percentage_usage > 1\` threshold the global banner uses.

body:
## What Changed

Additive change (no breaking impact). Adds the tinyexec adapter at `shell-cassette/tinyexec` plus full test coverage.

```ts
import { x } from 'shell-cassette/tinyexec'

const r = await x('git', ['status'])
console.log(r.stdout)
```

Both `execa` and `tinyexec` peer deps are optional. Install only what you use.

### Source

- `src/options-tinyexec.ts` (17 lines): option validator. Rejects `persist:true` (subprocesses outliving host process can't be replayed) and `stdin` as Result (pipe chaining requires live process). Accepts everything else.
- `src/tinyexec.ts` (104 lines): thin adapter wiring tinyexec hooks into the shared `runWrapped` envelope. Honors `throwOnError` on replay (inverse of execa's `reject` default; tinyexec doesn't throw by default on non-zero exit).
- `package.json`: adds tinyexec to dev/peer deps with `optional: true`, plus the `./tinyexec` exports entry.

### Tests

| File | LOC | Tests | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `tests/unit/options-tinyexec.test.ts` | 77 | 12 | Validator: accepted shapes, rejection paths, error messages |
| `tests/unit/wrapper.test.ts` | 176 | 7 | Envelope behavior with synthetic hooks (runner-agnostic) |
| `tests/unit/tinyexec-adapter.test.ts` | 261 | 10 | buildCall, captureResult, synthesize behavior with mocked tinyexec |
| `tests/integration/wrapper-tinyexec.test.ts` | 137 | 4 | Real fs (temp dirs) + mocked tinyexec; record creates cassette, replay reads cassette, lazy load, lazy write |
| `tests/e2e/tinyexec-record-replay.test.ts` | 98 | 4 | Real tinyexec spawning real `node`; round-trip on `node --version`, non-zero exit, throwOnError, multi-line stdout |
| `tests/error-path/tinyexec-errors.test.ts` | 102 | 6 | UnsupportedOptionError on persist:true, ShellCassetteError inheritance, AckRequiredError, ReplayMissError variants |

Test count: 109 -> 136 (post-extract) -> 179 (this PR). +43 new tests.

## Documented replay limits (tinyexec)

- `result.process` is `null` (no live `ChildProcess` to expose).
- `result.pipe()` throws `UnsupportedOptionError`.
- `result.kill()` is a no-op.
- `for await (line of result)` async iteration throws `UnsupportedOptionError`.
- Synchronous reads of `pid`, `killed`, `aborted` before `await` are not honored (the wrapper returns `Promise<TinyResult>`, not the tinyexec ProcessPromise shape).
- `signal` mapping is lossy: tinyexec exposes only `killed: boolean`, not the actual signal name. We unconditionally record `'SIGTERM'` on kill. Tracked in backlog.

## Notes

- The first version used `Options` (tinyexec's required-fields interface) in the public function signature. tinyexec's `Options` declares all six fields as required; tinyexec itself wraps the call site in `Partial<Options>` for ergonomics. Without `Partial<>`, common usage like `x('node', ['-v'], { throwOnError: true })` fails typecheck with TS2345. Verified empirically and fixed.
- tinyexec preserves trailing newlines from stdout (e.g., `console.log('c')` produces `'a\nb\nc\n'`, not `'a\nb\nc'`). The line-array round-trip handles this correctly.

## Related Issues

Issue #26: `ensureMatcher` type smell, tracked separately; affects test scaffolding (added comment with details).

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `npm test` (28 files / 179 tests / all green)
- [x] `npm run test:coverage` (88.28% statements / 83.87% branches; above 80/75 thresholds)

author: johanrd
body:
> [!NOTE] > This is part of a series where Claude has audited `eslint-plugin-ember` against [jsx-a11y](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y), [vuejs-accessibility](https://github.com/vue-a11y/eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility), [angular-eslint](https://github.com/angular-eslint/angular-eslint/tree/main/packages/eslint-plugin-template), [lit-a11y](https://github.com/open-wc/open-wc/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin-lit-a11y) and [html-validate](https://gitlab.com/html-validate/html-validate), `ember-template-lint`, and the HTML and WCAG specs. ## Summary Add `template-heading-level`: enforce a heading outline within a single template file. Default-on: at most one `

` per sectioning root (the only check reliably verifiable within a single file in a component-based app). Opt-in: `allowSkippedLevels: false` to also flag level skips, `minInitialRank` to set a floor on the first heading. `` / `role="dialog"` / `role="alertdialog"` create nested sectioning roots that reset the count. **Authoring convention, not a WCAG requirement.** - **Premise 1:** Heading rank (`

`–`

`) is the primary navigation affordance screen readers expose for skimming a page — JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver all offer heading-jump commands that rely on rank order. Authoring guides ([WebAIM Semantic Structure](https://webaim.org/techniques/semanticstructure/), [MDN `

`–`

`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Heading_Elements#accessibility_concerns), [A11y Project](https://www.a11yproject.com/posts/how-to-accessible-heading-structure/)) consistently recommend a contiguous outline with no skipped ranks so heading-jump lands where users expect. - **Premise 2 (honesty disclaimer):** This is an **authoring convention**, not a WCAG requirement. No WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion prohibits skipped heading levels. [SC 2.4.6 Headings and Labels](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/headings-and-labels.html) is about *content quality* of headings and labels (do they describe topic/purpose), not hierarchy. [Technique G141](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/general/G141) is a *sufficient technique* for SC 1.3.1/2.4.6 — one way to conform, not itself normative. The HTML outline algorithm that would have made sectioning elements reset heading rank [was removed from WHATWG HTML](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/7829) after never being implemented by browsers or AT. `html-validate`'s `heading-level` enforces the same convention on the same authoring-guide basis. - **Conclusion:** Only the multiple-`

` check is reliably verifiable within a single template file, so it is the only default-on check. Skipped-level and initial-rank checks defeat themselves in component-based apps (intermediate headings live in child components and layouts the lint can't see), so both default to off and are opt-in via `allowSkippedLevels: false` and `minInitialRank: 'h1'|'h2'|…`. The rule as a whole remains opt-in (not added to any preset). ## Fix - New rule `lib/rules/template-heading-level.js`; tests in `tests/lib/rules/template-heading-level.js` (48 cases, covering default + all three opt-in configurations). - Stack-based traversal: entering a sectioning root pushes a fresh `{current: 0, h1Count: 0}`; exiting pops. Heading visitor updates the top frame. - `isSectioningRoot` (`template-heading-level.js:32-42`) recognizes ``, `role="dialog"`, `role="alertdialog"` — mirroring html-validate's defaults. - Schema: `allowMultipleH1` (`boolean`, default `false`), `allowSkippedLevels` (`boolean`, default `true`), `minInitialRank` (`'h1' | 'h2' | ... | 'h6' | 'any'`, default `'any'`). The three defaults flip the rule from html-validate's all-on posture to Ember-friendly minimal-on: only the within-file multi-h1 check is active by default. ## Scope caveat — shapes the defaults Ember apps compose pages from many templates (layouts, routes, components). The *true* outline spans files this rule can't see. That's not just a caveat — it's a design input that determined the defaults: - **Skipped levels** (`

` → `

`): intermediate `

` may live in a child component the lint can't see. Can't reliably distinguish real skip from cross-file composition. **Default: `allowSkippedLevels: true` (off).** - **Initial rank**: layouts and parent routes commonly supply the outer `

`. A route template that starts at `

` is almost always correct, not a bug. **Default: `minInitialRank: 'any'` (off).** - **Multiple `

` in same sectioning root**: a within-file signal — two `

` in one template file is suspect regardless of what ancestors render. **Default: on.** Teams whose templates are flat enough that cross-file tracking is reliable can opt in to the stricter checks per-scope via ESLint overrides. ## Prior art | Plugin | Equivalent | Verified behavior | |---|---|---| | [jsx-a11y](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/main/src/rules/heading-has-content.js) | `heading-has-content` | Different concern — checks every heading has content; does NOT check hierarchy. | | [vuejs-accessibility](https://github.com/vue-a11y/eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility/blob/main/src/rules/heading-has-content.ts) | `heading-has-content` | Same as jsx-a11y. | | [lit-a11y](https://github.com/open-wc/open-wc/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin-lit-a11y/lib/rules/heading-hidden.js) | `heading-hidden` | Different — checks headings aren't hidden via `aria-hidden`/`hidden`. | | [@angular-eslint/template](https://github.com/angular-eslint/angular-eslint/tree/main/packages/eslint-plugin-template/src/rules) | — | No equivalent hierarchy rule. | | [html-validate](https://gitlab.com/html-validate/html-validate) | [`heading-level`](https://gitlab.com/html-validate/html-validate/-/blob/v10.13.1/src/rules/heading-level.ts) — [spec](https://gitlab.com/html-validate/html-validate/-/blob/v10.13.1/src/rules/heading-level.spec.ts) | Full DOM-walk implementation. Our port operates within a single template; otherwise logic matches. html-validate documents the rule as convention-based, not WCAG-mandated. | No peer implements heading *hierarchy*; html-validate is alone in this space, and frames the rule as codifying the WebAIM/MDN authoring convention — same framing we adopt. ## Flags (default config) ```hbs {{! Multiple h1 in one sectioning root — the default check }}

One

Two

``` ## Flags (opt-in config) With `allowSkippedLevels: false`: ```hbs

Title

Subsection

{{! skipped h2 }} ``` With `minInitialRank: 'h1'`: ```hbs

Start

{{! initial heading coarser than h1 }} ``` ## Allows (default config) ```hbs

Title

Section

Subsection

Another section

{{! Default: skipped levels permitted — child components may supply intermediates }}

Title

Subsection

{{! Default: initial-rank check off — layout supplies the outer h1 }}

Route title

{{! dialog creates a nested sectioning root — h1 inside is fine }}

Page title

Dialog title

Dialog section

 ``` ## Notes - **Opt-in, framed as authoring convention**: not added to any preset config. Teams that have not adopted the "no skipped heading levels, one h1 per sectioning root" convention should not be forced into it by enabling this rule. - **Sectioning-root reset is also conventional.** The HTML outline algorithm that would have given `` / `role="dialog"` a spec-defined "reset" role was [removed from WHATWG HTML](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/7829) after never being implemented. The `` reset matches html-validate's behavior and reflects how AT modality actually works with dialogs, but it is convention, not spec. - Configure `minInitialRank` at the route-template scope (via ESLint overrides) for layouts that supply the `

` outside the file.

author: johnjezl
body:
## Summary

Third milestone of the admin & telemetry suite. Mirrors M1's pattern (latency_hist + rate_ewma) to the remaining two consumers: eviction (Rust runtime) and inference (Lua model_infer dispatch).

* New: `kernel/include/admin_telemetry.h` + `admin_telemetry.c` — consumer-scoped storage. Eviction has decision-rate + fallback-rate; inference has call-rate + error-rate. Each consumer also tracks lifetime totals + latency histogram.
* `runtime/src/mm/eviction/registry.rs` calls `admin_telemetry_record_eviction_decision(dt)` (from `select_victim`) and `admin_telemetry_record_eviction_fallback()` (from `update_feedback(_, true)`). FFI is wait-free and scalar-only.
* `kernel/src/lua_slm.c` wraps the three `slm.model_infer*` bindings with `slm_get_time_ns()` measurement → `admin_telemetry_record_inference(dt, ok)`.
* New Lua bindings (`slm_lib_safe` — read-only):
  - `slm.eviction_decision_rate()` — same shape as M1's `slm.sched_decision_rate()`.
  - `slm.inference_rate()` — calls/s + errors/s + percentiles + totals (single global series; per-model breakdown deferred — see below).
  - `slm.latency_histogram("eviction"|"inference")` now returns real bucketed data (M1 stubbed both to nil).

## Per-model inference rate deferral

Spec §6.2 specs `slm.inference_rate()` as `{[model_name] = {calls_per_s, p50_ns, ...}}`. M3 ships a single global series instead. Rationale (recorded in spec §14 question 3):
- A fixed-size in-kernel map of (model_name → rate_ewma) is awkward sizing and wastes BSS.
- M4's telemetry feed publishes `/telemetry/inference/<model>/result` events. A subscriber gets natural per-model aggregation without kernel-side state.
- If a demo needs per-model in-kernel breakdown before M4 lands, it's a small follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 unit tests in `kernel/tests/test_admin_telemetry.c` cover: reset semantics, decision/fallback counting, call/error counting, latency bucket placement (5µs lands in bucket 7 = `[4096, 8192)`), NULL-out-arg safety.
- [x] `make kernel` (QEMU) — clean.
- [x] `make test` (QEMU) — 8 new tests pass; 11 M2 + 18 M1 tests still green; only #412 pre-existing failures.
- [x] Cross-platform builds clean: `RASPI5`, `JETSON_ORIN_NANO`, `X86_64`.
- [ ] Hardware (Jetson) — meaningful exercise needs a real eviction load + inference request stream. Deferred to the demo runbook in M7.
