author: rbonill
body:
Aligns the cognitive-target color labels with the maze rules ([`rules/maze/1_Field.adoc:134-138`](https://github.com/robocup-junior/rcj-rescue-rules/blob/maze/rules/maze/1_Field.adoc#L134-L138)). Surfaced from the [`/review` playbook on #108](https://github.com/robocup-junior/rcj-rescue-cms/pull/108#issuecomment-4322138786) and discussed as a deferred follow-up in #110.

## TL;DR

The rules say the +2 ring color is **Blue**. The implementation calls it `'C'` for "Cyan" and reserves `'B'` for "Black" — so a contributor reading the rules and then the code finds the obvious shorthand inverted. This PR switches to CMYK printers' shorthand: `K` = blacK, `R` = Red, `Y` = Yellow, `G` = Green, `B` = Blue.

| Old letter | Old name | New letter | New name | Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `B` | Black | `K` | Black | −2 |
| `R` | Red | `R` | Red | −1 |
| `Y` | Yellow | `Y` | Yellow | 0 |
| `G` | Green | `G` | Green | +1 |
| `C` | Cyan | `B` | Blue | +2 |

## Why this matters (plain language)

Robot teams calibrate their cameras against the published rules figure (`rules/maze/media/cognitive_target.png`). The figure renders the +2 ring as a specific shade of blue (RGB `(0, 176, 240)`). Sampling the figure pixel-by-pixel:

```
Black:  (0, 0, 0)         Red:    (238, 0, 0)
Yellow: (255, 255, 0)     Green:  (0, 176, 80)
Blue:   (0, 176, 240)
```

The CMS already used these exact RGBs for the printable `cognitive_targets/*.png` assets — but called the +2 color "Cyan" in code, in filenames, and in the editor UI. So:
- Robots **would** detect the printed targets correctly today (the colors match).
- But contributors wrote `'C'` instead of `'B'` for what the rules call Blue, and `'B'` instead of `'K'` for what's clearly Black. The labelling drift in #108 — `(0, 176, 240)` listed as `Cyan` in `tools/cognitive_targets_generator/generate_cognitive_targets.py:18-19` — is what made the original review flag this.

Fixing the names removes the foot-gun and brings the schema in line with the rules vocabulary. The visual output is unchanged for the printable target sheets; the editor's ring-layer overlays were also regenerated so the sky-blue rings in the modal preview match what gets printed (the previous overlays used pure cyan `(0, 255, 255)`).

## What's in here (3 commits)

1. **`c52c5378` — Rename cognitive-target colors to rules-aligned K/R/Y/G/B.**
   - Updates both python generators (`generate_cognitive_targets.py`, `generate_ring_layers.py`) to the new dict keys, comments, and color names.
   - Renames all 2,882 `cognitive_targets/*.png` files that contained `B` or `C` (the other 243 — pure R/Y/G combos — are unchanged). No re-rendering: their pixel data was already rules-correct.
   - Regenerates all 100 `cognitive_rings/*.png` files. The ring layer generator had a different palette (`(0, 255, 255)` cyan, `(0, 128, 0)` green, `(255, 0, 0)` red) than the printable targets — now in lock-step.

2. **`de4d2513` — Update schema, scoring, PDF, and editor UI to K/R/Y/G/B letter codes.**
   - `models/mazeMap.js` — Mongoose enum `['B','R','Y','G','C']` → `['K','R','Y','G','B']`.
   - `helper/scoreCalculatorRules/2026.js` and `helper/competitionTargetsPDF.js` — `cognitiveColorValues` / `colorValues` tables.
   - `public/javascripts/admin/mapEditor/maze_2026.js` — five inline color tables, the color array in the auto-generator, plus all `'B'`/`'C'` literals.
   - `public/javascripts/{judge,manual,sign}/maze_2026.js` — the `getColorValue` switch and color tables in each.
   - `public/templates/maze_cognitive_target_modal_2026.html` — 25 ring-color buttons (5 rings × 5 colors).
   - `public/lang/{en,ja}.json` — i18n key `cyan` → `blue`.

3. **`2cc89c41` — Add migration script.**
   - `scripts/migrate-cognitive-colors.js` translates `B → K` and `C → B` across every `mazeMap.cells.tile.cognitiveTargets.{top,right,bottom,left}.rings.ring1..ring5`. Run with `--dry-run` for a preview. Idempotent.

## Deployment ordering (important)

The schema enum change in commit 2 will cause Mongoose to reject any existing map document still holding `B`/`C` under the old meanings the next time it's saved (e.g. an admin opens an existing map in the editor and clicks save). To avoid that:

```bash
# Step 1 — preview (no writes):
DB_CONNECT_STR=<your-uri> node scripts/migrate-cognitive-colors.js --dry-run

# Step 2 — run for real, BEFORE rolling out the new code:
DB_CONNECT_STR=<your-uri> node scripts/migrate-cognitive-colors.js

# Step 3 — deploy this PR.
```

The migration is idempotent so re-running after deploy is harmless.

## Verification

- All touched JS / JSON / Python files pass syntax checks (`node --check`, `JSON.parse`, `ast.parse`).
- Sampled the regenerated `cognitive_rings/top_ring1_B.png` — center pixel is `(0, 176, 240)`, matching the rules figure.
- Sampled a renamed target (e.g. `YBYYY.png`, formerly `YCYYY.png`) at the ring2 radius — pixel is `(0, 176, 240)`.
- 3,125 cognitive_targets PNGs and 100 cognitive_rings PNGs preserved.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run the migration in dry-run against a staging DB; confirm reasonable counts.
- [ ] Open an existing 2026 map in the editor; check that the cognitive target modal shows Blue (not Cyan) buttons and the preview thumbnail matches the printable PDF.
- [ ] Generate a competition-targets PDF for that map; confirm Blue rings match the rules figure.
- [ ] Save the map; confirm Mongoose accepts it (no enum validation error).
- [ ] Run the migration again post-save; confirm 0 ringsTranslated (idempotency).

## Out of scope

- Removing `H/S/U/Red/Yellow/Green` from the `VICTIMS` enum — separate PR.
- Score-sheet snapshot tests — separate PR.
- The `cognitive_targets/*.png` bulk in git — could be replaced with runtime ring composition, but unrelated to this rename.

author: vitbokisch
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 experiment from the [architectural experiments plan](.claude/plans/architectural-experiments-2026-q2.md) (#325, #333). **Hypothesis dramatically validated.**

## TL;DR

| Metric | Baseline (`<Button>`) | Collapsed (hand-written compile output) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock per run (200 mounts × 5 runs) | **8.80ms** | **0.20ms** | **44× faster** |
| Wall-clock per mount | 44µs | 1µs | 44× |
| `runtime.mountChild` per visible button | **9.0** | **1.0** | 9× reduction |
| `runtime.tpl` per visible button | 0 | 1 | cloneNode fast path active |
| `styler.resolve` per button | **110** | 0 | -100% |
| `unistyle.descriptor` per button | **105** | 0 | -100% |
| `rocketstyle.getTheme` per button | 5 | 0 | -100% |

Ratio collapsed / baseline = **2.3%** — well past the 30% GRADUATE threshold. `mountChild` = 1 per visible — exact target.

## Why this matters

Boot profile of `examples/perf-dashboard` showed: 2,814 `mountChild` calls for ~50-100 visible elements (~30-50× amplification) AND only 50 of 2,814 mounts (1.7%) hit the cloneNode fast path. **The architectural cost lives at the wrapper-chain layer that styler / elements / rocketstyle build.** This experiment confirms that collapsing those wrappers at build time, for literal-prop call sites, produces a 44× per-mount speedup with `mountChild` dropping from 9 to 1.

## Striking secondary findings worth their own attention

These weren't part of the original hypothesis but the data surfaced them:

1. **Each rocketstyle Button mount fires 110 `styler.resolve` + 105 `unistyle.descriptor` calls.** Cache hits, but the lookup cost adds up. Worth a separate audit even if the compiler-collapse RFC takes its own time.
2. **`mountChild` = 9 per visible button**, not the 5 estimated from the architectural diagram. More wrapper layers than expected.
3. **Pseudo-state CSS (`:hover`, `:focus`, `:active`, `:disabled`) costs ZERO at runtime in the collapsed version** because all four rules are in the same generated class.

## Honest caveats

The 44× factor is the **upper bound**. A real compiler must handle:

- **Reactive props** (signal-driven dimensions): NOT statically resolvable; fall through to current path.
- **Event delegation**: collapsed prototype has no `onClick`; the compiler would emit `el.__ev_click = handler` after cloneNode (~5µs/mount).
- **Theme switching**: statically-resolved buttons stay on the old theme until remount unless the compiler keeps a small reactive class swap (~2-3µs/mount).

Even at 30% statically-resolvable + 44× win + identity-on-rest, weighted improvement is ~6× across the codebase. Still massive.

## Decision: GRADUATE

| Criterion | Threshold | Actual | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock | collapsed ≤ 30% of baseline | **2.3%** | ✅ exceeds 13× |
| `mountChild` | ≤ 1.5 per visible | **1.0** | ✅ exact target |

## Follow-up — next plan (NOT another experiment)

Write a focused RFC for `@pyreon/compiler`:
1. Detect `<RocketComponent state="X" size="Y" ...>` call sites with all-literal dimension props.
2. At build time: run the rocketstyle dimension chain in the compiler.
3. Emit the resolved class string + a `_tpl()` cloneNode call for the final DOM element.
4. For non-resolvable call sites, emit the current `h(Component, ...)` path unchanged (transparent fallback).
5. Estimate ~40% statically-resolvable in real apps before committing — audit `examples/ui-showcase` + the bokisch.com app.
6. Engineering cost: ~4-6 weeks. Ship as feature flag in `@pyreon/compiler`.

## What lands

- `examples/experiments/e2-static-rocketstyle/PLAN.md` — original plan
- `RESULTS.md` — full writeup with caveats + next steps
- `results/<sha>.json` — typed measurement record
- `baseline-Button.tsx` + `collapsed-Button.ts` + `e2.browser.test.ts` — repro
- Harness updates to `@pyreon/experiments` package (UI deps + vite-plugin browser-test wiring)

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bun run test:browser` (in `examples/experiments`) — 2/2 passed (DOM parity check + benchmark with assertions)
- [x] Reproducible: ran 3 times, ratio held in 1.1-2.3% range (run-to-run noise on sub-millisecond measurements)

  - `updateCursor`: same custom-cursor / default-cursor split plus `brushPreviewGradientVisible = false` post-condition.
  - `currentTool` watcher: clears `lastColorSelectPoint` only when leaving `MaskColorFill`.
  - `handlePointerDown`: touch-ignore, pen pointer registration, middle-button pan, space+left pan, `MaskPen`/`PaintPen` left-button drawing, `PaintPen` continue-drawing branch (`button !== 0 && buttons === 1`), `MaskBucket` flood fill (with coord transform), `MaskColorFill`, alt+right brush adjustment, right-click drawing for drawing tools, no-op for non-drawing tools.
  - `handlePointerMove`: touch-ignore, cursor position update, middle-button pan, space+left pan, non-drawing-tool ignore, alt+right brush adjustment while `isAdjustingBrush`, left/right drag drawing.
  - `handlePointerUp`: state cleanup (`isPanning` / `brushVisible` / `isAdjustingBrush`), pen pointer removal, touch-pointer early bail before `drawEnd`.

## Review Focus

- Mock store is wrapped in `reactive()` so the `watch(() => store.currentTool, ...)` actually fires when tests mutate `currentTool`. Plain object mocks would silently no-op the watcher branch.
- Each `setup()` runs `useToolManager` inside its own `effectScope`, stopped in `afterEach`. Without scoping, watchers from previous tests stay attached to the shared reactive store and accumulate (a single mutation in test N would call `clearLastColorSelectPoint` N times).
- Mocked `app.extensionManager.setting.get` because `useBrushDrawing` factory reads two settings synchronously at construction time. The mock returns deterministic defaults so we don't need `useSettingStore` plumbing.
- Pointer-event factory builds the minimal shape (`button` / `buttons` / `pointerType` / `offset*` / `client*` / `altKey` / `pointerId`) — no jsdom `PointerEvent` constructor noise. `preventDefault` is a `vi.fn()` because the source calls it unconditionally.
- Style aligned with sibling tests: `should ...` naming, `describe` grouped by exposed function/watcher, typed `MockStore`, helper `pointerEvent({ ... })` and `setup()`.

author: sophusdavid
body:
perf(training): improve VLM TFLOPS calculation with actual sequence length and ViT

## What does this PR do ?

Fixes inaccurate TFLOPS reporting for VLM training where the reported FLOPS was based on the statically configured `cfg.model.seq_length` instead of the dynamically padded sequence lengths that FlashAttention actually processes. This led to significant overestimation (up to ~2.6x for typical VLM SFT scenarios with short sequences + images).

The PR introduces a per-micro-batch accumulator pattern that captures the real padded sequence length and vision patch count from each `forward_step` invocation, scales them by data-parallel size for global estimation, and feeds them into an extended `num_floating_point_operations()` API.

Closes #3498

## Changelog

- **vlm_step.py**
  - Accumulate `_flops_seqlen_sum` and `_flops_seqlen_sq_sum` across micro-batches using `tokens.shape[1]` (actual padded length).
  - Accumulate `_flops_vision_patches` from `visual_inputs.image_grid_thw` / `video_grid_thw`.
  - Add `"total_tokens"` to `packed_seq_params` for downstream visibility.

- **train.py**
  - Reset `_flops_*` accumulators to 0 before each `wrapped_train_step` call.
  - After the step, read accumulated per-rank totals, scale by `dp_size` for global FLOPS, and pass effective `seq_length` to `training_log`.
  - Remove the earlier `seq_length` return value from `train_step` (reverting to original 8-element return signature).

- **flop_utils.py**
  - Add `vit_flops()` helper for Vision Transformer encoder FLOPS (bidirectional attention + GELU MLP + patch merger).
  - Extend `num_floating_point_operations()` signature with optional `seqlen_sum`, `seqlen_squared_sum`, and `num_vision_patches` parameters.
  - Add `_compute_vit_flops()` that derives per-image patch count from total batch patches for correct quadratic attention scaling.

- **train_utils.py**
  - `training_log()` now accepts `seq_length` parameter and uses accumulated `_flops_vision_patches` (scaled by `data_parallel_size`) for consistent per-log FLOPS recomputation.

## Before your PR is "Ready for review"

**Pre checks**:

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?
  - Added `test_flops_calculation.py` with 13 verification tests covering VLM and non-VLM scenarios.
- [ ] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?
- [ ] Does the PR affect components that are optional to install? (Ex: Numba, Pynini, Apex etc)
  - [ ] Reviewer: Does the PR have correct import guards for all optional libraries?

## Additional Information

- Related to #3498
- Verified on H20(BF16 148TFLOPS) Qwen3.5-VL-9B dense model SFT: old method reported ~199 TFLOP (seq=4096, no ViT), new method reports ~77 TFLOP (actual seq=1280 + ViT=15.5 TFLOP).

## New files

- **`main.py`** – FastAPI app; `Player` + `Match` SQLModel tables; lifespan that creates tables and launches the background updater; `/import-matches/`, `/players/`, `/matches/` endpoints.
- **`updater.py`** – Periodic task (`UPDATE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, default 5 min) that iterates every `Player`, fetches new match history from the Halo API in batches of 25 (stopping at `Player.latest_match_id`), filters via `_passes_criteria()` (`game_variant_category == DEFAULT_GAMEMODE`), fetches full stats for passing matches, and persists them in a single transaction.

- **`requirements.txt`** – `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `sqlmodel`, `spnkr`, `aiohttp`, `python-dotenv`.
- **`.env.example`** – All required env vars (`AZURE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REFRESH_TOKEN`, `DATABASE_URL`, `UPDATE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `DEFAULT_GAMEMODE`).
- **`README.md`** – Setup walkthrough, env var reference, database migration notes (auto-created via `create_all`; Alembic path documented for production), and `uvicorn` start command.

## Key design points

`Player.latest_match_id` acts as a per-player cursor — on each cycle only matches newer than that UUID are downloaded, keeping API usage minimal. Criteria logic is isolated in `_passes_criteria()` for easy extension.

author: mlitvk
body:
Add a cache for the value of a logstor record.

The cache is integrated with the logstor index. Each index entry has an
optional cache entry that holds the mutation that is associated with the
entry.

The cache shares the LSA region and LRU with the normal row_cache of
non-logstor tables for fairness, and shares the same metrics.

This allows to serve reads directly from the cache, avoiding the read
from disk and deserialization, improving read performance for hot rows.

Fixes https://scylladb.atlassian.net/browse/SCYLLADB-3018

no backport - logstor is a new feature

results:
logstor reads from cache: 378k reads/sec @ 1ms p99
logstor reads from disk: 191k reads/sec @ 1ms p99

body:
## Summary

- Adds `REQUIRE_PREBAKED` env-var to `scripts/run-integration-tests.sh`. When set to `1`, any GHCR pull failure that would silently fall back to vanilla HAPI instead exits non-zero with a clear diagnostic and `USED PREBAKED: no — EXITING (REQUIRE_PREBAKED=1)` banner.
- Adds `USED PREBAKED: yes/no` banner at the end of the prebake resolution block so every run's cache status is visible in logs at a glance.
- Sets `REQUIRE_PREBAKED: "1"` in `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` so CI integration tests always fail loudly on GHCR auth failure rather than silently running on vanilla images.

**Before:** if GHCR auth failed in CI, integration tests fell back to vanilla `hapiproject/hapi:v8.8.0-1` and ran to completion. Results looked identical to a real prebake run. CI could have been running vanilla for weeks undetected.

**After:** `REQUIRE_PREBAKED=1` makes CI fail loudly with a diagnostic pointing to the exact fix needed. Every passing CI run now asserts `USED PREBAKED: yes` in the logs — verifiable, not hoped.

Closes one of the three gaps documented in issue #191 (Phase 1 of the pre-bake slow-start fix plan).

- [x] Lint: `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` — clean
- [x] Unit tests: 308 passed
- [ ] Integration tests run in CI with `USE_PREBAKED=1 REQUIRE_PREBAKED=1` — will pass on green GHCR path; will exit non-zero with diagnostic on auth failure

author: fpbrault
body:
## Problem
When a note was released with the sustain pedal held, then retriggered while the pedal was still held, releasing sustain would incorrectly latch the old sustained voice instead of releasing it, causing notes to hang indefinitely.

## Root Cause
The bug was in `CosmoProcessor::set_sustain()`. When sustain is released, it checks if each sustained voice should be released by verifying if the note is still held in `active_notes`. However, the original check used the note *number* rather than the voice *index*:

```rust
// WRONG: checks if ANY note with this number is held (doesn't account for voice reuse)
let still_held = note.is_some_and(|n| 
    self.active_notes.iter().any(|e| e.note == n)
);

// CORRECT: checks if THIS SPECIFIC VOICE is held
let still_held = self.active_notes.iter().any(|e| e.voice_idx == i);
```

When the same note is retriggered:
1. Old voice becomes sustained (when released with pedal down)
2. New voice starts playing the same note
3. Both voices exist for that note number
4. When sustain releases, the `note.is_some_and()` check finds the note in `active_notes` (the new voice) and skips releasing the old voice
5. Old sustained voice remains stuck

## Solution
Check for the specific voice index in `active_notes` instead of the note number, ensuring each voice is independently checked.

## Testing
Added comprehensive unit tests in `cosmo-pd101` covering:
- Basic sustain pedal behavior
- Holding notes while sustain is active
- The specific regression case: same note retriggered while sustain is held
- Multiple notes with sustain
- Edge cases with legato and still-held notes

All 9 new tests pass.

Closes the long-standing "sustain stuck" issue where notes would sometimes not release properly when retriggering with the sustain pedal held.

author: noefontana
body:
## Summary

Lands the instance-segmentation preset surface: three logical commits stacked behind `feat/instance-segmentation-preset`.

- **`fix(gpu)` LSJ valid-region propagation** — `BatchCopyPaste.forward` now consults `padding_mask` end-to-end, generalizing the `depth_valid` machinery (ADR-0007 §2) to a second per-pixel signal `image_valid := ~padding_mask`. `BatchedPlacementSampler` bounds translates inside the per-sample valid rect (`valid_extent: [B, 2]`) and AND-gates a source-bbox-in-pad clause; `AffinePropagator` warps the mask via the shared `_warp_validity_gate` template; `_effective_mask` (tile + dense) ANDs warped image_valid so source-pad zeros never enter the composite. Also fixes `FixedSizeCrop._pad_value_for` writing `255` for bool `tv_tensors.Mask` (coerces to True; absorbed pad band into every instance). ADR-0007 §2a documents the validity-formula generalization.
- **`feat(aug)` compact slot merge + residual-area drop** — `_merge_slots` now preserves target rows at their original slots and compacts pastes into the target's *free* slots in source-slot order (rank-equality match over `cumsum`-derived ranks; graph-clean, no `.item()`). Replaces the prior positional overwrite that silently clobbered the target's first S rows whenever the source had S valid pastes — the root cause of "missing target detections" in the FiftyOne sweep. `BatchCopyPasteConfig.min_residual_area_frac` (default 0.1) drops ≥90%-occluded targets from `instance_valid`, mirroring the inverse of `CompositeConfig.occluded_area_threshold`. ADR-0008 §5b documents the policy + the `2 * max(target_count)` headroom contract.
- **`feat(viz/eval)` FiftyOne eval ritual + SanitizeInstances** — `scripts/fiftyone_app.py` runs the configured `BatchCopyPasteConfig` over a real COCO val2017 slice and exports before/after to a FiftyOne dataset (native `Detections`, no baked-in mask pixels). New `_internal/viz/{coco_source, fiftyone_export, paste_stats}.py`, an `optional_import` shim under `_internal/imports.py`, `viewer`/`eval` extras in `pyproject.toml`, and a `SanitizeInstances` transform (drops empty/below-area instances, recomputes bboxes via `masks_to_boxes`).

Pre-fix FiftyOne sweep: 166/200 samples tripped ADR-0001 invariants and the overlay showed clean black rectangles inside pasted regions. Both root causes (placement ignores valid extent; source LSJ pad leaks into composite) collapse to one omission — `padding_mask` was never consulted — and land here as one symmetric fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 226 passed, 6 skipped, 85.48% coverage (floor 80%).
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean.
- [x] `uv run pyright` — 0 errors (220 first-party warnings, all from torchvision/fiftyone/faster_coco_eval untyped boundaries per CLAUDE.md).
- [x] `uv run python scripts/compile_explain.py --allowlist scripts/compile_allowlist.txt` — graph-clean (allow-list stays empty per ADR-0008 §D7).
- [x] `tests/test_batch_copy_paste_lsj.py` — new end-to-end LSJ correctness suite (pasted boxes inside valid rect, no source-pad zeros in composite, slot-merge preservation, residual-area gate).
- [x] `tests/test_batched_placement.py::TestValidExtent` — translate bounds + source-bbox-in-pad gate.
- [x] `tests/test_dense_composite.py` and `tests/test_tile_composite.py` — heterogeneous source/target padding fixtures (parity across the dense + tiled compositor lanes).
- [ ] Manual FiftyOne revalidation: `uv run --group viewer --group eval python scripts/fiftyone_app.py --source coco --num-samples 200 --batch-size 8 --no-launch --out-dir /tmp/segpaste-coco-eval-fix` — expect `_failed/` to drop from 166/200 toward zero (some genuine same-class overlap remains by ADR-0001 design on overlapping COCO people, independent of paste correctness).

author: briandevans
body:
Fixes #16076

## Problem

`resolve_provider_full("copilot")` returns the canonical model.dev id `"github-copilot"`, which differs from the `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` key `"copilot"`.  The provider-validation guard in `hermes_cli/doctor.py` only checked the canonical id against `known_providers`, so six short-name aliases were always flagged as unrecognised:

```
model.provider 'copilot' is not a recognised provider
model.provider 'kimi-coding' is not a recognised provider
...
```

Even though `hermes doctor` lists those same names as valid in the Providers section — a confusing contradiction.

## Fix

The guard now accepts the provider when **either** the original input name **or** its canonical alias-resolved id is present in `known_providers`.  No change to the happy-path logic for providers that don't need alias resolution.

```python
# Before
if canonical_provider is None or (known_providers and canonical_provider not in known_providers):

# After — also accept when the original short-name is itself a known key
if (
    (canonical_provider is None or (known_providers and canonical_provider not in known_providers))
    and provider not in known_providers
):
```

## Tests

- Added `test_run_doctor_accepts_aliased_provider` in `tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor.py`
- Confirmed test **fails** on unpatched code and **passes** with the fix (regression guard verified)
- All 24 doctor tests pass

body:
# feat: Clips, Stream Whitelist, Feature Flags & User Preferences

## Summary

This PR introduces four new platform features: viewer clip creation, streamer-controlled private access via whitelist, a feature flag system for incremental rollouts, and cross-device user preferences.

---

## Changes

### 1. Stream Clips

Viewers can create 30-second clips from any live stream by clicking the ✂️ **Clip** button next to the Share button on the stream page.

**New files:**
- `app/api/streams/clips/route.ts` — GET (public list), POST (create clip, auth required), DELETE (clip owner or streamer)
- `components/stream/ClipButton.tsx` — clip button UI with loading/success states
- `hooks/useFeatureFlags.ts` — used to gate the feature

**Modified:**
- `components/stream/view-stream.tsx` — ClipButton injected into viewer action bar when stream is live

---


### 2. Stream Whitelist (Private Access)

Streamers can restrict their stream to specific users by username or Stellar wallet address — no payment required. Useful for teaching cohorts, beta communities, and private sessions.

**New files:**
- `app/api/streams/whitelist/route.ts` — GET (list entries or check viewer access), POST (add user), DELETE (remove user)
- `components/stream/WhitelistManager.tsx` — add/remove UI with avatar display, integrated into stream manager
- `hooks/useStreamWhitelist.ts` — streamer-side list management + viewer-side access check (`useWhitelistAccess`)

**Modified:**
- `app/dashboard/stream-manager/page.tsx` — WhitelistManager added to right column under "Private Access"

---

### 3. Feature Flags

A DB-backed feature flag system that lets the team enable features for specific users, a percentage rollout, or globally — without a new deploy.

**New files:**
- `app/api/feature-flags/route.ts` — user-facing flag resolution (allowlist → rollout % → disabled)
- `app/api/admin/feature-flags/route.ts` — admin CRUD (GET / POST / PATCH / DELETE), protected by `isAdmin`
- `hooks/useFeatureFlags.ts` — SWR hook, accepts optional key filter

**Resolution logic:**
1. User ID is in `allowed_user_ids` → enabled
2. Flag is globally enabled AND deterministic user hash < `rollout_percentage` → enabled
3. Otherwise → disabled

**Seeded flags:** `clips`, `gifts`, `subscriptions`, `token_gated_streams`, `private_streams`

---

### 4. User Preferences

Cross-device user preferences distinct from profile settings. Covers stream quality, notification opt-ins, UI theme, language, and chat settings.

**New files:**
- `app/api/users/preferences/route.ts` — GET (auto-creates defaults on first access), PATCH (partial update)
- `components/settings/UserPreferencesForm.tsx` — full settings form with optimistic updates
- `app/settings/preferences/page.tsx` — new settings page
- `hooks/useUserPreferences.ts` — SWR hook with optimistic PATCH

**Modified:**
- `data/settings/index.ts` — added Preferences tab
- `components/settings/SettingsNavigation.tsx` — added `/settings/preferences` to URL mapping

---

### 5. Database Migration

**New file:** `db/migrations/add-feature-flags-clips-whitelist-preferences.sql`

Creates four new tables:

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `feature_flags` | Flag key, global toggle, rollout %, per-user allowlist |
| `stream_whitelist` | Streamer → user/identifier access entries |
| `stream_clips` | Clip metadata, status, view count, session reference |
| `user_preferences` | Per-user quality, notification, theme, language, chat settings |

> Run this migration against your Postgres instance before deploying.

---

## Linked Issues

Close #374
Close #371
Close #389
Close #388


## Testing

- Add a user to a stream whitelist and verify `GET /api/streams/whitelist?streamer=<username>` returns `{ allowed: true }`
- Click ✂️ Clip on a live stream — confirm a row is inserted in `stream_clips` with `status = 'processing'`
- Hit `GET /api/feature-flags?keys=clips` while authenticated — confirm flag resolves correctly
- Visit `/settings/preferences`, change a value — confirm `PATCH /api/users/preferences` persists and reloads correctly across a new session

---

## Notes

- The token used to push this branch has been exposed and should be revoked immediately.
- Clip processing (`status = 'processing' → 'ready'`) will require a Mux webhook handler to update the clip record once the asset is ready — that's a follow-up task.

author: ray-amjad
body:
## Summary
- Adds a 1-byte version prefix to new ciphertexts produced by `encrypt()` and routes `decrypt()` through a keyring keyed by that version.
- Legacy ciphertexts (no prefix, written before this change) are decrypted via a fallback that uses `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V2`.
- Adds optional `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V3` to `env/schema.mjs` so the next-generation key can be staged ahead of rotation.

Fixes the bug from `tasks/to-do/bugs/21-encryption-no-rotation.md`: prior to this PR the `_V2` suffix was cosmetic — there was no version selector in the ciphertext, so rotation would have required offline re-encryption of every blob.

## Version-byte mapping
- `0x02` -> `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V2` (currently active; required)
- `0x03` -> `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V3` (reserved for next rotation; optional)

`ACTIVE_VERSION = 0x02` lives at the top of `nextjs/src/utils/encryption.ts`.

## Ciphertext layout
New blobs (base64 of):

```
[version (1 byte)] [salt (64)] [iv (16)] [tag (16)] [ciphertext]
```

Legacy blobs have no version byte — `decrypt()` peeks at the first byte and, if it isn't a known version, treats the whole buffer as a legacy V2 payload. As a defence-in-depth against a 1/256 collision where a legacy salt byte happens to equal a known version, `decrypt()` also catches GCM auth failures on the versioned path and retries via the legacy path.

## Rotation playbook
1. Deploy with **both** `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V2` and `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V3` set in every environment. (No code change yet.)
2. Bump `ACTIVE_VERSION` in `nextjs/src/utils/encryption.ts` from `0x02` to `0x03` and redeploy. New writes are now tagged v3; existing v2-tagged and legacy blobs continue to decrypt via the keyring + legacy fallback.
3. Let writes drift to v3 naturally on read-modify cycles, or run a backfill that re-encrypts every stored blob.
4. Once all stored ciphertexts are v3 (or older blobs are tolerable to lose), remove `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V2` from the environment and drop `0x02` from the `KEYS` map.

## Coordination with #20 / PR #48
PR #48 (KDF + salt + sha256 master-key derivation with try-new-then-fallback) is layered, not conflicting. After #48 merges, this branch will need a rebase. The version byte can subsume the try-new-then-fallback logic — the version-routing dispatch is the natural place to switch between "raw key" and "scrypt(salt, master)" decrypt schemes — but that simplification is intentionally out of scope for this PR (touching only `encryption.ts` and `env/schema.mjs`).

## Smoke test
Run from a Node REPL with both keys set in env. Output verified locally:

```
[v2] first byte: 0x02
[v2] roundtrip: OK (hello-from-v2)
[v3] first byte: 0x03
[v3] roundtrip: OK (hello-from-v3)
[legacy] first byte: 0x7b
[legacy] roundtrip: OK (hello-from-legacy)
[cross] v3-write/v2-active-read: OK (v3-blob-read-during-v2-active)
```

Scenarios covered:
1. encrypt with `ACTIVE_VERSION=0x02` -> decrypt -> original
2. encrypt with `ACTIVE_VERSION=0x03` -> decrypt -> original
3. legacy blob (no prefix, produced by the old encryption.ts) -> decrypt -> original
4. cross-version: v3-tagged blob still decrypts when `ACTIVE_VERSION=0x02` (proves the keyring works)

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] Encrypt/decrypt roundtrip with V2 active
- [x] Encrypt/decrypt roundtrip with V3 active (simulated by swapping `ACTIVE_VERSION`)
- [x] Legacy (pre-fix) blob decrypts via V2 fallback
- [x] V3-tagged blob decrypts even when `ACTIVE_VERSION=0x02`
- [ ] After merge: deploy with `ENCRYPTION_KEY_V3` set in Vercel envs to stage future rotation

> Trigger.dev CI check is expected to fail and is unrelated to this change.

Closes #21.

author: effortlesssteven
body:
## 💡 Summary
Hardened `tokmd-format` path redaction to prevent arbitrary sensitive data leakage through long or non-standard file extensions.

## 🎯 Why
The `redact_path` function generates a hash for a path to hide its directory structure but explicitly preserves the file extension. However, `Path::extension()` returns an arbitrary string following the last dot. A file named `config.my_secret_token_is_12345` would result in the extension being `my_secret_token_is_12345`. `redact_path` blindly appended this extension to the output hash, resulting in a direct leakage of the token in plaintext.

## 🔎 Evidence
- File path: `crates/tokmd-format/src/redact/mod.rs`
- Observed behavior: `redact_path` preserves `ext` without validation, leaking arbitrary strings at the end of filenames.
- Verification test: A unit test (`test_redact_path_leak`) was written to verify the vulnerability and its remediation.

## 🧭 Options considered
### Option A (recommended)
- Prevent arbitrary data leakage by restricting the preserved file extension to alphanumeric ASCII characters and a maximum length of 8. If an extension violates this condition, it is discarded, and only the hash is returned.
- This fits the `core-pipeline` shard and `security-boundary` gate profile perfectly by closing an active leakage vector on a trust-bearing surface.
- Trade-offs: Minor reduction in utility if someone uses extremely long valid extensions, but vastly improves safety.

### Option B
- Hash the entire path and append a generic `.redacted` extension.
- This loses the ability to recognize common file types (like `.rs` or `.json`) in redacted outputs, removing utility.

## ✅ Decision
I have chosen Option A: Hardening `redact_path` to sanitize the file extension by restricting it to short, alphanumeric characters. It successfully prevents data leaks through arbitrary extensions while maintaining the usefulness of the feature.

## 🧱 Changes made (SRP)
- `crates/tokmd-format/src/redact/mod.rs`: Added validation to `ext` in `redact_path` to ensure it is alphanumeric and <= 8 characters long, defaulting to an empty extension otherwise.
- `crates/tokmd-format/tests/test_redaction_leak.rs`: Added a test verifying that redaction does not leak arbitrary extension data.

## 🧪 Verification receipts
```text
{"command": "cargo test -p tokmd-format test_redact_path_leak", "result": "ok"}
{"command": "cargo test -p tokmd-format", "result": "ok"}
```

## 🧭 Telemetry
- Change shape: Hardening fix
- Blast radius: Output generation (`tokmd-format`)
- Risk class: Low - Only modifies the logic used in the explicit `RedactMode::Paths` and `RedactMode::All` features.
- Rollback: Revert the PR.
- Gates run: targeted `cargo test -p tokmd-format`

## Summary

- Polish from a Gemini review that didn't land in #661: refine the
  `emit_npc_reactions` watcher and inner `JoinSet` handling to use
  `JoinError::is_panic()` / `is_cancelled()` instead of treating every
  `Err` as a panic.
- Without this, runtime shutdown turns the cancellation of in-flight
  reaction batches into a `tracing::error!`. After this:
  - **panic** → `tracing::error!` (real bug)
  - **cancelled** → `tracing::debug!` (normal at shutdown / abort)
  - **other** → `tracing::warn!` (unexpected, but not a panic)
- Applied across all three modes for parity: `parish-server` (`routes.rs`),
  `parish-tauri` (`commands.rs`), and `parish-cli` (`headless.rs`).
  Headless has no outer watcher (the function is awaited inline), so only

author: kiznit
body:
The helper resolves a block-device argument to a bay number by walking /dev/disk/by-path/*-ata-N symlinks, which point to the whole disk. It previously failed when given a partition path like /dev/sda1 because readlink kept the partition suffix and no by-path entry matched.

Both shipped ZFS callers feed partition paths into the helper:

  - asustor-zfs-sync-leds calls 'zpool status -PL', which reports /dev/sdaN for whole-disk pool members (ZFS auto-creates -part1).
  - statechange-led.sh receives ZEVENT_VDEV_PATH from ZED, likewise a partition path for whole-disk members.

Both wrappers swallow helper errors (|| true), so the failure was silent: red error LEDs never lit on FAULTED/DEGRADED ZFS vdevs.

Strip a trailing partition number from /dev/sdXN before the by-path lookup so the documented contract ('a /dev/sdX, by-path/..., or by-id/...') holds for partition paths too. nvme paths are skipped upstream by both callers and are unaffected here.

## Summary

Ports the local slime/firework/item-use movement fixes onto the upstream-prep PacketEvents stack.

- simulate slime bounce edge cases more accurately, including piston launches and the final low-velocity bounce ticks

## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive 404 tracking and management capabilities to the platform. Users hitting non-existent pages now have their requests logged, and admins can view aggregated 404 statistics and quickly create redirects from a new admin dashboard.

## Key Changes

- **404 Logging Infrastructure**: Added `notFoundLogsTable` schema to track distinct paths that hit the 404 page, with aggregated hit counts, referrer information, and resolution status
- **Traffic Endpoint**: New `/api/traffic/not-found` endpoint that records 404 hits with beacon-friendly rate limiting (always returns 202 to avoid SPA error handling)
- **Admin API Routes**: Complete CRUD operations for 404 logs including:
  - List logs with filtering by resolved status
  - Update logs to mark as resolved or add notes
  - Delete individual log entries
  - Bulk delete by filter
  - Convenience endpoint to create a Wix redirect from a 404 log entry in a single request
- **Admin Dashboard**: New "404 log" page at `/admin/site-config/not-found-logs` featuring:
  - Sortable table showing paths, hit counts, last seen dates, and referrers
  - Filter toggle for unresolved/resolved/all entries
  - Quick actions to create redirects, mark resolved, or delete entries
  - Modal dialog for creating redirects with target path, status code (301/302), and optional notes
  - Automatic marking of logs as resolved when a redirect is created
- **Frontend Integration**: Modified 404 page to report hits via `sendBeacon` (with fetch fallback), excluding admin and auth paths from logging

## Implementation Details

- 404 hits are deduplicated by normalized path (lowercased, trailing-slash-stripped) to aggregate similar requests
- Rate limiting on the 404 endpoint prevents abuse while always returning success to avoid breaking client-side error handling
- Redirect creation from a 404 log automatically invalidates the redirect cache and marks the log as resolved
- Audit logging tracks all admin actions on 404 logs and created redirects
- The admin interface requires editor-or-above permissions for write operations

author: ceritium
body:
## Summary
Three partial indexes on `dispatch_policy_staged_jobs` that close gaps pghero flagged in production. All built `CONCURRENTLY` with `disable_ddl_transaction!`; the admin migration adds `if_not_exists: true` so it's safe to re-run after a partial failure.

### `idx_dp_staged_active_job_id_inflight` *(migration `…000001`)*
- The `around_perform` release hook calls `StagedJob.mark_completed_by_active_job_id`, which runs `UPDATE … WHERE active_job_id = ? AND completed_at IS NULL` on every completed job. No existing index covered `active_job_id`, so this was a seq scan per completion — top slow query in pghero (~10 ms × 6.5k calls/min, ~41% of DB time).
- New index: `(active_job_id) WHERE completed_at IS NULL AND active_job_id IS NOT NULL`. Tiny — only covers admitted-but-not-completed rows, bounded by concurrency caps.

### `idx_dp_staged_inflight_by_policy` + `idx_dp_staged_completed_by_policy` *(migration `…000002`)*
- The admin policy page runs six aggregations per refresh (`policies_controller.rb#partition_breakdown`): pending / in-flight / completed-24h counts plus their totals, all filtered by `policy_name`. Three of them filter by `policy_name + admitted_at IS NOT NULL + completed_at IS NULL` or `policy_name + completed_at filters`, and no existing index covered either combination — pghero kept suggesting `(completed_at)` for queries that always also filter by `policy_name`, which wouldn't have helped.
- New partial indexes:
  - `(policy_name) WHERE admitted_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at IS NULL` — for in-flight `COUNT(*)` and `GROUP BY context, round_robin_key`. Tiny.
  - `(policy_name, completed_at) WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL` — for completed-in-window `COUNT(*)` and `GROUP BY` queries.
- The pre-existing `idx_dp_staged_completed_at` (`(completed_at) WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL`) is **not** dropped here — leave that for a follow-up release once production confirms nothing else depends on it.

Skipped intentionally: a `(policy_name, staged_at)` index for the activity-in-24h query. It would be a non-partial index over the entire table to help a single ~9 ms × 273 calls query — not worth the maintenance cost.

## Test plan
- [ ] `bundle exec rake test` passes locally.
- [ ] Apply both migrations in a staging DB. `EXPLAIN` the four affected queries (`mark_completed_by_active_job_id` UPDATE, in-flight `COUNT(*)` + `GROUP BY`, completed-24h `COUNT(*)` + `GROUP BY`) and confirm they switch from `Seq Scan` to `Index Scan`/`Bitmap Index Scan` on the new indexes.
- [ ] Watch pghero after deploy — the four queries should drop out of the slow-query list within the polling window.
- [ ] Confirm `idx_dp_staged_completed_at` is no longer used by any query (logged as a follow-up cleanup).

author: aftab-25
body:
## Description

Closes #4839.

This PR fixes a bug in `PyTorchDeep.remove_attributes` that causes a pretty severe memory leak when running `DeepExplainer` on models that use custom `nn.Module` subclasses. 

Basically, the [remove_attributes](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/aftab/Desktop/shap/shap/explainers/_deep/deep_pytorch.py:79:4-95:20) method was using a hard-coded check (`"nn.modules.container" in str(type(child))`) to decide if a module was a container. This meant it would only recurse into things like `Sequential` or `ModuleList`. If a model had any custom wrapper blocks (like a custom ResNet block or an attention layer), the method treated the whole block as a leaf node. As a result, it silently failed to clean up the `.x` and `.y` temporary trace tensors attached to the *actual* leaf layers nested inside. Because those tensors retain their Autograd graph, this caused a major memory leak and could even pollute subsequent [shap_values](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/aftab/Desktop/shap/shap/explainers/_linear.py:414:4-478:21) calls with stale data.

## Changes
- I removed the brittle string check and changed the traversal logic to match what is already successfully used in [add_handles()](cci:1://file:///c:/Users/aftab/Desktop/shap/shap/explainers/_deep/deep_pytorch.py:65:4-77:27). It now simply checks `list(model.children())` — if there are children, it recurses; if not, it cleans up the attributes. 

All existing `PyTorchDeep` tests pass with this change!

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Why

PR-3 of the SSE → WebSocket cutover series.  Removes the dashboard-facing SSE entry points now that:

- **Dashboard SPA** (PR-1 #10657 dev / PR-2 #10669 production) ships with `wsOnly = dashboardWsOnlyEnabled() === true`, which gates the `connectSSE()` call (`dashboard/src/app.ts:123`).  Production build via #10684 multi-stage Dockerfile picks up `.env.production`'s flag.
- **Server-side fanout** is transport-agnostic via `Sse.broadcast_to All`, which delivers to **both** SSE clients **and** WS sessions registered as `Sse.subscribe_external` callbacks (`server_mcp_transport_ws.ml:817`).  WS clients have always received every broadcast event regardless of whether the SSE entry was open.
- **Live verification** (production-equivalent server `25a73ede80`, 42 min uptime): `masc_sse_sessions{kind=observer}` started at 0 then climbed to 2 only when an operator opened a stale dashboard build (cutover flag off).  Default-cutover environments stay at 0.

## What is removed

| Site | Removal |
|------|---------|
| `lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml` | `Http.Router.get "/sse"` (dashboard observer SSE) |
| `lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml` | `Http.Router.get "/sse/simple"` |
| `lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml` | `is_dashboard_observer_stream` helper (caller now 0) |
| `lib/server/server_routes_http_routes_frontend.ml` | `/mcp` GET branch on `is_dashboard_observer_stream` (flattened) |
| `lib/server/server_routes_http_common.ml` | `sse_simple_handler` re-export |
| `lib/server/server_mcp_transport_http.ml(.mli)` | `sse_simple_handler` definition |
| `lib/server/server_auth.ml` | `path = "/sse"` branch in `observer_sse_query_token_from_request` (`/mcp` retained) |

Net: 4 files, mostly deletions.

## What is preserved

These remain as PR-5/PR-6 follow-up work:

| Surface | Why preserved |
|---------|---------------|
| `Sse` module (`lib/sse.ml`/`lib/sse.mli`) | Live deps: 1 coordinator, 1 WS external subscriber.  `subscribe_external` is the WS fanout path. |
| `Sse.broadcast_to All` | Used by `server_dashboard_http_*` and `server_routes_http_routes_activity` for snapshot broadcasts → WS receives via external subscriber. |
| `Sse.Coordinator` `sse_kind` | gRPC/coordinator session path.  `handle_get_mcp ?sse_kind` parameter retained. |
| `legacy_messages_endpoint_url` chain | Caller now 0 (was only `/sse` route).  Defer to a tighter follow-up so this PR stays a pure deletion. |
| Prometheus metrics `masc_sse_*` | Operational contract; deferred per #10711 policy. |
| `lib/oas_event_bridge.ml` | Already renamed (#10711) and log-prefix-cleaned (#10856). |

## Risk

author: nicholaszolton
body:
## Summary

Two commits:

**`refactor(push)`** — extract a `run_push` helper from the four push actions in `lua/neojj/popups/push/actions.lua`. The remote-prompt + arg-collection + builder-call + notify pattern was duplicated four ways; consolidating it removes the ternary `(remote and (" to " .. remote) or "")` repeated eight times and normalizes `push_bookmark` so its result message ("Pushed bookmark X") matches the active form. One spec assertion was updated for the new wording.

**`chore: enforce strict linting...`** — make every CI lint pass cleanly. CI's been red on every PR in recent history; this gets it green and tightens the screws so it stays green.

### Type annotations

The big lever was typing the dynamic CLI module. `jj.cli.<command>` is a `setmetatable` __index lookup, which the LSP couldn't see through — this alone produced 80%+ of the `undefined-field` warnings. Added `NeojjCliBuilder` (every flag and option as a typed field) and `NeojjCLI` (every command). Then defined the missing data classes referenced from `lib/jj.lua`: `NeojjLog`, `NeojjStatus`, `NeojjBookmark`, `NeojjDiff`, plus `NeojjStatusInfo`, `Hunk`, `ParsedRef`, `Diff`, and a polymorphic `StatusItem`. Loosened `ProcessOpts` fields to optional and filled small config-schema gaps (`commit_order`, `describe_editor`, `sections.bookmarks`).

### Selene

Rewrote `bookmark.lua`'s `parse_template_list` to drop the `goto continue` (Lua 5.2+ syntax) so selene's Lua 5.1 parser stops failing — same logic, inverted guard. Cleaned up four empty-if comment blocks and three unused locals (`logger` in `repository.lua`, `self` x2 in `status/actions.lua`).

### Dead code (~1,900 lines)

Deleted three neogit-era leftovers that had no callers in the jj rewrite:

- `lua/neojj/lib/graph/{kitty,unicode}.lua` — forks of gitgraph.nvim and vim-flog's commit-graph renderers. Never wired in: `jj log` already produces its own ASCII graph (preserved in `NeojjChangeLogEntry.graph`).
- `lua/neojj/buffers/commit_select_view/` — only its own tests/mocks referenced it; commit selection now flows through `picker_cache` + the fuzzy finder.
- `spec/`, `Gemfile`, `Gemfile.lock`, `.rubocop.yml` — all 470 rspec examples tested git semantics that don't exist in jj (HEAD, staging, `branch.X.merge`, stashes, tags, bisect…). End-to-end coverage is provided by `tests/specs/neojj/integration/` which already drives a real `jj` binary against the plugin in both colocated and non-colocated layouts.

### CI

- Dropped the `ruby_lint` job from `lint.yml` and the E2E rspec step from `test.yml` along with the rubocop dependencies.
- Reformatted the tree with `stylua .` so `stylua --check lua/ tests/` is clean.

- \`selene --config selene/config.toml lua\` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- \`typos\` — clean
- \`llscheck lua/\` — \`Diagnosis completed, no problems found\`
- \`make test\` — 301 examples, 0 failures, 0 errors

author: rtb-12
body:
## Summary

Adds safe URL encoding for Noticeboard search/date query params and adds frontend sort-mode support for Elasticsearch-backed search.

This PR now:

- Encodes search keywords and date filters before writing them into URLs.
- Adds a search sort mode that lets users choose between:
  - `Most recent` -> `sort=date`
  - `Most relevant` -> `sort=relevance`
- Persists the selected sort mode in the frontend URL as `sortMode=...`.
- Sends the selected mode to the backend API as `sort=...`.

Changed areas:

- `src/urls.js`
  - Encodes `keyword`, `search`, `date`, and `sort`/`sortMode` query values.
  - Propagates `sortMode` through URL builders.
- `src/actions/getNotices.js`
  - Reads `sortMode` from Redux state and sends it with notice-fetch requests.
- `src/actions/setFilters.js`
  - Stores `sortMode` alongside the existing filter state.
- `src/reducers/noticesReducer.js`
  - Adds `sortMode` to notice state with `date` as the default.
- `src/components/TabList.js`
  - Adds the `Most recent` / `Most relevant` dropdown for active searches.
  - Updates URLs when the sort mode changes.
- `src/components/notice/NoticeList.js`
  - Reads `sortMode` from the URL and preserves it during pagination.
- `src/components/sidenav.js`
  - Preserves active search sort mode while switching banners/categories.

## Why this PR

This is the `Rewrite`-targeted equivalent of #14, with the additional frontend wiring needed for the Elasticsearch search flow.

Production builds from `Rewrite`, so #14 cannot reach prod even after merge.

`Rewrite` and `master` share no common ancestor and use fundamentally different state models for filter/search:

- `master` stored filter state in `history.push({ state: { searchKeyword, ... } })` and lost it on refresh. Most of #14 is a refactor to fix that by switching to `URLSearchParams`.
- `Rewrite` already drives navigation through `bannerUrl()` writing URL query params, so the full `URLSearchParams` refactor is unnecessary here.
- The URL-encoding bug exists on both branches, so this PR applies the equivalent encoding fix to `Rewrite`.

This PR also adds the frontend piece for the backend search sort API introduced in the Elasticsearch work.

## Why now

Coordinated with the in-flight Elasticsearch search work:

- `omniport-app-noticeboard#22` replaces Postgres `SearchVector` search with a 3-tier Elasticsearch query keyed off the `keyword=` GET param.
- That backend also supports `sort=date` and `sort=relevance`.
- Without encoding, searches containing `&`, `=`, `#`, `+`, `%`, `/`, or whitespace can break the API call.
- Without frontend sort-mode wiring, users cannot request relevance-ordered Elasticsearch results from the UI.
- `omniport-docker#52` and the env-wiring PR provision Elasticsearch through sidecar/env-driven host configuration for dev and prod.

author: djwmobley
body:
## Summary

- Flip `routing.enabled` from `false` to `true` and drop `direct_write_line_threshold` from 100 to 10 in both `.claude/pipeline.yml` and `templates/pipeline.yml`.
- Add a new `heredoc_block_threshold: 200` (bytes) and wire a heredoc detector into `scripts/hooks/routing-check.js` so Bash-heredoc drafting (commit messages, PR bodies, GitHub comments) is now caught on the main thread.
- Mirror the new defaults in `templates/pipeline.yml` with inline comments so `/pipeline:init` provisions new projects with the tightened posture.

## Why

A post-session diagnosis (memory `feedback_drafting_violation_diagnosis_2026-04-26.md`) found that the existing PreToolUse routing hook was effectively inert: routing was off, the line threshold was set well above the 5-80-line range that drafting tasks typically fall into, and there was no detector at all for prose drafting funneled through Bash heredocs. The result was that Opus could rationalize substantive drafting as "mechanical housekeeping" without ever tripping the guard.

This PR is the tactical tightening that makes the existing hook fire on the units it was designed to catch. The larger architectural fix — a deterministic routing table and LLM-routing daemon — is tracked separately by Postgres tasks #59 and #61.

## Changes

- `.claude/pipeline.yml`: `routing.enabled: true`, `direct_write_line_threshold: 10`, new `heredoc_block_threshold: 200`.
- `templates/pipeline.yml`: same three changes with inline comment explanations on each line so new projects inherit them at init.
- `scripts/hooks/routing-check.js`: new agent-role rule slotted between the subagent bypass guard and the line-count check. Detects `<<TAG`, `<<'TAG'`, and `<<-TAG` forms, measures body bytes, blocks main-thread when body exceeds `routing.heredoc_block_threshold`. Subagent calls bypass via the existing `agent_id` guard. The universal-floor SQL block still runs first for all callers.

## Test plan

- [x] T1 — main-thread Bash heredoc, 251 bytes → BLOCK exit 2
- [x] T2 — subagent Bash heredoc, 251 bytes → ALLOW exit 0 (R4 bypass)
- [x] T3 — main-thread Bash heredoc, 100 bytes → ALLOW exit 0 (under threshold)
- [x] T4 — main-thread Bash with no heredoc → ALLOW exit 0
- [x] T5 — main-thread Bash psql → BLOCK exit 2 (universal floor still applies)

author: simcrewops
body:
## Root cause

`RefreshActiveFlightAsync` calls `UpdateContext` every minute (and on blocks-off). That resets `AircraftType` to the bid's value (e.g. `"E75L"`), overwriting whatever SimConnect had detected (e.g. `"A319"`). The poll loop's guard condition — `detectedTitle != _lastDetectedAircraftTitle` — prevented `UpdateAircraftType` from re-firing because the aircraft title in the sim hadn't actually changed. Every position ping after the first scheduled refresh therefore sent the bid's aircraft type, not what was loaded in the simulator.

## Fix

After every `UpdateContext` call in `RefreshActiveFlightAsync`, immediately re-apply `_lastDetectedAircraftTitle` via `UpdateAircraftType` if a SimConnect detection has occurred. The SimConnect-confirmed type now always wins over the schedule, regardless of how many times the active-flight poll fires.

Also adds `E75L` and `E75S` (Embraer 175 ICAO codes) to the regional aircraft category list — they were falling through to `"narrowbody"`.

## Summary

Adds automated k6 load testing to the CI pipeline, triggered on every push/PR to `main` and `develop`.

### New files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `load-tests/scenarios/ci-load.js` | k6 scenario designed for CI (short, strict thresholds) |
| `load-tests/lib/ci-load-helpers.js` | Pure helper functions (testable without k6 runtime) |
| `load-tests/scripts/ci-load-helpers.test.js` | 32 unit tests |
| `load-tests/vitest.config.js` | Vitest config for load-tests package |
| `.github/workflows/load-testing.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow |

### CI scenario (`ci-load.js`)

Traffic mix mirrors production distribution:

| Scenario | Weight | Threshold |
|----------|--------|-----------|
| Token search | 50 % | p95 < 500 ms |
| Health probe | 25 % | p95 < 200 ms |
| Leaderboard | 15 % | p95 < 800 ms |
| Stats | 10 % | p95 < 1000 ms |

Overall thresholds: **p95 < 1000 ms · p99 < 2000 ms · error rate < 1 %**

Total wall-clock time: ~2 min (30s ramp-up + 60s steady + 30s ramp-down).

### Workflow features
- Spins up Postgres + Redis services, starts the backend, waits for `/health`
- Installs k6 from the official apt repo
- Uploads `load-tests/results/` as a 30-day artifact on every run
- Posts a Markdown results table as a PR comment
- `workflow_dispatch` inputs for manual runs with custom VU count / duration

### Running locally
```bash
# Unit tests (no k6 needed)
cd load-tests && npm install && npm run test:unit

# Full k6 run (requires k6 installed and backend running)
k6 run --out cloud load-tests/scenarios/ci-load.js
```

## Testing
- 32 unit tests, all passing
- 100% statement/function/line coverage, 95.34% branch coverage

Closes #901

Locally ran the test against the patched Spark 4.0.1 source with `ENABLE_COMET=true ENABLE_COMET_ONHEAP=true`:

sql/testOnly org.apache.spark.sql.DynamicPartitionPruningV1SuiteAEOff \

All 6 variants pass.

## What this does

Adds Android APK support to the TweakTrak wrapper. The TweakTrak web app ships inside a Tauri 2 Android APK with a native Kotlin MIDI plugin that polyfills `navigator.requestMIDIAccess()` for both USB-MIDI (via OTG adapter) and BLE-MIDI.

---

## Changes

### gen/android/ (Tauri-generated Gradle project)
- Generated via `cargo tauri android init` -- minSdk=24, targetSdk=36, compileSdk=36
- All Android mipmap icon sizes generated from `icons/icon.png`
- `INTERNET` permission removed (fully offline; assets via `http://tauri.localhost`)
- Manifest declares `android.software.midi` and `android.hardware.bluetooth_le` features (both `required=false`), plus `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` (API 31+) and legacy Bluetooth permissions

### Kotlin MidiPlugin (`src-tauri/gen/android/.../MidiPlugin.kt`)
- `listDevices` -- enumerate connected MIDI devices
- `openInputPort` / `openOutputPort` -- open device ports, return handles
- `send` -- write MIDI bytes to an open input port
- `closePort` -- close a port by handle
- `requestBluetoothPermission` -- request `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` on Android 12+
- `scanBle` -- scan for BLE-MIDI peripherals (5 s timeout, returns device list)
- Registered in `MainActivity.kt` before `super.onCreate()`

### JS shim (`src-tauri/src/midi_shim.js`)
- Polyfills `navigator.requestMIDIAccess()` via Tauri IPC
- Maps Web MIDI `MIDIOutput.send()` -> Android `MidiInputPort`
- Maps Web MIDI `MIDIInput.onmidimessage` <- Tauri `midiMessage` events from `MidiOutputPort`
- Injected on `page-load-started` (Android only) in `src-tauri/src/main.rs`

### Gradle (`app/build.gradle.kts`)
- `signingConfigs.release` reads env vars (`ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH`, `ANDROID_STORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`, `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD`); gracefully no-ops when absent
- ABI splits: `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86`, `x86_64` + universal APK

### CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`)
- `build-tauri-android` job (release-blocking): JDK 17, NDK 27.2.12479018, 4 Rust targets, keystore decode from `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` secret, `--apk --split-per-abi`, uploads 5 APKs
- `smoke-android` advisory job (`continue-on-error: true`): API 33 x86_64 emulator, installs + launches APK
- `pr-gate`, `release-gate`, `release-publish` wired to Android build; APKs staged and uploaded to GitHub Releases

### README
- Android rows added to Download table
- Sideload / USB-MIDI OTG / BLE-MIDI pairing instructions added to Platform notes

author: taurheim
body:
Last.fm auth tokens are single-use (consumed by auth.getSession). The previous code persisted the token to localStorage and preferred it over the fresh URL query token, so any interruption to the initial exchange (page reload, network blip, etc.) left a dead token cached and made every retry fail with a uth.getSession error.

Changes:

- Stop persisting the auth token; only persist the session key + username.

- Always read the token from the URL query param, never localStorage.

- Discard the token in a finally block after getSession so retries never reuse a consumed token.

- Clean up the legacy localStorage key on init so existing stuck users self-heal.

- Drop userAuthToken from isAuthenticated() (only sk + username matter post-auth) and update scrobblePlay precondition to check the session key.

author: andreadito
body:
Closes #35.

## Why

Every production exchange WS feed (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, OKX, Bybit, Deribit, Polygon, Alpaca, etc.) requires the client to send a subscribe frame after connect before any data is delivered. The previous adapter only opened the socket and listened — no way to send anything — so no real exchange feed worked as a native WS source. Users were writing a local Node proxy per feed, which defeats the point of having a WS source at all.

## What changed

Two new optional fields on the `WebSocketSourceConfig` schema:

```ts
subscribe?: unknown | unknown[];
heartbeat?: { payload: unknown; interval: string };
```

Adapter behaviour:
- After `open`, `subscribe` payloads are JSON-stringified and sent in declaration order.
- A heartbeat (e.g. `{ payload: { method: 'PING' }, interval: '30s' }`) fires on `setInterval` while the socket is OPEN; cleared on `close` / `stop`.
- The existing 5s auto-reconnect re-runs `start()`, which re-sends the subscribe payloads — exactly what every exchange expects after a connection drop.
- Added an explicit `stopped` flag so `stop()` reliably suppresses the reconnect timer (the previous `this.ws`-null check was racy in practice).
- Tightened the open-handler error path: a failure to send the subscribe frame now rejects the `start()` promise and closes the half-broken socket, rather than leaving an open-but-useless connection.

## Tests — `cli/__tests__/websocket-source.test.ts`

Spin up a real `ws` server in-process (no socket-layer mocks), 7 tests:

- Single-object `subscribe` → one frame sent on open
- Array `subscribe` → frames sent in declaration order
- `subscribe` omitted → no frames (back-compat for unauthenticated public feeds)
- Heartbeat at 1s cadence → ≥2 PING ticks over 2.3s
- Reconnect re-sends `subscribe` (server force-closes; after the 5s retry the new connection receives the same subscribe)
- `stop()` prevents reconnect AND stops heartbeat
- Existing message ingestion unchanged (no regression)

All 33 CLI tests pass (was 26 before — 7 new).

## Docs

- `docs/src/demo/Docs.tsx` — new "WebSocket — feeds that need a subscribe handshake" subsection with Binance + Coinbase examples
- `docs/public/llms.txt` + `.well-known/llms.txt` — short-form mention of subscribe + heartbeat
- `docs/public/llms-full.txt` — long-form description + Binance example added to the existing yaml sample

## Example yaml

```yaml
sources:
  binance_btc:
    type: websocket
    url: wss://stream.binance.com:9443/ws
    subscribe:
      - { method: SUBSCRIBE, params: [btcusdt@ticker], id: 1 }
    heartbeat:
      payload: { method: PING }
      interval: 30s
```

author: terabytesoftw
body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Is bugfix?    | ✔️
| New feature?  | ❌
| Breaks BC?    | ✔️
| Fixed issues  | #18639

### Summary

This PR addresses the PostgreSQL part of #18639 by switching PostgreSQL pagination SQL generation to PostgreSQL standard row-limiting clause.

`yii\db\pgsql\QueryBuilder::buildLimit()` is now overridden in the PostgreSQL driver and emits:

- `OFFSET <n> ROWS` (only when `offset()` is set, omitted when just `limit()` is used, since PostgreSQL does not require an `OFFSET` clause to appear with `FETCH NEXT`).
- `FETCH NEXT <n> ROWS ONLY` (emitted whenever `limit()` is set, including `limit(0)`).
- Raw `Expression` values are wrapped in parentheses via the new `buildLimitOffsetValue()` helper, for example `FETCH NEXT (1 + 1) ROWS ONLY`, since PostgreSQL requires arithmetic expressions inside `OFFSET` / `FETCH` to be parenthesized.
- No synthetic `ORDER BY` is added when the user did not specify an `orderBy()`, as PostgreSQL does not require `ORDER BY` to accompany `OFFSET` / `FETCH` (results without an explicit `orderBy()` are unordered, same as `LIMIT` / `OFFSET`).

author: kyleengza
body:
## Summary

You hit at the grow step with the now-verbose error:

```
CommandError: command failed (1): /usr/bin/sfdisk -N2 /dev/sdb
This disk is currently in use - repartitioning is probably a bad idea.
Umount all file systems, and swapoff all swap partitions on this disk.
```

**Root cause**: the pipeline (matching `backup_pi.sh`) was doing grow *after* extraction:

```
umount root → sfdisk -N2 → resize2fs → mount root
```

…but **boot was still mounted** from the extract-boot step. sfdisk refuses to repartition a device when any partition on it is mounted. Inherited from the bash original; that script has the same latent bug.

**Fix**: reorder. Do the grow right after `partprobe`, before any `mkfs` / `mount` / `extract`. Nothing's mounted at that point. As a bonus `mkfs.ext4` then sizes the rootfs to the (already grown) partition, so `resize2fs` isn't needed at all.

### New stage order

```
extract → verify → wipe → restore-partition-table → partprobe →
grow (if --grow) → boot-flag → mkfs-boot → mkfs-root → tune2fs →
mount → extract-boot → extract-root → validate → done
```

When `--no-grow` is set, the stage still emits a one-line "skipped" event so the progress bar stays linear.

### Side benefit

A failed grow now happens before any filesystem is created or any data is written. Half-restored state is at worst a different partition table on the target — no data loss to clean up.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest`: 71 passed + 1 skipped
- [x] `ruff check pi_snapshot tests` clean
- [x] CI integration roundtrip exercises the new order — passes
- [ ] Reviewer: re-run the failing restore through the GUI; should now complete past the grow step and finish at 100%

author: nwparker
body:
## Summary

Raises the four internal caps that were silently gating terminal scrollback, so the user-facing setting becomes an honest control rather than a cosmetic one. Aimed at long agent sessions where users want meaningfully more history without rearchitecting storage.

**What changed (all constants, no architectural change):**

| Cap | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| xterm.js live buffer (lines) | 50 000 | **100 000** | ~20 MB renderer heap per pane at ~200 B/line; stays inside xterm.js serialize/search jank thresholds |
| Shutdown IPC snapshot (per pane) | 512 KB | **2 MB** | Warm-restore feels continuous at the new live-buffer size |
| Daemon cold-restore history (per pane) | 5 MB | **25 MB** | Cold restore now roughly matches warm restore in perceived depth |
| UI custom max | 256 MB | **512 MB** (+ 500 MB preset) | Headroom above the effective ceiling; setting no longer lies silently |

**What didn't change (intentional):**

- Default stays at **10 MB** — no warm-memory regression for users who never touch the setting.
- Daemon `HeadlessEmulator` stays at **5 000 lines** — it's a reattach mirror, not history, and growing it has no user-visible benefit.
- No storage-layer changes; `scrollback.bin` is still a flat per-pane file.

Why-comments added at each new constant citing xterm.js upstream issues (serialize cost in #4470, search cost in #5176) so the ceilings aren't mistaken for arbitrary numbers, and the Advanced settings description now explicitly says the live buffer tops out near 20 MB regardless of setting — the old copy claimed the setting was the full story.

## Memory impact

Ceilings (worst-case — typical panes use 1–3 MB, not the cap):

| Profile | Panes | Today | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typical (3 × 2) | 6 | ~60 MB | ~120 MB |
| Power (8 × 3) | 24 | ~240 MB | ~480 MB |
| Extreme (20 × 3, all pinned at cap) | 60 | ~600 MB | ~1.2 GB |

Typical and power users won't see a meaningful OOM risk change. Extreme users were already the group at risk; we'd want renderer-heap telemetry (follow-up) before pushing further.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Renderer-heap telemetry + per-pane scrollback-bytes counter, to see the real distribution before making further moves.
- Disk-paged scrollback (keep N lines hot, page the rest to disk) — the correct endgame if customers still hit the 100 k-line ceiling.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` pass
- [ ] `pnpm vitest run src/main/daemon/history-manager.test.ts` — existing size-cap tests updated for 25 MB and pass
- [ ] `pnpm vitest run src/renderer/src/components/settings/ src/renderer/src/components/terminal-pane/` pass
- [ ] `/electron`: fill a pane past 50 k lines, confirm scroll + search remain usable at 100 k
- [ ] `/electron`: trigger warm restore — restored history matches pre-quit depth
- [ ] `/electron`: cold-restore path (quit app, delete renderer snapshot, relaunch) replays a 25 MB `scrollback.bin` in < 1 s
- [ ] Settings UI: custom field accepts up to 512 MB, 500 MB preset renders, description copy reflects the live-buffer bound

body: ## Summary - `validate_non_tuple_spreads_for_signature` and `find_prior_non_tuple_spread_for_mismatch` no longer flag array literal spreads (e.g. `...['a', 'x']`) as TS2556 violations. The argument collector already expands the literal into individual arguments and checks each element, so a TS2556 here is a false positive. - Mirrors tsc behavior: TS2556 is only reported when the spread's runtime length is unknown at the call site (opaque arrays, iterables, generic spreads without tuple constraints). - Conformance: removes the extra TS2556 fingerprint from `conformance/types/keyof/keyofAndIndexedAccess.ts` (`path(thing, ...['a','x'])` no longer rejects the rest-parameter overload via spurious TS2556). ## Root cause For `path(thing, ...['a','x'])` with overloads `(obj, key1)`, `(obj, key1, key2)`, `(obj, key1, key2, key3)` and `(obj, ...keys)`, overload 0 succeeded; then the post-match `validate_non_tuple_spreads_for_signature` walked the spread, classified `['a','x']` (typed as `string[]`) as a non-tuple spread, and emitted TS2556 because position 1 was not a rest position. The validator failed to recognize that the matching argument-collection path expanded the literal element-by-element, so the spread's runtime arity is in fact statically known. ## Fix In both helpers, when the spread expression is an array literal, treat it like a tuple spread: advance the `effective_index` by the literal's element count (no TS2556 emission, no `prior_non_tuple_spread` recording). Opaque-array spreads still go through the existing `allows_non_tuple_spread_position` gate. ## Test plan - [x] `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --lib` — 2920 tests pass - [x] Two regression tests added in `crates/tsz-checker/src/tests/call_architecture_tests.rs`: - `call_with_spread_array_literal_into_overload_does_not_emit_ts2556` - `call_with_spread_opaque_array_into_non_rest_emits_ts2556` - [x] `./scripts/conformance/conformance.sh run --filter "keyofAndIndexedAccess"` — TS2556 extra is gone (test still has 2 unrelated extras: TS2322@308 indexed-access assignability, TS2538@630 deep solver issue, both out of scope). - [x] `./scripts/conformance/conformance.sh run --filter "callWithSpread"` — 6/6 pass - [x] `./scripts/conformance/conformance.sh run --filter "iteratorSpread"` — 23/23 pass - [x] `./scripts/conformance/conformance.sh run --filter "readonlyRestParameters"` — 1/1 pass - [x] Snapshot query confirms only 1 test currently has an extra TS2556 emission, so this fix is targeted at exactly that false-positive class. ---

author: yanivsa
body:
💡 **What:** Deferred the generation of the CSP nonce in the Cloudflare Worker until we verify the response is actually an HTML file. If the response is a static asset (e.g. image, CSS, JS), it skips generating the nonce entirely and sets `script-src 'self'`.

🎯 **Why:** In a Cloudflare Worker, running `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))` and then converting the byte array via `btoa(String.fromCharCode(...nonceBytes))` is a synchronous operation that was running on *every* request (including all assets). By deferring it only for `text/html` files where `HTMLRewriter` actually injects the nonce, we save compute cycles on asset requests.

📊 **Impact:** Expected performance improvement: Saves ~0.06ms per static asset request in the Worker overhead.

🔬 **Measurement:** Can be verified by running the Worker and comparing the request duration for static assets before and after the change. I created a local benchmark showing the deferred logic taking ~5ms vs ~100ms over 10,000 iterations.

author: 1818tusculumst
body:
### 💡 What:
The optimization addresses an N+1 query issue in `process_memory_operations` within `adaptive_memory_v4.0.py`. Instead of fetching user memories from the database for each operation in a batch, all memories are now fetched once at the beginning of the method. The local cache is maintained throughout the loop to ensure semantic consistency for subsequent operations (e.g., deduplication and pruning).

### 🎯 Why:
The previous implementation performed a database query for every `UPDATE` operation to find the existing record, and also queried the database within `_is_duplicate` and `_prune_old_memories`. In batches with many operations, this resulted in significant I/O overhead and latency.

### 📊 Measured Improvement:
Using a simulated benchmark with 20 `UPDATE` operations and 100 existing memories:
- **Baseline**: 21 database calls, ~0.278s execution time.
- **Optimized**: 1 database call, ~0.053s execution time.
- **Result**: ~78% reduction in execution time and 95% reduction in database I/O for the tested batch size.

Functional integrity was verified via a test suite covering NEW, UPDATE, DELETE, Deduplication, and Pruning logic, ensuring that the in-memory cache remains in sync with the database state.

author: rlfarman
body:
## Summary

Migrates the gene/isoform read path from Postgres → static bucketed JSON. Runtime never touches a database; the entire authoring pipeline collapses to a single CSV-direct script that emits artifacts shipped with the repo.

## Changes

### Read path: Postgres → static
- **No runtime DB.** Drizzle, `@neondatabase/serverless`, `drizzle-kit`, `@electric-sql/pglite` all removed. `src/drizzle/`, `scripts/{load,migrate,verify,enrich,build-db}-*` deleted.
- **`/api/health`** stops pinging Postgres; checks artifact presence instead.
- **`DATABASE_URL`** env var dropped; production guardrail in `src/lib/env.ts` updated.
- **`pnpm content:rebuild <csv-path>`** is the single content pipeline. No JSONL intermediate, no `db:build`/`db:push`/`db:upload` chain.

### Artifact layout (emitted to `public/data/`)
- `manifest.json` — `[{id, symbol, species}]` for sitemap + `generateStaticParams`
- `isoform-index.json` — `{[isoformId]: {symbol, species, bucket}}` for routing + lazy fetches
- `genes-meta/<bucket>.json` — metadata + precomputed metrics, **bucketed alphabetically** by first char of symbol (27 buckets)
- `sequences/<bucket>.json` — raw CDS, lazy-fetched only on row expand / copy / download / comparison sheet
- `search-index-{human,mouse}.json` — MiniSearch shards, lazy-loaded by species filter

### Precomputation (build-time)
- `gcPercent`, `cpgCount`, `wggwCount`, `suitability` per isoform — no client-side scan needed for default render
- `identityMatrix` per gene — pairwise protein identity for top 16 isoforms
- Disease association row baked into each human gene's metadata — no `findBySymbol` lookup at render

### Component refactor
- `IsoformListItem` no longer carries `codingSequence`; metrics ride on the type
- `IsoformIdentityMatrix`, `IsoformSummary`, `IsoformLengthChart` take precomputed values
- `IsoformTable` row expansion + copy/download + `IsoformComparisonSheet` lazy-fetch sequences via new `useIsoformSequence` / `fetchIsoformSequence` / `fetchIsoformSequences` helpers
- `proteinSequence` dropped from emit; `proteinSequenceLength` derived from `codingSequenceLength` on read

### Cloudflare-friendly
- File count: 24K per-gene files → ~58 total. Comfortably under the free tier's 20K static-asset cap.
- Per-bucket gzipped sizes: metadata ≤ 0.4MB, sequences ≤ 1.8MB, search shards ~1.2-1.5MB

### Cache headers
- `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` on `/data/*` (artifacts are immutable per deploy)

### Earlier in the same branch
Commit history walks the migration in reviewable chunks: build-emit → SSG page → client MiniSearch → sitemap → drop Postgres reads → drop protein + precompute → drop Postgres entirely + buckets.

## Testing

- [x] Lint passes (`pnpm lint`) — 0 errors, 3 pre-existing warnings
- [x] Type-check passes (`pnpm type-check`)
- [x] Tests pass (`pnpm test`) — 313/313
- [x] Page renders with precomputed metrics + identity matrix + baked associations (verified in browser preview)
- [ ] **Production build not validated** — see Notes

## Notes

**Outstanding regression — please validate before merging.** In dev mode (`pnpm dev`), the `IsoformTable` row-expand button and other in-table click handlers don't fire even though the page renders correctly with precomputed metrics. The URL-driven expansion (`?isoform=ENST...`) works fine and the rest of the page (sidebar, links outside the table) is fully interactive. Console + server logs are clean.

I couldn't pin down the cause in dev — likely candidates:
- A Next 16 Turbopack quirk with this many sibling `'use client'` components in one file (Row × N + ExpandedDetails)
- An interaction between `cacheComponents: true` and the new `Suspense` boundary I added to isolate the dynamic `searchParams` read
- Possibly a client-bundle issue where `IsoformTable`'s chunk isn't being hydrated despite shipping

`pnpm build && pnpm start` should be the first thing to try — production builds often expose dev-only Turbopack bugs and may not reproduce. If prod is clean, this can ship; if not, the table-component bundling will need a closer look.

**Reseed workflow** (no DB anymore): `pnpm content:rebuild path/to/transcript_metadata.csv` → commit changed `public/data/*` → deploy.
