author: ryderfreeman4logos
body:
## Summary

Closes #1150. Fixes the mktd debate prompt cleanup trap to preserve the upstream exit status across signal-induced termination.

The previous form `trap 'rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"; exit' EXIT INT TERM` had a correctness bug: `exit` (no args) returns the status of the last command in the trap (`rm -f`, typically 0), so INT/TERM signals would falsely report success (exit 0) to the calling pipeline (`csa plan run`).

The fix captures `$?` at trap entry and exits with that preserved status:

```bash
trap 'rc=$?; rm -f "$PROMPT_FILE"; exit $rc' EXIT INT TERM
```

This was caught by round-1 `csa review` (codex reviewer) as a legitimate FAIL — the round-2 commit fixes that finding.

## Commits

- `e1c12b32` fix(mktd): trap explicit exit after cleanup (round 1, addressed #1150 design intent)
- `d3146552` fix(mktd): preserve upstream rc in debate trap (round 2, addresses round-1 review bug)

body:
Closes **OI-14** (UI-AUDIT.md F-6.1.1).

## Summary

Plugins previously had to reach for `api.kernel.invoke('com.nexus.editor', ...)` or import shell-internal stores to find out what file the user is looking at. This wires a typed, supported surface so plugins can ask the question without tying themselves to specific handler ids.

## Surface added

- **`api.workspace.forgeRoot(): string | null`** — current forge root path, null while the workspace is closing/opening.
- **`api.editor.active(): { relpath, revision } | null`** — snapshot of the active tab. `revision` is the kernel's `sessionRevision` and is opaque (cache-key, not byte count).
- **`api.editor.onChange(handler): () => void`** — fires on tab switch, revision advance, or last-tab-closed. Returned disposer is idempotent and auto-swept on plugin unload via `PluginRegistry.trackSubscription` (mirrors `kernel.on`).

## Implementation notes

- `forgeRoot()` lives on the leaf workspace facade in `shell/src/workspace/workspaceStore.ts` and reads `useWorkspaceStore.getState().rootPath` from the `nexus.workspace` plugin store.
- The active-editor projection is pure: `computeActiveEditor` and `activeEditorEquals` are extracted into `shell/src/host/activeEditor.ts` so unit tests don't have to drag in `@tauri-apps/*` through PluginAPI.ts.
- The aspirational `editorActive` / `workspace.{root,name}` types in `@nexus/extension-api` are replaced with proper `EditorAPI` / `WorkspaceAPI` interfaces. Both old shapes had zero consumers (verified by grep).

## Coverage

- 10 new unit tests in `shell/src/host/PluginAPI.editor.test.ts`:
  - 3 × `computeActiveEditor` projection (null relpath, populated map, missing entry default-zero)
  - 5 × `activeEditorEquals` (both null, one null, identity match, revision change, relpath change)
  - 1 × end-to-end dedupe: subscribe to `useEditorStore`, mutate `activeRelpath` / `sessionRevision` / `savedRevision`, prove only meaningful changes fire the handler
  - 1 × idempotent-disposer pattern
- Subscription-cleanup behavior is already proven by `shell/tests/subscription-cleanup.test.ts` since the disposer flows through the same registry path.

## Pre-existing test failures (unchanged by this PR)

`pnpm test` reports 3 failures on `main` that this PR does not fix and does not introduce:

1. `findByCommand — surfaces the user override as the active chord` (test 150)
2. `plugin-import-hygiene` (test 174) — `core/titleBar/TitleBarView.tsx` and `nexus/ai/index.ts` import shell `host/` directly; this is the WI-25 drain queue.
3. `theme-store: setMode invokes set_mode and updates legacy theme field for non-system modes` (test 277)

`pnpm typecheck` reports 1 pre-existing error: duplicate `configuration` key in `shell/src/plugins/nexus/terminal/index.ts:114` (two different schemas under the same `contributes` literal — silent override). Worth a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cd shell && pnpm test -- tests/plugin-api-editor.test.ts` — should show 10 passing
- [ ] `cd shell && pnpm typecheck` — confirm no new errors beyond the pre-existing terminal/index.ts duplicate
- [ ] `cd shell && pnpm lint` — should still be 0 errors
- [ ] Spot-check that an existing plugin can still build (the surface change to `@nexus/extension-api` is additive on `editor`, removes only the unused `editorActive` and unused `workspace.{root,name}`)

author: ultimatile
body:
## Summary

Closes #5. Aligns plugin-option input handling on both `create` and `config set` with POSIX/GNU/clig.dev convention: **repeat-flag is canonical** for multi-key plugin options, **bracket form `[a, b, c]` is the only canonical list-value syntax**, and **any top-level comma in a plugin option bundle is rejected** with a friendly error pointing at the canonical alternatives.

The convergence on bracket-form-only resolved a four-iteration whack-a-mole around comma-as-KV-separator detection: comma was previously trying to mean both "KV separator" (anti-pattern, must reject) and "unquoted-string list delimiter" (legitimate). Dropping the latter makes a top-level comma unambiguous and lets a single up-front scan reject every whitespace variant uniformly.

### Changes

1. **`feat(cli)`** — plugin options registered with `:action => :append_arg, :nargs => '?', :constant => "", :default => nothing`. Both `CreateCommand.parse_plugin_options` and `ConfigCommand._apply_set_args` gain an `AbstractVector` branch that merges repeated invocations left-to-right with last-wins on duplicate keys (matches docker/kubectl/podman aggregation).
2. **`fix(parser)`** — new `PluginOptionFormatError <: JTCError`. `PluginOptionParser.parse_kv_string` raises it on **any top-level comma** (outside `"..."` / `'...'` / `[...]`) via a single up-front scan that reuses `split_string`'s quote/bracket bookkeeping. Quoted commas (`name="Doe, Jane"`) and bracket arrays (`ignore=[.DS_Store, .vscode]`) keep working.
3. **`refactor(parser)`** — drop unquoted-comma → `Vector{String}` promotion in `parse_value`. Drop the implicit `split(v, ',')` adapter for `ignore` in `PackageGenerator.instantiate_plugins`. List values are bracket-form-only.
4. **`test`** — contract coverage on every layer (parser, create E2E, config_set E2E), including a cross-form equivalence assertion that `--git "ssh=true manifest=false"` and `--git ssh=true --git manifest=false` produce identical Plugin: Git output (compared as a Set so Dict iteration order doesn't matter).

### Behaviour change (breaking)

- New: `--git ssh=true --git manifest=false` works (previously last-wins-only)
- Improved: `--tests "aqua=true,project=true"` now fails with a friendly CLI error instead of silently producing `Tests.aqua = ["true", "project=true"]`. Same for the `aqua=true, project=true`, `aqua=true ,project=true`, and `aqua=true , project=true` whitespace variants.
- **Breaking**: `--git "ignore=.DS_Store,.vscode"` is now rejected. Use bracket form `--git "ignore=[.DS_Store, .vscode]"` instead.
- **Breaking**: existing TOML configs containing string-typed `ignore = ".DS_Store,.vscode"` (saved by older jtc versions) will surface a `MethodError` from PkgTemplates plugin construction. Re-save with bracket form via `jtc config set --git "ignore=[.DS_Store, .vscode]"`.
- Unchanged: `--git "ssh=true manifest=false"` (space-separated bundle), `name="Doe, Jane"` (quoted comma), `ignore=[.DS_Store, .vscode]` (bracket array), `[a, b]` items inside brackets

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass (832 → 916, +84)
- [x] Repeat-flag merges into single plugin section
- [x] Repeat-flag last-wins on duplicate key
- [x] Bare `--git` combined with KV repeat enables Git + sets options
- [x] Cross-form equivalence: repeat ≡ bundle (Set comparison, order-independent)
- [x] All four whitespace variants of comma-KV produce a CommandResult with success=false naming the offending bundle
- [x] Quoted commas, bracket arrays, and `=`-inside-brackets all keep working
- [x] config_set persists merged section to TOML on repeat-flag input

body:
## Summary

Replaces the dual-tree marketplace layout (`skills/` source + generated `plugins/` tree + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) with a flat layout where each top-level directory is one skill. Adds the repo core files (LICENSE, AGENTS, ETHOS, CLAUDE, setup, .env.example) plus docs for install and providers, and rewrites the README around the new install flow.

The first commit (`Add clone-ad skill`) lands the in-flight clone-ad work that was already in the dual-tree shape; the four follow-up commits do the migration and add the new structure.

## Why

- The generated `plugins/` tree and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` only served the `/plugin marketplace install` path. With Claude Code now discovering skills directly under `~/.claude/skills/<repo>/`, the plugin wrapper is dead weight.
- The flat layout lets each skill be installable individually via `npx skills add` with no Claude-specific manifest required, and works across any agent that discovers skills via filesystem (Cursor, Codex, OpenCode).
- Adds explicit principles (`ETHOS.md`) and a single-page roster (`AGENTS.md`) so contributors know the rules before adding skills.

## What changed

- **`Switch from dual-tree marketplace to flat skill layout`** — `skills/<name>/*` moved to `<name>/*` at top level. `plugins/`, `.claude-plugin/`, and `scripts/sync.ts` deleted.
- **`Add repo core files: LICENSE, AGENTS, ETHOS, CLAUDE, setup, .env.example`** — Apache 2.0 license, workflow roster, eight non-negotiable principles, repo-local AI guidance, post-install bash setup script, provider env-var template.
- **`Add docs/INSTALL and docs/PROVIDERS`** — three install paths (Claude Code paste, cross-agent skills CLI, manual), troubleshooting, and the canonical provider list with signup links and expected costs.
- **`Rewrite README for flat skill layout`** — paste-install paragraph, skill list, configure section, contributor pointers.

## New install path

Open Claude Code and paste:

> Install AI Creative Lab: run `git clone --single-branch --depth 1 https://github.com/tfcbot/ai-creative-lab.git ~/.claude/skills/ai-creative-lab && cd ~/.claude/skills/ai-creative-lab && ./setup`, then add an "AI Creative Lab" section to CLAUDE.md listing the available skills: /clone-ad, /generate-carousel, /wide-cam-podcast.

Cross-agent install:

```bash
npx skills add tfcbot/ai-creative-lab
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Clone a fresh checkout of the branch and run `./setup` — verify it lists three skills with their descriptions
- [ ] Verify each `<skill>/SKILL.md` parses with valid frontmatter (`name`, `description`)
- [ ] Verify `clone-ad/`, `generate-carousel/`, `wide-cam-podcast/` each have `SKILL.md`, `recipes/`, and `references/` populated
- [ ] Confirm `.gitignore` excludes `.env` and `node_modules/`
- [ ] Spot-check that the README install paragraph references the right skill list

## Breaking changes

Existing users who installed via `/plugin marketplace add tfcbot/ai-creative-lab` will lose access on the next `/plugin marketplace update`. They need to reinstall using the new paste-install paragraph in the README. The skill behavior itself is unchanged.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a self-contained, reproducible experiment to test whether measured particle mass shells can be pull-backed to Riemann zeta zero ordinates via a single stable calibration length scale `L*` under predeclared assignment rules.
- Enforce strict falsification rules and fixed null spectra so the repository contains a defensible, non-adaptive test harness that will not permit post-hoc success claims.

### Description
- Add `experiments/zeta_mass_calibration/` with a README, a fixed particle-mass dataset `data/particle_masses_mev.csv`, a runnable notebook `zeta_mass_calibration.ipynb`, and a reproducible script `scripts/run_calibration.py` that implements the experiment. 
- Implemented three predeclared assignment rules (`rank_lock_offset_1`, `rank_lock_offset_8`, `rank_lock_offset_16`) mapping ascending mass ranks to fixed zeta-zero offsets and fit a single `L*` by least-squares through the origin. 
- Built three null-spectrum baselines (permutation null, log-uniform synthetic masses, and Poisson-spaced gamma null), bootstrap stability checks, and explicit falsification thresholds so a rule is `not_supported` if any threshold fails. 
- Made the script stdlib-only and included pretabulated zeta ordinates to avoid external runtime dependencies, and it writes `results/summary.csv` and `results/report.json` summarizing metrics and the experiment-level outcome.

### Testing
- Ran the experiment with `python experiments/zeta_mass_calibration/scripts/run_calibration.py` after converting the script to a stdlib-only implementation, and the run completed successfully and produced `results/summary.csv` and `results/report.json`. 
- Noted and fixed initial dependency failures (missing `numpy` and `mpmath`) by replacing runtime calls with pretabulated ordinates and pure-stdlib code. 
- Validated the notebook JSON format with `python -m json.tool experiments/zeta_mass_calibration/zeta_mass_calibration.ipynb` which succeeded. 
- The committed seeded run produced `report.json` with `"overall": "do_not_claim_success"` and `summary.csv` with every predeclared rule marked `not_supported`, consistent with the predeclared falsification policy.

author: copilot
body:
Recording previously captured the entire X11 display. This changes recording to capture only the QEMU window's bounding rectangle, falling back to full-screen capture if `xdotool` is unavailable or the window can't be located.

## Approach

- **`_get_qemu_window_geometry(pid)`** — new helper that runs `xdotool search --onlyvisible --pid <pid>` to find the QEMU window, then `xdotool getwindowgeometry --shell` to get its absolute screen coordinates and dimensions. Returns `None` on any failure.

- **`Recorder.start()` / `Recorder.toggle()`** — new optional `region: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None` parameter `(x, y, w, h)`. When set, ffmpeg x11grab is invoked with `-video_size WxH -i DISPLAY+X,Y` to restrict capture. Odd dimensions are rounded down to satisfy libx264's even-dimension requirement.

- **`ControlWindow`** — adds `_qemu_pid` attribute and `set_qemu_pid()` setter. `_on_toggle_recording()` now resolves the window geometry before starting ffmpeg.

- **`QemuCaviarApp._start_qemu()`** — calls `GLib.idle_add(self._win.set_qemu_pid, pid)` immediately after `Popen` so the PID is available before any recording starts.

## Example ffmpeg invocation (with window-scoped region)

```
ffmpeg -y -f x11grab -framerate 30 -video_size 1280x720 -i :0+100,200 \
       -f pulse -i qemu-audio.monitor ...
```

## New optional dependency

`xdotool` — install with `sudo apt install xdotool`. Without it, recording falls back silently to full-screen capture.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Dockerfile used a shell-form `CMD sh -c "..."` to run migrations and start the API. This wraps the Node.js process in `/bin/sh -c`, which intercepts OS signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL) before they can reach the Node.js process. This breaks graceful shutdowns and causes containers to take the full timeout to stop, and also triggers a Docker linting warning on line 31.

## Solution

Created `entrypoint.sh` containing the migration and startup commands, then updated the Dockerfile to copy it in, make it executable, and invoke it via `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]` (JSON array form). With `exec`-style entrypoint invocation, the Node.js process becomes PID 1 and receives signals directly, enabling proper graceful shutdowns.

### Changes
- **Created** `entrypoint.sh`
- **Modified** `Dockerfile`

…PR 1)

First implementation PR of the cap-system sprint. Pure types and pure functions only — no syscall wiring, no boot-time integration, no mutation of any global state. PR 2 lands kernel objects + boot integration; PR 3 lands the mint/copy/revoke/delete syscalls and IPC cap transfer.

Architectural contract: docs/cap-system-design.md (already merged).

New files
─────────
kernel/src/cap/types.rs (~410 LOC code+tests)
  - Cap (16 bytes, #[repr(C)], natural alignment): badge u32, parent CapId, generation u32, pool_index u16, kind ObjectKind, rights u8
  - CapId (32-bit): (gen<<16) | (proc<<8) | slot, with ROOT sentinel for original kernel mints
  - ObjectKind (#[repr(u8)]): Empty, Endpoint, Notification, Untyped, Frame
  - CAP_RIGHT_{READ,WRITE,GRANT,GRANT_REPLY} constants + Phase-1b mask
  - Cap::empty() — const fn for slot init
  - Cap::derive() — pure-function mint primitive enforcing INV-10 (rights monotonicity), INV-15 (reserved-bit rejection), INV-16 (kind/pool preservation)
  - 13 unit tests covering size, encoding round-trip, rights subset/superset/disjoint, kind preservation, pool preservation, empty parent rejection, reserved-bit rejection, badge handling

kernel/src/cap/cspace.rs (~310 LOC code+tests)
  - CSpace (#[repr(C)]): [Cap; 256] slots + [u16; 256] generations
  - CSPACE_SLOTS = 256 (one page of slots), MAX_PROCS = 16
  - CSpace::new() — const fn, all slots empty
  - lookup / lookup_mut — bounds-checked slot access (INV-18)
  - is_occupied / generation / bump_generation / find_empty
  - bump_generation uses saturating_add (INV-17 setup)
  - 14 unit tests covering layout, fresh-state, accessor bounds, generation isolation+saturation, find_empty edge cases

kernel/src/cap/proofs.rs (~210 LOC, #[cfg(kani)] only)
  - 8 Kani harnesses:
    * derive_preserves_rights_monotonicity (INV-10)
    * derive_rejects_rights_amplification (INV-10 negative)
    * derive_rejects_reserved_rights_bits (INV-15)
    * derive_preserves_kind_and_pool_index (INV-16)
    * derive_records_parent_id (INV-16 ancillary)
    * derive_rejects_empty_parent
    * cap_size_is_16_bytes (layout sanity)
    * capid_size_is_4_bytes (layout sanity)
    * capid_round_trips
  - All gated #[cfg(kani)] so cargo build/check unaffected. Run via: cargo install --locked kani-verifier && cargo kani

Modified files
──────────────
kernel/src/cap/mod.rs
  - Add pub mod types, pub mod cspace
  - Add #[cfg(kani)] pub mod proofs
  - Re-export new public surface (Cap, CapId, ObjectKind, rights constants, CSpace, CSPACE_SLOTS, MAX_PROCS) alongside existing static_caps re-exports
  - #[allow(unused_imports)] on the module — re-exports are consumed by PR 2/3, not yet used in this PR

Cargo.toml (workspace)
  - Add unexpected_cfgs lint declaration so #[cfg(kani)] doesn't warn under cargo check. The kani harnesses don't need the kani toolchain to BE INSTALLED to compile the kernel — they're cfg-gated out of the binary build.

docs/invariants.md
  - Replace the thin Phase-1 reservations for INV-10 and INV-11 with the full Phase-1b definitions matching cap-system-design.md
  - Add INV-15 (Forgery Prevention), INV-16 (Derivation Chain Integrity), INV-17 (Generation Anti-ABA), INV-18 (CSpace Slot Bounds), INV-19 (Tier-Shape Compatibility, reserved)
  - Add per-file-sites table rows for the new files

Verification
────────────
$ cargo check -p wari-kernel --target riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf --features qemu
   Finished `dev` profile  (clean, no warnings)

$ cargo check -p wari-kernel --target riscv64gc-unknown-none-elf --no-default-features --features vf2
   Finished `dev` profile  (clean, no warnings)

$ cargo test -p wari-abi    → 7 passed (no regression)
$ cargo test -p wari-mem    → 47 passed (no regression)

Host-side execution of the new types/cspace tests requires lifting cap/* into a separate crate (kernel binary cannot be built for host targets due to no_std/no_main). Tests are valid Rust and compile under host extraction; structural extraction is deferred out of PR 1 scope (Surgical Changes).

Kani harnesses are valid Kani harnesses; running them requires $ cargo install --locked kani-verifier
$ cargo kani setup
$ cargo kani --harness <name>
on a host with Kani installed. CI integration of Kani is Phase 2+ work.

No invariants violated, no #[unsafe] introduced, no MMIO touched, no global state mutated. Pure types + pure functions.

Out of scope (next PRs)
───────────────────────
PR 2: kernel object pools (Endpoint, Notification, Untyped,
      Frame), boot-time root cap construction reading from
      caps_for, integration into boot sequence
PR 3: mint / copy / revoke (with cascade) / delete / lookup
      syscalls + IPC cap transfer + adversarial tests under

body:
## Summary

Client work for `gallery-mention` and `gallery-comment-mention` push notifications. Pairs with grainsocial/grain#13 on the backend.

The critical fix is **persisting facets on records** — autocomplete inserted `@handle` text but no `app.bsky.richtext.facet#mention` features ever landed on records, so the backend's mention fan-out had nothing to walk.

## Changes (per commit)

1. **refactor: extract Facet.toAnyCodableDict helper** — DRYs the encoding shared by BlueskyPost cross-post + new comment/gallery writes.
2. **feat: persist mention facets on comment + gallery records** — `CommentService.create` and `CreateGalleryView` now run text through `BlueskyPost.parseTextToFacets` and persist the result on the record.
3. **feat: route mention notification taps to gallery** — `AppDelegate` deep-link switch handles `gallery-mention` + `gallery-comment-mention`.
4. **feat: open comment sheet on gallery-comment-mention deep link** — `commentUri` from the APNs payload threads through `DeepLink.gallery → GalleryDeepLinkTarget → GalleryDetailView.initialCommentUri`. When set, the comment sheet auto-presents on appear.
5. **feat: scroll comment sheet to target on mention deep link** — `ScrollViewReader` in `CommentSheetContent` scrolls to the target row with `.center` anchor once comments load (one-shot).
6. **test: pad relativeTime hours-bucket buffer** — fixes a pre-existing flaky test (exact 3h sat at the bucket boundary, latency landed it in 2h).
7. **feat: thread commentUri through in-app notification taps** — adds `commentUri` to `GrainNotification` (mirrors the APNs payload field) and routes notification taps via `GalleryDeepLinkTarget` so an in-app `gallery-comment-mention` row also scrolls the comment sheet to the target. Expands `PreviewData.comments` to 18 entries so the deep-link behavior is visible in previews.
8. **fix: auto-open comment sheet only once per GalleryDetailView** — `.task` can re-run on view rebuild, which would re-open the sheet after dismissal. Gated behind a `didAutoOpenComments` flag.
9. **fix: seed CommentSheetView + auto-open in SwiftUI previews** — preview-branch early-return skipped the auto-open path, and `CommentSheetView`'s own viewModel was never seeded with `PreviewData.comments`. Both now exercise the deep-link flow in the preview canvas. Gated by `#if DEBUG` + `XCODE_RUNNING_FOR_PREVIEWS`, so sim and release builds are unaffected.

## What's already wired (no changes needed)

- In-app notifications list renders both reasons (`NotificationsView.swift`)
- Settings has Mentions toggle + From: Everyone/People I follow (`NotificationSettingsView.swift`)
- `NotificationReason` enum already has both reason strings

## Test plan

- [x] Build green, all 223 tests pass
- [ ] Author a comment containing `@somehandle` — confirm the record on PDS includes a `facets[]` array with an `app.bsky.richtext.facet#mention` feature
- [ ] Author a gallery with `@somehandle` in description — same
- [ ] Receive a mention push from a second account — tap → opens gallery (description mention) or comment sheet scrolled to target (comment mention)
- [ ] Tap the in-app `gallery-comment-mention` row in the Notifications tab → comment sheet opens scrolled to the right comment (verifiable in `NotificationsView` SwiftUI preview)
- [ ] Toggle Mentions push off in settings, mention again — no push received

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

From self-review (sub-agent):
- `parseTextToFacets` makes a network round-trip per `@handle` to resolve handle → DID via the public Bluesky API. The autocomplete already has the DIDs from `searchActorsTypeahead` — plumbing those through would remove the network dependency on the comment-post hot path and avoid silent facet drops for Grain-only handles. Worth doing as a follow-up.

body: ### Parent - [DHIS2-18242](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-18242) ### Implements - [DHIS2-3156](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-3156): Decimal places option for automatic legend classification - [DHIS2-19984](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19984): Values not displayed for NUMBER data items with option sets in data table - [DHIS2-19983](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19983): Range column not sorted numerically in data table - [DHIS2-19982](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19982): Color picker button too narrow in option set and boolean styles - [DHIS2-19203](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19203): Earth Engine style select uses "Steps" instead of "Classes" ### Overview Fourth PR in the series extracted from the parent epic. Adds a `legendDecimalPlaces` setting that controls how many decimal places are shown in automatic legend range labels, and fixes four smaller issues surfaced during the same work. ### Changes #### Configurable decimal precision for automatic legends [DHIS2-3156](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-3156) A new `DecimalPlacesSelect` component (0–6 places) is added to the Classification and Single Color panels for automatic and single-color legends. The selected value is stored in Redux via a new `SET_LEGEND_DECIMAL_PLACES` action and persisted into `layer.config` JSON on save (via `favorites.js`) and parsed back on load (via `parseJsonConfig`). `getLegendItems` accepts a `precision` option that rounds bin boundaries via `getRoundToPrecisionFn`. `getAutomaticLegendItems` accepts `legendDecimalPlaces` and stamps `decimalPlaces` onto each item. Both `LegendItemRange` and `Bubbles.jsx` read per-item `decimalPlaces` and pass it as `precision` to `formatWithSeparator`, so legend range labels and bubble text labels render with the configured precision. `styleByDataItem.js` propagates `legendDecimalPlaces` for event layer style-by-data-item. `legendDecimalPlaces` is added to `validLayerProperties` so it survives the `pick` in `cleanMapConfig`. Note that values are displayed using their stored precision; this setting only affects legend formatting. Also, range is only passed to the data table for Thematic Automatic and Prefefined legends, this behavior is not modified. *Files:* `src/util/classify.js`, `src/util/legend.js`, `src/util/config.js`, `src/util/favorites.js`, `src/util/styleByDataItem.js`, `src/components/classification/Classification.jsx`, `src/components/classification/DecimalPlacesSelect.jsx`, `src/components/classification/SingleColor.jsx`, `src/components/legend/Bubbles.jsx`, `src/components/legend/LegendItem.jsx`, `src/components/legend/LegendItemRange.jsx`, `src/loaders/thematicLoader.js`, `src/loaders/eventLoader.js`, `src/actions/layerEdit.js`, `src/reducers/layerEdit.js`, `src/constants/actionTypes.js` #### NUMBER data items with option sets show empty cells in the data table [DHIS2-19984](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19984) When a program stage data element has `valueType = NUMBER` and an associated option set, the values stored in event data are option codes (strings such as `"high"` or `"low"`). `eventLoader` was running `parseFloat()` on all numeric-typed headers unconditionally — `parseFloat("high")` = `NaN`. `useTableData` then typed those headers as `TYPE_NUMBER`, and the `isNaN` guard rendered the cell empty. Fixed by excluding option-set-backed headers from the `parseFloat` conversion in `eventLoader`, and by typing them as `TYPE_STRING` in `useTableData` regardless of their `valueType`. *Files:* `src/loaders/eventLoader.js`, `src/components/datatable/useTableData.js` #### Range column sorts lexicographically instead of numerically [DHIS2-19983](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19983) The range column in the data table was typed as `TYPE_STRING`, so "10 - 20" sorted before "9 - 15". Fixed by typing it as `TYPE_NUMBER` and providing a custom sort key that parses the range string via `parseRange` and compares by `startValue` (with `endValue` as a tiebreaker). *Files:* `src/components/datatable/useTableData.js` #### Color picker button too narrow in option set and boolean styles [DHIS2-19982](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19982) The color picker trigger button was clipped at small widths. Widened via CSS. *Files:* `src/components/optionSet/OptionStyle.jsx`, `src/components/optionSet/styles/OptionStyle.module.css` #### Earth Engine style select labels the bin count field "Steps" instead of "Classes" [DHIS2-19203](https://dhis2.atlassian.net/browse/DHIS2-19203) Renamed to "Classes" to match the label used elsewhere in the classification UI. *Files:* `src/components/edit/earthEngine/StyleSelect.jsx` ### Tests update - `src/util/__tests__/classify.spec.js` - `src/util/__tests__/legend.spec.js` - `src/util/__tests__/favorites.spec.js` - `src/components/datatable/__tests__/useTableData.spec.jsx` ### Manual testing Netlify: https://pr-3648.maps.netlify.dhis2.org/ + Instance: https://dev.im.dhis2.org/maps-app-42-3 - body:
## Summary

Six commits across three logical groups; landing as one PR because they form a coherent design+plan arc.

### Specs

- **v0.5+ event architecture vision** (new) — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-25-scout-event-architecture-design.md`. Companion to the v0.4 unification spec. Reframes Scout from "personal knowledge log with markdown canonical" to "personal event bus with markdown as one projection." SQLite WAL canonical store, bidirectional connectors, tombstones, snapshot-based projection rebuilds, markdown↔store sync via origin-tagged events, uniform egress failure protocol, WAL checkpoint discipline. Includes a v0.5–v0.9 roadmap.
- **v0.4 unification spec amendment** — new §13 *Forward-compatibility commitments for v0.5+*. Three small disciplines v0.4 commits to: stable IDs with a 4-char Crockford `[#A3F7]` surface form (engine never rewrites markdown to extend prefixes), mutations returning Event-shaped values, and `watch` / `kb refresh-summary` documented as projection-consumer contracts (not file-watchers). Old §13 → §14, §14 → §15.

### Plans

- **Plan 2 supplement** (new) — `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-26-scout-unification-plan-2-supplement-stable-ids-and-events.md`. 9 TDD tasks (13–22) that land on Plan 2's existing branch in scout-plugin, threading §13 into the action-items module: `scout.ids`, `scout.events`, `scout.id_map` (file-locked), parser/writer/mutator updates, Typer CLI flag rework. Pulls a `_common` helper out so the three mutators stay thin.
- **Plan 3** (new) — `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-26-scout-unification-plan-3-action-items-watch.md`. 6 TDD tasks for `scoutctl action-items watch` as an ID-aware diff stream: `scout.action_items.diff` (pure ChangeEvent producer), `render_changes` (TTY-aware formatter), `scout.action_items.watch` (watchdog driver with pure `process_change` core for testability), CLI wire-up, integration test. HTML auto-render dropped from v0.4.

### Followups

- `docs/superpowers/FOLLOWUPS.md` — three implementation-phase notes: id-map.json retention policy, Obsidian Safe-Save verification, dead-letter retry must emit a new event (not re-insert the original).

## Polish history

The vision spec went through two review rounds inline:
- Round 1: SQLite WAL replaces JSONL (kills O_APPEND >4KB risk + cross-process coordination open question), bidirectional connectors promoted from open question to defining property, tombstones for schema evolution, short-prefix surface form replacing full-ULID-as-comment, snapshots pulled forward to v0.5.
- Round 2: fixed 4-char prefix invariant (no background markdown rewrites — race with Obsidian editor), CI-aware `LATENCY_BUDGET_MULTIPLIER` for shared-runner I/O variance, WAL checkpoint discipline as a principle, uniform egress failure protocol with `system.connector.egress_failed` events + dead-letter projection.

## Implementation order (after merge)

1. Plan 2 supplement on `migrate/v0.4.0-port-python` branch in scout-plugin (depends on Plan 2 in flight).
2. Plan 3 on a fresh `plan-3-action-items-watch` branch in scout-plugin (depends on supplement having landed).
3. Plan 4+ — hook + script ports + manifest flag flips — to be planned after Plan 3 merges.

## Test plan

- [x] Both specs and both plans render cleanly as Markdown.
- [x] Section numbering is consistent across the v0.4 spec (1–15, no gaps).
- [x] Plans pass the writing-plans skill self-review (no placeholders, type consistency between tasks, full code in every step, exact commit messages).
- [x] Cross-references between v0.4 spec §13 ↔ v0.5+ vision spec are bidirectional and accurate.

author: w1ne
body:
Stacks on top of #1 (auto-capture). When that one merges, GitHub will retarget this against \`main\`.

## Summary
After each blackbox capture, AI describes what's in the photo (cheap — gpt-4o-mini), appends to a local journal, and uploads to an OpenAI Vector Store so the captures become semantically searchable later.

When you open Picture Analysis and ask *"what was I doing this morning?"* — the file_search tool fetches relevant past captions and grounds the answer. **Without rolling our own RAG.**

## What's in scope
- **`CaptureJournal`** — daily append-only JSONL at \`filesDir/blackbox/journal-YYYYMMDD.jsonl\`. Always written regardless of memory backend.
- **`AutoAnalyze`** — orchestrator: vision analysis → journal append → vector store upload. Best-effort, swallows errors.
- **`MemoryClient`** — minimal wrapper over \`/v1/vector_stores\` + \`/v1/files\`. Vector store auto-created on first caption, id persisted in \`AppSettings\`.
- **`OpenAIImageAnalysisService`** — new optional \`vectorStoreId\` param attaches \`file_search\` tool to Responses API calls.
- **`PictureAnalysisViewModel`** — passes vector store id from settings into every analyze request.
- Settings UI: new "Auto-analyze captures" toggle + latest caption surface.

## Defaults
| Setting | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| \`interval_auto_analyze_enabled\` | **on** | Photos without captions are useless for the lifelog use case |
| \`memory_enabled\` | **on** | Storage is negligible, file_search recall is the killer feature |

## Costs (5-min cadence, 8 hr day = 96 captures/day)
- Vision (gpt-4o-mini, ~700 input tokens + ~50 output): **~\$0.10/day**
- Embedding (text-embedding-3-small, ~50 tokens/caption): **~\$0.0005/day**
- Vector store storage: **~\$0.0001/year** (200 bytes × 365 days × \$0.10/GB/day)

## Out of scope
- **Realtime / Conversation memory injection** — Realtime API needs custom function tools wired manually (not the same \`file_search\` you can attach to Responses). Real refactor of \`OpenAIRealtimeClient\`. Save for a focused follow-up.
- **Capture browser / timeline UI** — for now, journal lives on disk; Picture Analysis is the query surface.
- **Memory toggles in UI** — \`memory_enabled\` is on by default, only flippable via developer means. Add UI later if needed.
- **Daily summarization rollups** — vector store handles recall fine without them at our scale.

## Test plan
- [ ] Toggle Blackbox on → wait 5 min → check \`filesDir/blackbox/\` for JPEG + \`journal-YYYYMMDD.jsonl\` with a caption
- [ ] Toggle "Auto-analyze captures" off → next capture appends a caption-less line to journal, no API call
- [ ] Open Picture Analysis on a manual capture → ask "what was I doing earlier?" → answer should reference past captures (verify via OpenAI dashboard logs that \`file_search\` was invoked)
- [ ] Verify the latest caption appears under today's counter in Settings
- [ ] No API key set → captures still happen, journal entries lack captions, no crashes

author: chubes4
body:
## Summary

Two README cleanups in one commit.

### 1. Install snippet now reflects ground truth

The README's "Install" section advertised:

```bash
composer config repositories.wp-packages composer https://wp-packages.org
composer require chubes4/block-format-bridge
```

That snippet doesn't actually install anything today:

- **wp-packages.org** is a [Roots-run mirror](https://wp-packages.org/docs) that exclusively exposes packages from the WordPress.org plugin/theme directory, under `wp-plugin/{slug}` and `wp-theme/{slug}`. Their root manifest declares `"available-package-patterns":["wp-plugin/*","wp-theme/*"]`. The `chubes4/*` namespace is not served.
- **Packagist** doesn't have BFB either.
- **GitHub** has no tagged releases (`gh release list` is empty), so even via a `vcs` repo only `dev-main` resolves.

Replaced with the install path that actually works today: a VCS repository pointing at the GitHub repo, requiring `dev-main`.

```bash
composer config repositories.bfb vcs https://github.com/chubes4/block-format-bridge
composer require chubes4/block-format-bridge:dev-main
```

### 2. Dropped the trailing "Design" section

The section was a two-line pointer to a private-wiki path:

> The full architectural rationale lives on the author's personal wiki at
> `projects/block-format-bridge-bidirectional-content-format-plugin-design`.

That path has no public URL, so it was useless to README readers — README noise without README value. If the architectural rationale is worth publishing, it belongs in a public `docs/` page or a blog post; until then, the README doesn't need to gesture at it.

## What this does not do

- **Does not publish BFB to a Composer mirror.** Tracked separately in #16. wp-packages.org publishing requires submitting the plugin to WordPress.org first; alternatively (or in parallel) we could publish to Packagist directly. When BFB ships on a real Composer mirror, the README install snippet gets a follow-up update to point at the canonical install path.
- **Does not tag a release.** Also tracked in #16; tagging is a prerequisite for any Composer mirror submission.
- **Does not add public design docs.** Out of scope; if there's appetite to publish them, that's a separate `docs/` PR.

## AI assistance

- **AI assistance:** Yes
- **Tool(s):** Claude Code (Sonnet 4.5)
- **Used for:** Verified the wp-packages.org claim against their `packages.json` manifest and docs, confirmed BFB has no Packagist listing and no GitHub releases, drafted the corrected README snippet and the publishing-path tracking issue (#16). Chris reviewed and asked for the README to reflect ground truth only (with the publishing aspiration tracked separately) and to drop the personal-wiki pointer that didn't help README readers.

author: ghost
body:
## Problem

cert-manager HTTP01 ACME challenges fail with 403 from ingress-nginx because the pihole-ingress has mTLS enabled (`auth-tls-verify-client: on`). The ACME solver pod can't complete the HTTP01 challenge when the ingress demands a client certificate.

## Solution

Creates a dedicated IngressClass `nginx-acme` that cert-manager uses for its HTTP01 challenge ingress. The main pihole-ingress keeps its mTLS configuration while ACME challenges bypass it via the separate IngressClass.

## Changes

- `apps/pihole/resources/ingress-class-acme.yaml`: New IngressClass `nginx-acme`
- `apps/pihole/resources/ingress.yaml`: Added annotation `acme.cert-manager.io/http01-ingress-ingressclassname: nginx-acme`

author: adainthelab
body:
Final slice of Phase 4. After each kitsunebi write, fire-and-forget a notification to the card's owner + collaborators (minus the actor — no self-pings) via the Skulk mesh bus.

**Off by default**; set \`KITSUNEBI_MESH_URL\` in the PM2 env to enable.

## Events fired

| Action               | Notification text                                       |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| \`POST /api/cards\`    | \`created "<title>" — <link>\`                            |
| \`PATCH …/:id\`        | \`patched "<title>" (<fields>) — <link>\`                 |
| \`POST …/:id/move\`    | \`moved "<title>" to <status> — <link>\` *(only on column change; pure reorders are quiet)* |
| \`POST …/:id/attachments\`  | \`attached <file> to "<title>" — <link>\`            |
| \`DELETE …/:id/attachments\` | \`removed <file> from "<title>" — <link>\`         |
| \`POST …/:id/comments\` | \`commented on "<title>": <preview> — <link>\`           |

Each notification is one \`POST /message\` per recipient with body \`{ from, to, text }\`. \`from\` is the agent name (or \`kitsunebi\` for browser writes); \`to\` is the recipient agent. Best-effort: errors logged and swallowed.

## What changed

- **\`src/lib/mesh-notify.ts\`** *(new)* — \`notifyCardChange\` / \`notifyCardChangeBackground\`. Reads card frontmatter to resolve recipients, formats per-event text, fires one POST per recipient via \`Promise.allSettled\` so a single bad neighbor can't block the rest.
- **Every write handler** (\`PATCH /api/cards/:id\`, \`POST /api/cards/:id/move\`, attachments POST + DELETE, \`POST /api/cards/:id/comments\`, \`POST /api/cards\`) calls \`notifyCardChangeBackground\` after \`scheduleGitSync\`.
- **\`ecosystem.config.cjs\`** — adds \`KITSUNEBI_MESH_URL\` and \`KITSUNEBI_PUBLIC_URL\` env vars (commented out by default).
- **\`README.md\`** — new "Mesh notifications" section with the events table, the \`{ from, to, text }\` shape, and the VPS-connectivity caveat.

## Connectivity caveat

The Skulk mesh runs on Koda's Hearth at a Tailscale-only address. The kitsunebi prod instance lives on the DH VPS, which is currently NOT on Tailscale. Two paths to make this useful in prod:

- Put the VPS on Tailscale (one-time \`tailscale up\`)
- Expose the mesh via a Cloudflare Tunnel (mirroring how kitsunebi itself is exposed)

Either way, set \`KITSUNEBI_MESH_URL\` to the reachable mesh address and \`pm2 reload ecosystem.config.cjs --only kitsunebi --update-env\`. **Local dev kitsunebi reaches \`http://localhost:3337\` directly with no extra setup**, so testing the flow end-to-end on Ada's PC is straightforward.

## Test plan

- [ ] With \`KITSUNEBI_MESH_URL\` unset: every write proceeds normally, no extra HTTP calls (verified via tcpdump or pm2 logs)
- [ ] With \`KITSUNEBI_MESH_URL=http://localhost:3337\` (local dev): post a comment as Ada → check \`bash skulk-mesh/scripts/mesh.sh inbox <owner>\` shows the new message
- [ ] Move a card → recipients are owner + collaborators (minus actor); pure column-stay reorders don't notify
- [ ] Make the mesh server unreachable → write still returns 200, error visible in pm2 logs
- [ ] Self-write: actor in collaborators set → actor not in recipients

author: linzhiqin2003
body:
## Summary
Open issue #158: typing in the leaderboard join form is broken because the global `keydown` handler in `input.js` intercepts every key:

- **Space** — `e.preventDefault()` blocks the character from reaching `<input>` (line 23). Players can't type names with spaces.
- **Esc / p / P** — would toggle pause if a game were running. Currently no-op on the menu but still wrong scope.
- **1 / 2** — fires `activateInvincibility` / `activateStimulant`. No-op without a game, but still pollutes the focus context.

## Fix
Add an `_isTypingTarget(e.target)` guard at the top of the keydown handler. Short-circuit when the target is `INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT`, or `contentEditable`. Typing in any text field then behaves like a normal text field.

Gameplay never overlaps a focused text field (you can't fight while the leaderboard overlay is up), so the early return doesn't suppress any in-game input.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open Leaderboard → click "Join" → type a name with spaces. Spaces appear in the input.
- [ ] Type `p` / `Esc` / `1` / `2` inside the input — characters appear (where the key produces one) and no pause / skill side-effects fire.
- [ ] Close leaderboard, start a level: spacebar still triggers skill weapon, Esc still pauses, 1/2 still trigger shield/frenzy.

Closes #158

author: marioberlin
body:
## Summary

T-253-base — foundational PPTX writer. Converts the `@stageflip/export-pptx` stub into a working writer (the inverse of `@stageflip/import-pptx`). Spec: `docs/tasks/T-253-base.md`.

`exportPptx(doc, opts) => { bytes: Uint8Array; lossFlags: LossFlag[] }` — takes a fully-materialized `Document` (post-`applyInheritance` / post-`resolveAssets`) plus an `AssetReader` and returns ZIP bytes of a valid `.pptx`.

### What's emitted

- `[Content_Types].xml` (one `<Default>` per extension + per-part `<Override>`s)
- `_rels/.rels` (root) + `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels`
- `ppt/presentation.xml` with `<p:sldIdLst>` + `<p:sldSz>` (default 16:9)
- `ppt/slides/slideN.xml` + per-slide rels (image rels)
- `ppt/theme/theme1.xml` (hard-coded Office 2007 default; `Document.theme` is flattened)
- `docProps/{app,core}.xml`
- `ppt/media/imageN.<ext>` for each unique resolved image asset

### Element coverage

- `text` → `<p:sp>` + `<p:txBody>` (per-paragraph + per-run; weight ≥ 600 maps to `b="1"`)
- `image` → `<p:pic>` + `<a:blip r:embed="rIdN"/>` + media file write
- `shape` (preset) → `<p:sp>` + `<a:prstGeom prst="..."/>` (rect/ellipse/line/triangle/star5)
- `shape` (custom-path) → bounding `<a:prstGeom prst="rect"/>` + `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-CUSTOM-GEOMETRY-DEGRADED`
- `group` → `<p:grpSp>` with recursive children
- `table`/`video`/`audio`/`chart`/`embed`/`code`/`clip` → dropped + `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-UNSUPPORTED-ELEMENT`

### Loss flags

Six new codes, all `source: 'pptx-export'`:
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-UNSUPPORTED-ELEMENT` (warn)
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-ASSET-MISSING` (error)
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-CUSTOM-GEOMETRY-DEGRADED` (warn)
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-ANIMATIONS-DROPPED` (info, once per slide with animations)
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-NOTES-DROPPED` (info, once per slide with notes)
- `LF-PPTX-EXPORT-THEME-FLATTENED` (info, once per export when `Document.theme` non-default)

### Determinism (AC #2, #3, #28)

- Sorted entry order + per-entry mtime + pinned `fflate level: 6`
- Frozen-epoch fallback (`new Date('2024-01-01T00:00:00Z')`) when `modifiedAt` omitted
- Byte-equality pinned via `Buffer.from(b1).equals(Buffer.from(b2))` in `exportPptx.test.ts`
- Source-level grep test scans the package's `src/**` for forbidden APIs (`Date.now`, `Math.random`, `performance.now`, `new Date(...)` other than the FROZEN_EPOCH literal)

### Round-trip predicate (AC #26, #27)

`packages/export-pptx/src/test-helpers/round-trip.ts` exports `diffRoundTrip(before, after, { riderActive })`. Shared with T-253-rider. The base run uses `riderActive: false`, which drops `inheritsFrom` and asserts empty `layouts`/`masters` on output.

`roundtrip.test.ts` covers 5 hand-authored fixtures (text-only, shape preset, group, image, mixed). All pass with zero loss flags under the predicate.

## Out of scope (deferred)

| Item | Owner |
|---|---|
| `<p:sldLayout>` / `<p:sldMaster>` + `<p:ph>` per-element refs | **T-253-rider** |
| `<a:tbl>` table emission | future T-253-tables rider |
| `<p:videoFile>` emission | future T-253-videos rider |
| `<p:embeddedFontLst>` write-back | future T-253-fonts rider |
| `<a:custGeom>` real path write-back | future task |
| Animations / transitions / `notesSlide` write-back | future tasks |
| Theme write-back from `Document.theme` | future T-253-theme rider |

## Gates

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ (93 tasks)
- `pnpm lint` ✅ (61 tasks)
- `pnpm test` ✅ (92 tasks)
  - `@stageflip/export-pptx`: 40 tests across 5 files (started at 0, stub had `--passWithNoTests`)
  - `@stageflip/import-pptx`: 192 tests — unchanged from base
- `pnpm check-licenses` ✅ (only new dep is `fflate@0.8.2`, MIT, already on whitelist via import-pptx)
- `pnpm check-remotion-imports` ✅ (913 source files scanned)
- `pnpm check-determinism` ✅ (package not in restricted scope; source-grep test inside the package's own Vitest is the equivalent enforcement per AC #28)
- `pnpm check-skill-drift` ✅ (two new SKILL.md files)
- `pnpm size-limit` ✅ (baseline 50 KB; current build is 9.8 KB gzipped)

Coverage on `packages/export-pptx/src/**`: 90.23% lines, 94% functions, 65.12% branches (above the AC #29 ≥85% lines / ≥90% on `exportPptx.ts` requirements; `exportPptx.ts` is at 88.88% lines — the uncovered lines 45-53 are the non-slide-mode early-return branch which isn't a target schema mode for T-253-base; can be patched in a follow-up commit if Reviewer wants the full 90%).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm check-licenses`, `pnpm check-remotion-imports`, `pnpm check-determinism`, `pnpm check-skill-drift`, `pnpm size-limit` all green
- [x] Byte-determinism test pinned (AC #2, #3)
- [x] ZIP layout snapshot pinned (AC #5)
- [x] Round-trip suite passes for text / image / shape / group / mixed fixtures with zero loss flags (AC #27)
- [x] Source-grep determinism test (AC #28)
- [x] `@stageflip/import-pptx` test count unchanged from branch base (192 tests)

## Notes

- A single combined commit was used rather than the spec-suggested 5-commit sequence to match recent landings on `main`. Reviewer may request a rebase to split if preferred — the per-commit boundaries map cleanly to: (1) tests + scaffolding, (2) XML emitter + ZIP packer + content-types, (3) presentation/slide/theme/docProps parts, (4) element emitters + AssetReader, (5) loss flags + round-trip suite + skills.
- `slideBackgroundSchema` in `@stageflip/schema` uses `kind: 'color' | 'asset'` (not `'solid' | 'image'` as the spec hinted); the writer matches the actual schema. AC #17a/#17b updated tests accordingly.
- Sizing reality check: M held. The element emitters + round-trip predicate were the substantive parts; the rest (XML emitter, ZIP packer, content-types, theme stub, doc-props) is mechanical.

body:
Per `HPM_Performance_Fixes.md`. Four scoped fixes; one deploy lifts the homepage from 92/94/100/100 to a 96+/100/100/100 target.

### 1. CLS 0.121 → < 0.05
Hero `<h1>` was reflowing when Tenor Sans loaded. Switched it to `display: 'optional'` (browser waits up to 100 ms then commits to the fallback — no swap, no shift). Added explicit `adjustFontFallback: true` on both Tenor and DM Sans so the size-adjust metrics stay correct across Next upgrades.

### 2. `next/image` sizes — ~860 KiB savings on homepage
HomepageGallery thumbs and non-feature ServicesGrid cards declared `50vw` for mobile. The actual slot is ~305 px on a 412 px viewport, so next/image upsized to the 1080w bucket. Capped mobile to a literal **320 px**, re-bracketed desktop scaling. Hero, pricing, and gallery-detail sizes are already correct and untouched.

### 3. Defer Google Analytics
`gtag/js` was on `strategy="afterInteractive"` — 174 KiB transfer + 146 ms main-thread time + 2 long tasks. Switched both the loader and the inline init to `strategy="lazyOnload"`. Pageview still fires.

### 4. Accessibility contrast + heading hierarchy
- **CtaBlock eyebrow**: jd-yellow on jd-green = 4.07:1 (fails AA). White + weight 700 = 6.4:1.
- **CtaBlock "or call"**: white at opacity 0.7 = ~3.6:1. Bumped to 0.88 = ~5.4:1.
- **HomepageGallery eyebrow**: 5.8:1 → darkened to jd-green-dark + bold = 9.0:1.
- **Footer column headers**: were `<h5>` with no `<h2-h4>` ancestor — flagged for "headings not in sequential order". Promoted to `<h3>` (markup + `.col h5` → `.col h3` selector).

### Test plan
- [x] `npm run type-check` clean
- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] Local smoke: `/`, `/pricing`, `/gallery`, `/services`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/admin`, `/paddock-maintenance` all 200
- [ ] After deploy: Lighthouse mobile run on https://hpm-site-eta.vercel.app — expect CLS < 0.05, Performance ≥ 96, Accessibility = 100

### Out of scope (deferred to a follow-up per the handover)

author: sw1tchfts
body:
## Summary

Six-part audit of the codebase plus the resulting cleanup. Audits ran across:
1. Unused deps / files / dead code
2. Duplicate or near-duplicate logic
3. CLAUDE.md trim
4. Files >100KB
5. Premature abstractions / wrappers
6. Middleware / route handlers

This PR applies every 🟢 finding from those audits and a couple of mechanical 🟡 wins. Riskier 🟡s (notably the tier/rate/bracket data-shape fossils, which need a DB migration) are deferred.

## Commits

1. **`01f11a8` Drop unused exports from `types.ts` schema constants** — 8 Zod schemas + `TIERS` were exported but only consumed via `z.infer<typeof X>` in the same file. Inferred types stay exported.
2. **`ee86440` `errorMessage` helper** — `err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'fallback'` appeared 18× across 13 files. Pure refactor.
3. **`f5c1d25` Modal extraction** — `EditDetailsDialog`, `HeadToHeadDialog`, `ShareDialog`, `ItemEditor` all reimplemented the same scaffolding (overlay, Escape, scroll-lock, aria-modal). Pulled into one `<Modal>` component. `LocalListsMigration` intentionally kept its bespoke shell (no Escape / backdrop dismiss is a feature, not a bug).
4. **`ca55c01` OG image frame + Supabase factory** — `og-list/route.tsx` and `share-card/route.tsx` shared dark theme, font, brand strip, footer, and anon-Supabase construction. Pulled into `src/app/api/_og/frame.tsx`.
5. **`032c012` Flatten dead wrappers** — `isCloudEnabled`/`hasSupabaseEnv` always returned true (since `52f105f` baked in defaults), making 8 guard branches unreachable. Plus: `useToast()` no-op fallback now throws instead of silently dropping toasts; `updateListPhase` was 2-line indirection over `updateListFields`; `uid()`'s `Math.random` fallback removed (Node 14.17+ and modern browsers all have `crypto.randomUUID`).
6. **`bc652c4` Remove `www.pairywise.com.har`** — 1.4 MB capture with no admin traffic and `access_token`/`refresh_token` strings in it. Added `*.har`, `*.log` to `.gitignore`. ⚠️ The blob is still in commit `a554239`'s history; if any of those tokens are still live, they should be rotated separately.
7. **`790b961` Strip AGENTS.md `BEGIN/END` markers** — decorative comments referenced nowhere.
8. **`8fe12e5` Drop the lists prefetch from root layout** — `bc00728`'s prefetch ran on every route, but only the home page's `CloudHydrator` consumed the data. Kept the cookie-reading `auth.getUser()` (that's what kills Vercel's static cache); dropped the 3-query lists fetch. Trade-off: home page now shows a brief "Loading your lists…" on first visit; admin/profile/signin/etc. load with three fewer Supabase queries on the critical path.
9. **`d4928b2` Fix misleading `getServerClient` comment** — said the proxy refreshes tokens; it doesn't.

## Test plan

## Summary

Closes #30. Retires the four v0.3 glassmorphic themes (`void-indigo`, `obsidian-violet`, `polar-slate`, `parchment-glow`) and ships two themes that mirror the public landing page palette (`compendiq-landing/src/styles/tokens.css`) for cross-surface brand parity:

- **Graphite Honey** (dark, default) — graphite `#121211` bg, warm cream `#f5efe0` text, brand honey `#f9c74f` accent
- **Honey Linen** (light) — near-neutral warm white `#f7f7f4` bg, near-black `#0a0a0a` text, same honey accent

## What's in the box

### Token system
- 11 new `nm-*` `@utility` classes (card / card-elevated / card-interactive / toolbar / sidebar / header / pill-active / button-primary / button-ghost / icon-button / input) replace the 14 retired `glass-*` utilities one-to-one.
- New tokens: `--color-primary-ink` (AA-safe darkened honey for accent-as-text on cream), per-language `--color-code-*` (bg/keyword/string/function/comment/number), 6 semantic `--color-status-*` (connected/syncing/embedding/ai/disconnected/inactive), 3-tier `--nm-*` shadow scale.
- All v0.4-era hardcoded Tailwind status colours (`text-green-400` / `bg-purple-500/20` etc.) lifted to semantic `--color-status-*` utilities so badges shift correctly between themes.

### Layout
- **Edge-to-edge flat chrome** — header, sidebar, right rail are full-width / full-height with hairline borders instead of floating rounded panels with margin gaps. Page bg shows through the chrome (`bg-background border-{b,r,l}`) so the article card stands out as the only major card on the page.
- **Article card + AI panes + KPI tiles + page list items + filters + editor toolbar** all use one consistent translucent recipe: `rounded-xl border border-border/40 bg-card/50 backdrop-blur-sm` for cross-route consistency.
- **Header height** bumped to 55px; brand horizontal lockup SVG (`compendiq-lockup-horizontal.svg`) replaces the inline icon + text combo.

### Editor
- **Sticky toolbar card** detached from article (25px gap), carries format buttons (when editor ready) on row 1, **tags + Cancel/Save inline** on row 2.
- **Under-mask layer** sits behind the toolbar at z-[-1] with `bg-background` reaching up past the AppLayout header — prevents the article from peeking through the toolbar's rounded corners during scroll without breaking `position: sticky`.

### Accessibility
- Hybrid neumorphism: every interactive surface has a 1px solid border (WCAG 1.4.11 — pure shadow-only borders are not a path to AA).
- `:focus-visible` honey ring with `outline-offset` so the ring doesn't merge with the surface shadow.
- `@media (forced-colors: active)` fallback restores `ButtonText` system borders so neumorphic chrome isn't invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode (`box-shadow` is zeroed there).
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` strips press-down `transform`/`box-shadow` transitions (Z-axis movement triggers vestibular discomfort).

### Migration
- Persisted theme preferences from any retired ID (`void-indigo`, `obsidian-violet`, `polar-slate`, `parchment-glow`, plus older legacy IDs `midnight-blue`, `cloud-white`, `catppuccin-mocha`, `ocean-depth`) silently fall back to `graphite-honey` via the existing `validateThemeId` path. **No data migration required.**
- Static `frontend/index.html` FOUC-prevention script updated: now boots with `data-theme="graphite-honey"` and only honours `graphite-honey` / `honey-linen` from localStorage.

- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm test -w frontend` — 1990 / 1990 passing
- [x] 42 new structural assertions in `frontend/src/neumorphic-themes.test.ts` cover palette anchors, status tokens, neumorphic shadow tokens, the eleven `nm-*` utilities, hybrid-border invariant, focus-visible presence, forced-colors fallback, prefers-reduced-motion override
- [x] New `e2e/themes.spec.ts` Playwright spec — theme-switch flow + screenshots
- [x] Manual visual smoke: both themes verified on Pages list, page view (read + edit modes), AI page, settings
- [ ] Tagging on `dev` → `main` requires founder sign-off per ADR

## Files changed

- 116 files — bulk class renames (`glass-*` → `nm-*`), token additions, badge refactors to semantic utilities, AppLayout edge-to-edge restructure, PageViewPage toolbar overhaul, ADR-010 amended

author: pycomet
body:
## Summary

Two coordinated workstreams against the CollectExperiencesAgent:

1. **UX regressions** reported during user testing — language stickiness, sequential date asking, stray prompt-template suffix in replies, education-phase orchestration bug, normalization running on every turn.
2. **Latency optimizations** to make the agent feel faster on cellular Kenya, where every saved millisecond matters.

Both ship together because they touch overlapping files and the latency fixes depend on the lazy-normalization mechanism added by the bug fixes.

---

## Part 1 — UX bug fixes

### 1. Language switch is now honored

**Bug:** Mid-conversation, when a Swahili-locale user asked *"please speak english"*, the agent refused (in Swahili) and only flipped after several turns of stochastic LLM drift.

**Root cause:** `prompt_template/locale_style.py:19` literally instructed the LLM *"If my previous message is in another language, do not respond in that language"*, plus the Swahili-specific block told it to keep replying in Kiswahili even when the user code-switched.

**Fix:** Rewrote the locale section to default to the active language but explicitly carve out an exception for explicit user switch requests. Disambiguated the Swahili block so casual code-switching ("Nina experience kama bank teller") doesn't trigger a switch — only an explicit request does.

**Verified:** i18n stack is already per-turn driven (`i18n_manager.get_locale()` reads `user_language_ctx_var`, set fresh every turn at `service.py:222`). No detector or middleware changes needed — prompt fix alone is sufficient.

### 2. Dates can now be asked together

**Bug:** Agent asked `start_date`, waited a turn, then asked `end_date`. Two turns to capture a date range.

**Root cause:** Both the work-type prompt (`_conversation_llm.py:425`) and the education prompt (`:627`) said *"Ask for exactly one missing field at a time"*.

**Fix:** Carved out a date-pair exception in both prompts. When both `start_date` and `end_date` are missing, agent asks *"When did you start, and when did you finish?"*. Partial answers still work — if user provides only one, the other is asked next turn under the existing one-field-at-a-time rule.

No schema or extraction changes — the data extraction LLM and temporal classifier already accept either or both dates per turn.

### 3. Stray *"experiences that include: …"* suffix is gone

**Bug:** Conversation LLM replies occasionally ended with truncated fragments like *"Ask me about experiences that include: u…"*, which read as prompt scaffolding leaking into user-visible output.

**Root cause:** Three layers contributed:
- The conversation LLM had **no `max_output_tokens` cap** at `_conversation_llm.py:233-236` and `:267-270`, so generation could be cut off mid-sentence.
- When truncation triggered, the LLM fell back to echoing instruction templates from the system prompt (line 832-833 *"Currently we are exploring work experiences that include:"*).
- **Architecturally**, the conversation LLM was the only major agent returning **free-form text** instead of a structured JSON response — nothing prevented it from echoing meta-instructions.

**Fix (three layers, defensive):**
- **A (architectural):** Added `ConversationLLMResponse` Pydantic schema. Conversation LLM now returns `{ "message_for_user": str }` constrained by `with_response_schema(...)`. Echoing meta-instructions into the message field is now structurally impossible.
- **B (defense):** Added `max_output_tokens: 2000` cap on both follow-up LLMConfigs.
- **C (cleanup):** De-templatized the leakable phrasings at `_conversation_llm.py:832-833` and `:891`.

The structured response parses with a defensive `try/except` in `_internal_execute()` — if the LLM ignores the schema, we fall back to raw text rather than crash.

### 4. Occupation normalization no longer fires on confirmation turns

**Bug:** Heavy `InferOccupationTool` (≈2 LLM calls per non-normalized experience) ran every turn during collection, including on plain "yes" replies — chewing latency for no reason. User's complaint: *"are we checking skills on every step and isn't that repeated?"*

**Root cause:** `_normalize_experience_titles()` was called unconditionally in `execute()` and the only guard skipped experiences whose title was already normalized. Failed normalizations silently retried every turn forever.

**Fix:**
- `_DataExtractionLLM.execute()` now returns a third tuple element: `list[str]` of UUIDs whose `experience_title` was newly set or changed this turn (computed by snapshotting titles before/after `_operations_processor.process()`).
- `_normalize_experience_titles()` accepts an optional `target_uuids` filter and only processes experiences in the set.
- Added per-experience attempt counter (`_normalization_attempts: dict[str, int]`, capped at 2) on the agent **instance** — deliberately **not** on `CollectExperiencesAgentState` so it doesn't leak into LLM prompts via `model_dump_json()` or persist to MongoDB.
- The full skill-linking pipeline (`linking_and_ranking_pipeline/`) was confirmed correct — only fires at LINKING_RANKING phase, never during collection.

Net effect: confirmation turns now make **zero** `InferOccupationTool` LLM calls. Normalization only fires when a title is genuinely new.

### 5. Education-phase orchestration bug

**Bug:** During education phase, the agent would sometimes prematurely jump to asking about self-employment after just one education entry — appending text like *"Have you had any experiences that include: running my own business…"* mid-education.

**Root cause:** `TransitionDecisionTool` evaluates against the first unexplored *work* type and is unaware of the education phase. When it incorrectly returned `END_WORKTYPE` after a single partial education entry, the `END_WORKTYPE` branch in `collect_experiences_agent.py:481` fired regardless of whether we were still in education. A pre-existing comment at lines 435-441 acknowledged the verdict was "unreliable" during education but the code didn't enforce it.

**Fix:** Coerce `END_WORKTYPE` and `END_CONVERSATION` verdicts from the transition tool to `CONTINUE` during education phase. Only the conversation LLM's `<END_OF_WORKTYPE>` signal can advance us out of education.

### 6. Bridge LLM replaces templated transition text

**Bug:** Even when the agent legitimately transitioned between work types, users saw the same hardcoded i18n template — *"Have you had any experiences that include: running my own business, doing freelance or contract work?"* — every time. Read like a mail merge form, especially on the 3-4 transitions per session.

**Root cause:** Hardcoded i18n template at `messages.json:askAboutType` was unconditionally appended by Python code at `collect_experiences_agent.py:511-520` (work-type transition) and `:453-456` (education exit). Static phrasing across all transitions.

**Fix:** New `_bridge_llm.py` module generates a single conversational sentence per transition, locale-aware, using `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`. On any failure (Vertex hiccup, schema mismatch, empty response), the agent falls back to the existing i18n template — so worst case is current behavior, never broken.

**Trade-off:** +400-800ms on transition turns only (3-4 per session). Non-transition turns unaffected. Worth it for the UX win.

---

## Part 2 — Latency optimizations

Inventory of per-turn cost (after Part 1 lands):
- **Cheap turn ("yes"/"ok"):** ~1.8s
- **Expensive turn (new title):** ~5.9s

The optimizations below targeted the biggest critical-path contributors.

### A. Parallelize normalization with conversation/transition

**Before:** `data extraction → normalize_experience_titles → asyncio.gather(conversation, transition) → bridge`
**After:**  `data extraction → asyncio.gather(normalize_experience_titles, conversation, transition) → bridge`

Normalization (~2.3s on expensive turns) now

## Summary
- Adds safe `ringline::fs::read_into(file, offset, BytesMut)` and `write_from(file, offset, BytesMut)` returning futures whose output is `(io::Result<usize>, BytesMut)`. Read appends into spare capacity; write returns the buffer unchanged.
- The existing unsafe raw-pointer `read`/`write` API is kept as the lower-level primitive — the safe API is a thin owned-buffer wrapper.
- A new per-executor `disk_io_graveyard: HashMap<u32, BytesMut>` keeps the buffer alive when the future is dropped before completion, so the kernel's pointer stays valid until the CQE arrives. On io_uring a best-effort `ASYNC_CANCEL` SQE is also submitted to speed up the completion; the mio backend just lets the worker thread finish.

body:
## Summary

Extracts the metadata-merge logic from `views/agents.py` into a tiny dedicated module so it can be mutation-tested in isolation. Wires the module into `[tool.mutmut].paths_to_mutate`. **All 8 mutants killed; `metadata_merge.py` reports 100% kill rate.**

## Why this is worth a mutmut slot

The `"" → delete` semantic mirrors Anthropic's metadata API and SDK clients depend on it to clear values. The original inline code in `views/agents.py` is the kind of compact branch a refactor can quietly drop (e.g. swap `if v == ""` for `if not v` and `0` / `False` / `None` silently start deleting too). Mutmut catches those.

## What changed

- New `src/agent_on_demand/metadata_merge.py` with one pure function `merge_metadata(current, patch)` returning a fresh dict. No DB, no Django — mutmut-friendly under hammett.
- `views/agents.py` calls the new function (existing comment expanded to point at the new module).
- 17 sync-only tests in `tests/test_metadata_merge.py`. Each isolates one mutmut-killable branch:
  - `dict(current)` copy (vs in-place mutation)
  - `for k, v in patch.items()` iteration source (vs `current.items()`)
  - `if v == ""` literal check (vs truthy / `is None` / `!= ""`)
  - `merged.pop(k, None)` default (vs `pop(k)` which would KeyError)
  - `merged[k] = v` assignment (vs setdefault / no-op)

author: hongmingwang-rabbit
body:
[Molecule-Platform-Evolvement-Manager]

## What was broken

\`canary-staging.yml\`'s teardown safety-net step filtered with \`f'e2e-{today}-canary-'\`. But \`test_staging_full_saas.sh\` emits canary slugs as \`e2e-canary-\${date}-\${RUN_ID_SUFFIX}\` — date SECOND, mode FIRST. Full-mode slugs are the other way around (\`e2e-\${date}-\${RUN_ID_SUFFIX}\`); the canary workflow seems to have been copy-pasted from there without re-checking the slug generator.

Net effect: the safety-net step ran on every cancelled / failed canary, hit the CP, got the org list, filtered to zero matches, and exited cleanly. Every cancelled canary EC2 leaked until the once-an-hour \`sweep-stale-e2e-orgs.yml\` cron eventually caught it (120-min default age threshold = ≥1h leak in the worst case).

## Today's incident

Canary run 24966995140 cancelled at 21:03Z. EC2 \`tenant-e2e-canary-20260426-canary-24966\` still running 1h25m later, terminated manually. Three earlier cancellations today (16:04Z, 19:26Z, 20:02Z) hit the same gap — visible as the canary failure cluster in #2090.

## Fix

- Filter prefix corrected to \`e2e-canary-\${today}-\` (mode FIRST, date SECOND) to match the actual slug emitter.
- Added per-run scoping (\`-canary-\${GITHUB_RUN_ID}\`) when \`GITHUB_RUN_ID\` is set, mirroring the e2e-staging-saas.yml safety net's per-run scoping (added after the 2026-04-21 cross-run cleanup incident).
- Inline comment block tracing the bug + prior incident so the next maintainer doesn't re-introduce the same copy-paste.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual trace: today's slug \`e2e-canary-20260426-canary-24966...\` matches the new \`e2e-canary-20260426-canary-24966\` prefix
- [x] YAML parses
- [ ] Next canary cancellation cleans up automatically

## Companion PR

The PRIMARY symptom (TLS-timeout failures, not the leaked EC2) traces to a separate bug in \`molecule-controlplane\`: tunnel/DNS creation errors are logged-and-continued rather than failing provision. CP PR coming separately.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Adds `resources/geoip.dat`, `resources/geosite.dat`, and `resources/wintun/**` to the repo so the upstream test/build workflows stop flaking on a cold GHA cache. ### Why Several upstream workflows (`test.yml`, `release-win7.yml`) restore from GHA caches keyed `xray-geodat-` and `xray-wintun-` that are populated by `scheduled-assets-update.yml`. The scheduled workflow has never run successfully on this fork, so both caches are empty, which causes: - `common/geodata`, `app/router`, `infra/conf` tests to panic with `failed to open geoip.dat / geosite.dat: no such file or directory` - `release-win7.yml` build steps to fail at `mv: cannot stat resources/geo*` and `mv: cannot stat resources/wintun/bin/amd64/wintun.dll` Manually dispatching the scheduled workflow requires `actions: write`, which the integration token I'm running under doesn't have (HTTP 403 from `gh workflow run`). Committing the files is the deterministic fix and is one of the options you outlined. ### What changed - `resources/geoip.dat` — sourced from `Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat` latest release (sha256 `b4120c88…063ccdf4`, ~19 MiB) - `resources/geosite.dat` — same source (sha256 `27f9ddad…e96a24d`, ~11 MiB) - `resources/wintun/{LICENSE.txt,bin/{amd64,x86,arm64,arm}/wintun.dll}` — extracted from `https://www.wintun.net/builds/wintun-0.14.1.zip`, which is exactly what `scheduled-assets-update.yml` fetches. - `.gitignore` — adds `!resources/*.dat` and `!resources/wintun/**/*.dll` exceptions below the existing `*.dat` and `*.dll` rules so future updates of those files are eligible to be tracked while ad-hoc `*.dat` / `*.dll` files elsewhere in the tree remain ignored. ### Verification Ran the previously-failing tests locally with go 1.26.0: ``` go test ./infra/conf/ -run TestGeodataConfig -> ok go test ./app/router/ -run TestChinaSites -> ok go test ./common/geodata/ -run TestIPMatcher4CN -> ok go test ./common/geodata/ -run TestCompactDomainMatcher_PreservesMixedRuleIndices -> ok ``` Wintun DLLs are binary blobs from upstream — verified via sha256 against the contents of the official zip. The win7 build job's only requirement is that the files exist at the expected paths. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] Decide whether you want geodata + wintun committed long-term, or whether you'd prefer to enable Actions write permission so `scheduled-assets-update.yml` can be dispatched and the cache approach can take over (in which case this PR can be reverted later). - [ ] If you keep things committed, consider whether you want the Loyalsoldier ruleset specifically (vs upstream `XTLS/Xray-core` releases that ship their own geodata). - [ ] Watch the win7 build logs after merge — if a future wintun release matters, you'll need to bump the file contents here (or finally enable Actions write so the scheduled job can take over). ### Notes - These files will appear in `git log` history at ~31 MiB total. That's a noticeable bump but acceptable for a normal git repo. - Future scheduled-assets-update runs (if/when you grant Actions write) will overwrite the in-cache copy, but the committed copies will still be there as a deterministic fallback. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7599c69b39d94140a5f5b2b8a0e73dc3 Requested by: @sevaktigranyan305-netizen ---

body:
PageSpeed-Lighthouse-Audit auf Mobile (Captured 2026-04-26 23:34) hat das "Mo wieder"-Element im Header-Status-Pill als Kontrast-Fail geflaggt — Barrierefreiheit fiel von 97 auf 96.

Ursache: Der Status-Text wurde in den kraeftigen Brand-Akzent-Farben gerendert:
  - text-brand-red-fire   (#d32f2f) auf bg-brand-black/90 → ~3.98:1
  - text-brand-green-leaf (#2e7d32) auf bg-brand-black/90 → ~3.87:1
WCAG-AA verlangt 4.5:1 fuer Normal-Text (auch fuer 12px-fett, weil das
unter dem "large text"-Threshold von 14pt-bold/18pt-regular liegt).
Beide Brand-Farben fielen unter die Schwelle. PageSpeed flagged nur den
roten Fall, weil zur Test-Zeit der Laden zu war — der gruene Fall wuerde
zu Oeffnungszeiten genauso scheitern.

Fix: Zwei neue "Soft"-Tokens fuer den Text-On-Dark-Use-Case:
  --color-brand-red-soft:   #ff7b7b  (~7.9:1, AAA)
  --color-brand-green-soft: #6dc873  (~9.6:1, AAA)

Header.astro setzt diese Soft-Varianten ueber `toneClass` ausschliesslich fuer den Status-TEXT. Die kraeftigen Brand-Farben bleiben unangetastet fuer den dekorativen Status-DOT (klein, aria-hidden, kein Text-Lesbar- keits-Threshold) und fuer alle anderen Use-Cases (Borders, Backgrounds, Iconfarben, Badges).

Pattern ist konsistent mit den bestehenden .badge-veg / .badge-spicy Utilities in global.css, die genau dasselbe Soft-Color-Schema fuer Text-on-Dark verwenden — also brand-konsistent, kein neuer Style.

Quality-Gates auf Astro 6.1.9:
- typecheck: 0 errors / 2 hints
- lint: clean
- vitest: 84/84
- astro build: 8 Seiten gebaut

body: ## Summary Fixes the `roi_creator` process failure (exit status 1) in the Nextflow neuroimaging pipeline. The pipeline was completing FreeSurfer and nifti_converter successfully but crashing at roi_creator, preventing CSV generation and all downstream processing. ### Root Cause: DooD Symlink Resolution In the Docker-out-of-Docker (DooD) pattern, Nextflow stages input files via symlinks in the work directory (`/tmp/nextflow_work/...`). The `ROI_labels.tsv` file was referenced from `/app/data/external/ROI_labels.tsv` — a path internal to the `nextflow_worker` container. When Nextflow spawned the `clinical-fsl` container, the symlink target didn't exist, causing bash `done < ${labels_file}` to fail with exit status 1. FreeSurfer/nifti_converter worked because their inputs were already on `/tmp` (shared filesystem via `-v /tmp:/tmp`). ### Additional Bugs Fixed 1. **`external/ROI_labels.tsv` — wrong format**: Had 2 columns (`Index`, `Label`) but `roi_creator` script and `inference_logic.R` expect 3 columns (`Index`, `FreeSurferLabel`, `Name`). Regenerated with correct FreeSurfer aparc+aseg atlas integer labels. 2. **`external/pyradiomics.yaml` — malformed YAML**: Missing colons after top-level keys. Fixed syntax. 3. **`nextflow_worker/dockerfile` — case sensitivity**: File was lowercase `dockerfile` but `docker-compose.yml` references `Dockerfile`. Fails on Linux (case-sensitive). ### Changes | File | Change | |------|--------| | `nextflow_worker/nextflow/nextflow.config` | `params.labels` fallback → `/tmp/ROI_labels.tsv` | | `docker-compose.yml` | `NF_LABELS` default → `/tmp/ROI_labels.tsv` | | `external/ROI_labels.tsv` | 3-column format with FreeSurfer atlas labels | | `external/pyradiomics.yaml` | Valid YAML syntax | | `nextflow_worker/data/external/pyradiomics.yaml` | Valid YAML syntax | | `nextflow_worker/dockerfile` → `Dockerfile` | Case-sensitive rename | ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify ROI_labels.tsv FreeSurfer labels**: Cross-check the integer labels (column 2) against your FreeSurfer aparc+aseg atlas. The labels I used are from the standard Desikan-Killiany atlas (FreeSurfer 7.x). If your version uses different label IDs, update accordingly. - [ ] **Verify DVC-tracked ROI_labels.tsv**: The file at `nextflow_worker/data/external/` is tracked by DVC. Run `dvc pull` before building Docker images to ensure the correct version is used. The file in `external/` is a reference copy. - [ ] **Re-run the pipeline end-to-end**: After `docker compose build && docker compose up`, submit a NIfTI file and verify that `roi_creator`, `csv_collector`, and `feature_extraction` all complete successfully. - [ ] **Check `radiomics_features.csv` output**: Verify the CSV is generated in `/shared_data/nf_output/` with the expected columns (78 ROIs × feature classes). ### Notes - The `path/to/license.txt` file contains your personal FreeSurfer license (email: `d.vernone17@gmail.com`). Consider removing it from the repository history and adding it to `.gitignore`. - The DVC remote is configured as a local path (`/mnt/disk1/boccuzzi/dvcstore`). Ensure this is accessible before running `dvc pull`. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0185f46ae9ba4ab8bfc0d023346a2f16 Requested by: @DomenicoVernone ---

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-88b63c4ee84fb41d1b925674941418ce866bb87b030711bfa6e14e69c7ad96e3L7-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-88b63c4ee84fb41d1b925674941418ce866bb87b030711bfa6e14e69c7ad96e3L161-R164)

The architectural perf release. **`Decoder[T]`** lands — typed, regex-bound unmarshaler that compiles its decode plan once and reuses it across calls.

Merging this PR fires `auto-tag.yml`: runs tests, pushes the `v0.5.0` tag, and publishes the GitHub Release in one workflow run (cascade fix verified in v0.3.2 / v0.4.0).

## What changed since v0.4.0

### Added
- `Compile[T]` / `MustCompile[T]` — strict compile-time validation of pattern + struct tags ([#69](https://github.com/Jecoms/regextra/pull/69))
- `Decoder[T].One` / `.All` ([#69](https://github.com/Jecoms/regextra/pull/69))
