author: mukundakatta
body:
Closes #1222.
Addresses #876.

## Why

Microsoft Edge users see a broken inspector layout while Chrome renders correctly (issue #1222 screenshots show the page squeezed/clipped on Edge). The same root cause is described in the older still-open #876, where an Edge user pinpointed `place-items: center` on `<body>` as the trigger and confirmed that removing it instantly restores normal full-width behavior.

There are two related Vite scaffold leftovers in `client/src/index.css` that bite on Edge but not Chrome:

1. `body { place-items: center }` — a no-op on a `display: block` body in most layouts, but Edge can interact with it (combined with `min-height: 100vh`) in a way that leaves the UI centered with empty margins.
2. No explicit height chain on `html`/`body`/`#root` — the App root uses Tailwind's `h-screen` (`height: 100vh`) and nested panes use `h-full`. On Edge these can collapse if the parent chain has no defined height, which makes the layout shift or clip.

## What

`client/src/index.css`:

- Drop `place-items: center` from `body`.
- Add `html, body, #root { height: 100%; width: 100% }` so `h-screen` / `h-full` resolve deterministically on Edge the same way they already do on Chrome.
- Comment explains why so we do not regress this later.

No JS/TS changes, no dependency changes, no new APIs.

## Tested

- Manually verified the inspector loads with full-width layout on Microsoft Edge (Chromium) on the symptoms reported in #1222 and #876.
- Verified Chrome still renders identically (no visual diff).
- `npm run build` in `client/` succeeds.

body:
## Sprint 3 of #26 — provenance + audit + critique + Drafting/Render

Single-handed (Pruthvi cut). All Sprint-3 acceptance items in #26 hit. Five phase commits — each independently green; final state has 177 / 177 tests passing.

### What landed

**New routes (deterministic + LLM)**

| Route | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/provenance` | Node runtime, no key required. Pure call into `lib/provenance/match`. Input `{ artifact, turns }` → `{ provenance, byline_pct }`. |
| `POST /api/audit` | Haiku 4.5 with structured tool output (`record_audit`). Stub fallback when no key. Same shape contract as the middleware. |

**Rewritten route (stub fallback preserved)**

| Route | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/draft/critique` | Sonnet 4.6 critic mode. SSE: one `event: card` per `record_critique_card` tool call (cliche / question / verified), then `event: done`. Stub mode unchanged — still returns `{ stub: true, cards }` JSON. Cache_control: ephemeral on system block. |

**New libs**

- `lib/provenance/match.ts` — pure deterministic matcher. Per artifact line: exact substring against user turns; if miss, per-word Levenshtein with ≤2 edit distance and a sliding window over the turn; otherwise `'none'`. Only `role: 'user'` turns count as sources. `byline_pct` = verified_words / total_words.
- `lib/interview/audit-middleware.ts` — `runAudit(message, guide, client)` calls Haiku 4.5 with the active guide's `audit_flags`. Default mode is log-only (`allow=true` even when flags fire); `process.env.AUDIT_BLOCK==="1"` promotes to blocking. Infra failures yield `allow=true` so an outage doesn't DoS the interview.

**Modified route**

- `app/api/interview/turn/route.ts` — wires `runAudit` after `finalMessage`. Flagged turns log warn; blocked turns emit an `audit_blocked` SSE frame and close the stream. Existing real-mode tests still pass — when the test mock leaves `messages.create` unimplemented, runAudit's catch-all returns `allow=true`.

**Components**

- `components/BylineMeter.tsx` — color band PLUS iconography (✓/◐/⚠) so it's not color-only. `aria-label` discloses the tier verbatim. Clamps pct to `[0, 100]`, rounds non-integers.
- `components/screens/Drafting.tsx` — split-A layout (left: textarea editor; right: streaming critique pane). Debounced fetch on user pause (600ms). Previous in-flight critique is aborted on each keystroke. Handles both stub-mode JSON and real-mode SSE responses. Persists draft to `state.artifact_text` so Render can read it.
- `components/screens/Render.tsx` — upgraded to fetch `/api/provenance` on mount when `artifact_text` + `turns` are present. Real provenance replaces the SCRIPT-driven `src → Q+A` mapping; the hover popover walks `turns[]` back one step from the source turn to find the original guide question. Falls back to the eulogy SCRIPT when no real artifact exists. Lines are keyboard-reachable via `tabIndex` with focus-driven hover. Postmark percentage now reflects live `byline_pct`. `BylineMeter` rendered alongside the wax seal.

**Store**

- `lib/store.ts` — adds `AppState.artifact_text` + `setArtifactText` action. PersistedSchema extended with `default("")` so existing v1 localStorage upgrades cleanly. Drafting writes; Render reads.

**App wiring**

- `components/App.tsx` — `step === "drafting"` now routes to `Drafting`.

### Tests — 65 new across this PR

| Suite | Cases |
|---|---|
| `tests/lib/provenance-match.test.ts` | 10 — exact / fuzzy / none / blank lines / empty / mixed pct / guide-turn exclusion / whitespace preservation |
| `tests/api/provenance.test.ts` | 5 — happy path / malformed body / non-JSON / empty turns / optional Turn fields |
| `tests/lib/audit-middleware.test.ts` | 5 — clean / log-only flagged / `AUDIT_BLOCK=1` flagged blocks / `AUDIT_BLOCK=1` clean still allows / infra failure → allow=true |
| `tests/api/audit.test.ts` | 6 — stub mode / clean / flagged / 404 / 400 malformed / 400 non-JSON |
| `tests/api/draft-critique-real.test.ts` | 5 — three-card streaming / invalid tool input dropped / no tool calls still emits done / 404 / SDK error → error frame |
| `tests/components/BylineMeter.test.ts` | 8 — each tier / clamping / rounding / aria-label tier disclosure / lines count / no-lines mode |
| `tests/lib/store.test.ts` | +1 — `setArtifactText` |
| `tests/api/draft-critique.test.ts` | hardened — file-scoped SDK mock prevents the BYO-key-leak test from making real Anthropic calls now that BYO triggers real-mode |

### Acceptance items (#26 § Sprint 3)

- [x] `lib/provenance/match.ts` — exact + Levenshtein fallback (≤2 edit distance per word). Pure.
- [x] `POST /api/provenance` — Node runtime, deterministic.
- [x] `POST /api/audit` — Haiku 4.5 flag-driven.
- [x] `lib/interview/audit-middleware.ts` — log-only by default, `AUDIT_BLOCK=1` promotes to blocking.
- [x] Wraps `/api/interview/turn`.
- [x] `POST /api/draft/critique` rewritten — Sonnet 4.6, 3 buckets, streaming, stub fallback.
- [x] `components/screens/Drafting.tsx` — split editor + streaming critique.
- [x] `components/screens/Render.tsx` upgraded — consumes real `provenance[]`.
- [x] `components/BylineMeter.tsx` — green / yellow / red + iconography (NOT color-only); WCAG AA focus indicators.
- [x] Tests: matcher coverage, audit middleware log-vs-block, critique stub→real swap.

### Notes
- Critique's "card-by-card" streaming is implemented via `finalMessage` rather than per-`contentBlock` events — cards are emitted in a single burst at end of stream rather than as Sonnet generates each tool call. The UX difference is small (~1-2s) and the test surface is much simpler. If we want true per-card streaming, switch to `ms.on('contentBlock', ...)` later.
- `AUDIT_BLOCK` blocking happens AFTER deltas have already streamed (audit runs on `finalMessage`). The route emits `audit_blocked` so the frontend can dim/warn; it can't unstream the text. Documented limitation.

### Gates

```
tsc --noEmit               ✓
vitest run                 177 / 177 across 22 files
next lint                  ✓
next build                 ✓ (production build, all routes resolved)
```

Refs #26 (Sprint 3 of three; Sprint 4 lands on `feat/sprint-4-guide-share` per the PR strategy in the issue body).

## Summary

Phase B design + ADR for issue #340 — the packaged React/Tailwind+shadcn web dashboard served at `/dashboard` from the existing daemon HTTP server, launched via a new `claude-tempo dashboard` CLI verb. Builds on Phase A research (PR #341) and the canonical Claude Design bundle in `docs/design/dashboard-handoff/` (PR #345).

- `docs/design/340-web-dashboard.md` — full design (14 sections, repo layout, daemon serving, design-token mapping, scope cut, build pipeline, test strategy, decision log)
- `docs/adr/0013-web-dashboard.md` — decision record
- `docs/adr/README.md` — index entry for 0013

## Locked decisions on the 10 open questions

| Q | Decision |
|---|---|
| Q1 Repo layout | Sibling `dashboard/` dir (mirrors Mink); NOT a separately-versioned sub-package |
| Q2 Build orchestration | In default `npm run build`; +30s cap; lazy fallback if exceeded |
| Q3 Hot reload | Vite dev server with `server.proxy` to daemon |
| Q4 Pairing-token shape | Opaque base64url 32-byte random; 5-min TTL; single-use; in-memory map |
| Q5 State management | **TanStack Query** (server) + **Zustand** (prefs); NO Redux |
| Q6 Versioning | Lockstep with root; CI enforced |
| Q7 v1 functional cut | **All 9 screens render**; only safe writes wired; destructive disabled-with-tooltip showing v2 roadmap |
| Q8 Browser support | Last 2 evergreen; Safari ≥16; no IE |
| Q9 Lighthouse / a11y | Targets 85/90/90; CI=size-limit only; Lighthouse=release-checklist |
| Q10 Reference-fork story | `dashboard/README.md` with explicit fork-and-customize guide |

## Wire surface — strictly additive

**Zero new Temporal signals / queries / updates.** Daemon-side adds:
- 1 new file: `src/http/dashboard.ts` (~80 LoC) for static + SPA fallback at `/dashboard/*`
- 2 new endpoints under `/dashboard/api/*` for QR-code cross-device pairing (POST `/pair` + GET `/pair/:token`)
- Reuses all existing `/v1/*` snapshot + SSE endpoints (PRs #320, #324, #325)

The dashboard is a thin client over `TempoClient.subscribe()` — new tools and surfaces light up automatically as `TempoClient` grows.

## Visual design — pulled from canonical bundle

Per `docs/design/dashboard-handoff/HANDOFF-NOTE.md`: implementer recreates pixel-perfectly from the bundle's HTML/CSS/JSX. Design §8 maps every CSS variable in `dashboard-handoff/styles.css` into the shadcn theme schema (`--accent` → `--primary`, `--bg` → `--background`, `--rule` → `--border`, …). Custom tempo motifs (Metronome, TempoStrip, PhaseDot, PlayerAvatar, TypeBadge, Brandmark) ported verbatim to `dashboard/src/components/tempo/`.

## v1 scope

**All 9 screens render** (Workspace, Player Detail, Overview, Recruit, Create Ensemble, Loadouts, Player Types, Schedules, Hosts). Read paths fully wired. **Safe writes** (cue, report, release, play, pause, recruit) wired in v1. **Destructive verbs** (destroy, restart, restore, shutdown), schedule edit, lineup edit, gates, worktrees → **disabled with `Coming in v2` tooltip**. Visible-but-disabled deliberately, so the v2 roadmap is on-screen.

## Bundle budget

≤1 MB gzip-on-wire / ≤3 MB unpacked for the dashboard portion. **Enforced by `size-limit` in CI**; hard fail if exceeded. Static assets shipped via `package.json#files` — **NO postinstall build** (Mink's known support black hole).

## Sequencing

- **Hard prerequisite**: PR-4 (#94/#95 Phase 3 TUI cutover) merged + 48h soak elapsed
- **Independent of**: #318 coat-check, #319 protobuf, #131 claude-api adapter
- **Composes naturally with**: #334 saveable-state (just landed) — v2 can surface "saved state" badge per player
- **eng-2 named as natural implementer** post-#329 TempoClient split (context fresh)
- **Single large PR** (~3,100-4,740 LoC) **or 3 sequenced PRs**:
  - PR-A: scaffolding + tokens + shell + plumbing (~1,000 LoC)
  - PR-B: 9 screens read paths + routing + SSE bridge (~1,800 LoC)
  - PR-C: safe-write wiring + pairing + CLI + daemon handler + tests (~1,000 LoC)

## Test plan

- [ ] qa-2 review: design correctness, token mapping table, scope cut rationale, ADR alignment
- [ ] Verify no breaking changes (all wire additions optional; old payloads unchanged)
- [ ] Confirm ADR 0013 number is correct (0012 just landed via #344)
- [ ] Confirm cross-references between design doc, ADR, Phase A research, and design bundle are accurate
- [ ] Sanity-check the design-token mapping against `dashboard-handoff/styles.css`
- [ ] Confirm the 3-PR sequencing is realistic given eng-2's bandwidth

- Issue #340 — original proposal with 6 design-space areas, sequencing, acceptance criteria
- PR #341 — Phase A research (`docs/research/340-web-dashboard-alternatives.md`)
- PR #345 — design bundle (`docs/design/dashboard-handoff/`)

body:
**Title:** Single-source changelog: lift version modal data into helper.js

---

## Summary

The version modal pulled its content from `/api/version-info` (a 295-line hand-curated Python dict in `web_server.py`); the "What's New" panel pulled from `WHATS_NEW` in `helper.js`. Same release notes, two files, two languages, hand-edited at every release — drift was inevitable (and was already happening on the 2.4.0 entries).

This branch makes `helper.js` the single editing surface and trims a bunch of dead code while we're in there.

## Commits

1. **Delete dead historical changelog strings** (`edb2c20`) — `_OLD_V22_NOTES` (655 lines) and `_OLD_V2_NOTES` (556 lines) were triple-quoted Python strings holding old release-notes JSON. Zero references in the codebase. Pure deletion, no behavior change.

2. **Lift version modal data into helper.js, delete `/api/version-info`** (`7714b51`) —
   - Adds `VERSION_MODAL_SECTIONS` const in `helper.js` next to `WHATS_NEW`, with a comment block documenting the relationship and release-time workflow.
   - Rewires `showVersionInfo()` in `downloads.js` to read from those consts directly (no backend round-trip).
   - Deletes the route + the 295-line `version_data` dict.

3. **Rewrite changelog entries in user voice** (`04ff287`) — trimmed all 27 `WHATS_NEW '2.4.0'` entries and all 23 `VERSION_MODAL_SECTIONS` from diagnostic-paragraph style into terse 1-2 sentence descriptions, 3-7 short bullets per modal section. Stripped parenthetical credits from titles.

## Net

- `web_server.py`: **-1,508 lines** (1,213 dead strings + 295 endpoint/dict).
- `helper.js`: +291 net (modal data lifted in, then trimmed by the voice rewrite).
- `downloads.js`: -35 (no more fetch boilerplate).

## Notes for review

- This is **collocation, not full unification**. `WHATS_NEW` and `VERSION_MODAL_SECTIONS` are still two distinct structures with overlapping content, linked by a comment convention rather than a shared schema. A deeper refactor (e.g. a `featured` flag on entries) was out of scope — the modal sections aren't all 1:1 mappable to `WHATS_NEW` entries (some are aggregator sections like "Recent Fixes"). Documented in the commit body as a possible follow-up if drift returns.
- Defensive `typeof !== 'undefined'` checks in `showVersionInfo` are belt-and-suspenders — load order rules out the actual race (helper.js is line 7967, downloads.js is 7873; both classic synchronous scripts; modal only opens on user click).

author: poyrazk
body:
## Summary
- Bounded memory hash join: process right table in 1024-row chunks instead of loading all at once
- LEFT join support with unmatched row emission
- State machine: LoadLeftBuffer → BuildRightChunk → ProbeChunk → EmitUnmatched → Done
- Fix INNER join cross-chunk deduplication (set matched flag for both join types)
- All left rows buffered for repeated probing across chunks

## Technical Details

### Memory Bounds
- `RIGHT_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024` limits right-side memory usage
- `left_rows_buffer_` holds all left rows (loaded once, probed against every chunk)

### State Machine
1. **LoadLeftBuffer**: Load all left rows into `left_rows_buffer_`
2. **BuildRightChunk**: Load next 1024-row chunk from right into hash buckets
3. **ProbeChunk**: Probe all buffered left rows against current chunk
4. **EmitUnmatched** (LEFT only): Emit left rows that found no match with NULLs for right columns
5. **Done**: All chunks processed

### Bug Fix
The `left_row_matched_[left_idx]` flag is now set for BOTH join types after the first match is found. This prevents the same left row from being re-emitted when it matches in a subsequent chunk's bucket.

Pull Request Description — PR #4
Title: feat(ingestion): Phase 1 data ingestion module — Anthropic Admin API

Base: develop ← Compare: feature/ingestion

Tier 3 — async spot check.

Summary
Implements the complete Phase 1 data ingestion layer. Fetches daily usage and cost data from the Anthropic Admin API, handles pagination and retry automatically, and schedules regular runs using node-cron. No writes to Supabase yet — that is the storage PR. No external API calls are made at test time.

What was built
[src/ingestion/types.ts](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/src/ingestion/types.ts) — TypeScript interfaces for all request/response shapes: UsageBucket, UsageReportResponse, CostRecord, CostReportResponse, ParsedCostRecord, IngestionType.

[src/ingestion/http-client.ts](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/src/ingestion/http-client.ts) — anthropicFetch(): shared fetch wrapper with exponential backoff (baseDelayMs × 2^attempt) on 429 and 5xx. Configurable maxRetries (default 3), baseDelayMs (1 s), timeoutMs (30 s). Logs HTTP status and path on every call — never the API key value. Throws ApiError(critical) on exhausted retries or non-retryable 4xx. sleepFn is injectable for zero-delay testing.

[src/ingestion/anthropic-usage.ts](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/src/ingestion/anthropic-usage.ts) — Calls GET /v1/organizations/usage_report/messages with bucket_width=1d for a rolling 30-day window. Paginates automatically via after_id cursor. Groups results by model:workspace key. Throws ValidationError on malformed response shape.

[src/ingestion/anthropic-costs.ts](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/src/ingestion/anthropic-costs.ts) — Calls GET /v1/organizations/cost_report. Auto-paginates. Parses the description field to extract model and feature context (e.g. "claude-3-haiku-20240307 prompt cache write" → model: "claude-3-haiku-20240307", feature: "prompt cache write"). Throws ValidationError on malformed response.

[src/ingestion/scheduler.ts](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/src/ingestion/scheduler.ts) — Two cron jobs: usage every hour (0 * * * *), costs daily at 02:00 (0 2 * * *). Guards against duplicate runs via IngestionStateStore interface (55-minute minimum for usage, 23-hour for costs). The store interface is injected — the Supabase implementation is wired in the storage PR. Alerting destination is ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL env var — no hardcoded target.

[tests/ingestion/](vscode-webview://0p0m2bic0kn1jl5l5dl0h77b5al2tvl6vutdikj46gk3fiht5kvh/tests/ingestion/) — 50 new tests (77 total across the project), all passing:

retry-backoff.test.ts (12): retry on 429/5xx, no-retry on 4xx, exponential delay verification, network error handling
pagination-handler.test.ts (7): single-page, multi-page concatenation, cursor passing, defensive stop on null cursor
deduplication.test.ts (10): first-run, within-interval skip, beyond-interval run, correct IngestionType passed, cron expressions verified
error-handling.test.ts (21): ValidationError on malformed responses, parseDescription edge cases, parseCostRecord enrichment, groupByModelAndWorkspace key logic
Alerting architecture — formal sign-off requested
This note was requested by the build specification.

The scheduler's alerting webhook uses ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL (environment variable). The original design referenced n8n as the delivery layer. Following an options appraisal in Session 2, Microsoft Teams webhook was selected as the initial target — it is already available via the Microsoft 365 MCP connection and requires no additional infrastructure. The module remains destination-agnostic: the webhook URL is read from the environment variable at runtime, with no hardcoded target in code. n8n will be introduced as a routing layer only when multi-destination alerting is confirmed as a requirement (cost/budget alerts to Stuart Rae, security alerts to Duncan MacLean, operational alerts to David Hamilton).

TDA approval of this PR constitutes formal sign-off on the alerting architecture change.
Ref: CF02, CF03 — carried-forward actions register.

API endpoint paths — GET /v1/organizations/usage_report/messages and GET /v1/organizations/cost_report are the paths specified in the build brief. These should be verified against the current Anthropic Admin API reference before the first deployment, as field names and pagination conventions may differ by API version.

parseDescription regex — matches claude- followed by alphanumeric-hyphen segments. This handles all current Anthropic model naming patterns. If Anthropic introduces a model name not starting with claude-, model and feature will both be null — a safe fallback.

author: joeykrug
body:
## Summary

Default the memory-core SQLite index database to `journal_mode=WAL` with
`synchronous=NORMAL`. This significantly reduces read/write contention
as the index grows — particularly noticeable on databases >100MB where
concurrent sync operations and search queries currently serialize on
the rollback journal.

## Change

Three lines in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-db.ts`:

```diff
 db.exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000");
+db.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL");
+db.exec("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL");
 return db;
```

## Why these defaults

- **WAL** lets readers and writers proceed concurrently without blocking
  each other. The memory index is exactly this kind of workload — sync
  ops (index updates) and search queries can overlap freely.
- **synchronous = NORMAL** is the recommended pairing for WAL.
  Sufficient durability for a rebuildable index without the
  per-transaction fsync overhead of FULL.
- **busy_timeout retained** — WAL does not eliminate writer-vs-writer
  contention (SQLite still serializes writers even in WAL mode), so
  the existing 5s retry-on-busy is still useful.

## Compatibility

- WAL is fully transparent to application code. No behavior change for
  any existing safe-path caller of `openMemoryDatabaseAtPath`.
- WAL mode is **per-database** and **persistent** — once set, subsequent
  opens (including by other tools, e.g. `sqlite3` CLI) use WAL until
  explicitly switched. Setting WAL on every open is idempotent.
- WAL adds two sidecar files: `<db>-wal` and `<db>-shm`. These live
  next to the DB and are managed by SQLite. Backup/restore tooling
  that copies the index DB should also copy these (or use `.backup`).
- WAL does not work over network filesystems (NFS/SMB) without
  `disable_mmap`. memory-core is local-only by design — no expected impact.

## Relation to prior PRs

- **#51986** (open) — proposes the same WAL change but ALSO removes
  `busy_timeout`. This PR is strictly additive (busy_timeout retained)
  to avoid regression on writer-vs-writer contention.
- **#36535** (closed) — earlier WAL attempt.

## Verification

- All existing tests pass (`pnpm --filter '@openclaw/memory-core' test`).
- Manually verified on a 1.7GB production memory-core DB: switching to
  WAL+NORMAL eliminated multi-second read latency during concurrent
  sync ops.

## Notes for reviewers

- The fix is intentionally narrow. If you'd prefer a config option
  (`store.journalMode`), happy to add that — but defaulting to WAL
  seems strictly better for the typical user.
- No `.changeset/*.md` added — please advise if one is required for
  this category of change.

## Problem

Without an explicit `limit`, `sync_journal` returned every item in the journal. On large journals with big content items this produces responses that overflow MCP tool-output buffers, making foray effectively unusable in practice.

## Change

Introduce `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 30`. When the caller omits `limit`, the server now returns at most 30 items per call. Callers that need more items pass an explicit `limit` or paginate with `cursor`. The hard cap of 500 (`MAX_LIMIT`) is unchanged.

## Also updated
- Tool description and `limit` param doc comment mention the new default
- `doc/blueprint.md` pagination cap note updated

## Tests
Two new tests:
- Omitting `limit` on a 35-item journal returns exactly `DEFAULT_LIMIT` items
- Explicit `limit` overrides the default

author: sunrisepeak
body:
## Summary

`xlings remove <pkg>` now prompts for confirmation before destructive uninstall and prints richer information about *what* is being removed.

### Before
- No prompt — typing `xlings remove gcc` goes straight to uninstall.
- Output: `gcc removed` (no version, no subos).

### After
- A plan panel is printed first:
  ```
    Package to remove:

      ◆ xim:gcc@15.1.0  (subos: default)
  ```
- A confirmation prompt with default **n** (uninstall is destructive — matches apt/dnf convention):
  ```
   ▸ Remove xim:gcc@15.1.0 from subos 'default' ?[y/N]
  ```
- Summary now includes subos + version:
  ```
    ✓ xim:gcc@15.1.0 removed  (subos: default)
  ```
- The existing global `-y` / `--yes` flag bypasses the prompt — same UX as `install`.

### Internal: hook-driven recursive removes stay silent
xpkgs can emit `pkgmanager.remove(...)` from their install hooks (e.g. `rust-crates-mirror.lua` cleans an old version when installing a new one). Those connected uninstalls now pass `yes=true` — the user already approved the parent install, no extra prompt.

### Resolve-active-version fix
The pre-resolve step uses `xvm::get_active_version` when the user did not pin a version. `catalog.resolve_target`'s default is the highest *declared* version, which would mis-report "not installed" when only an older active version is on disk (caught by the existing `remove_multi_version` e2e scenario 3).

## Files changed
- `src/core/xim/commands.cppm` — new `yes` parameter, plan event, prompt, active-version resolve.
- `src/cli.cppm` — pass `-y` through, handle `remove_plan` event.
- `src/capabilities.cppm` — accept `"yes": bool` in `remove_package` capability schema.
- `src/ui/info_panel.cppm` — `print_remove_plan` and updated `print_remove_summary` signature.
- `tests/e2e/subos_payload_refcount_test.sh` — add `-y` (relied on old no-prompt behavior).

## Test plan
- [x] `xmake build xlings` — passes
- [x] `xmake run xlings_tests` — 184 passed, 4 unrelated skipped
- [x] `tests/e2e/remove_multi_version_test.sh` — passes (covers active-version resolve fix in S3)
- [x] `tests/e2e/subos_payload_refcount_test.sh` — passes after `-y` update
- [x] `tests/e2e/script_type_install_test.sh` — passes (output shows the new summary line)
- [x] `tests/e2e/legacy_config_test.sh` / `sub_index_install_test.sh` — passes
- [x] Manual: piping `n` to `xlings remove <pkg>` cancels and prints `cancelled`; default-no-input also cancels via the `-n` default.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent duplicate orders and improve reliability by introducing real idempotency protection for order creation. 
- Reduce security risk of persistent access tokens by removing long-lived tokens from `localStorage` and using short-lived `sessionStorage` entries with TTL and migration for recent legacy tokens. 
- Capture the overall prioritized implementation plan (P0/P1/P2) for further hardening steps and sequencing. 

### Description
- Require and pass an `idempotencyKey` through `InsertOrderPayload` and into the `place_order` RPC, and validate presence in `src/hooks/useOrders.ts` to avoid double submissions. 
- Generate and use the order id as the idempotency key on checkout, and persist returned access tokens in `sessionStorage` with an expiry TTL instead of `localStorage` in `src/pages/Checkout.tsx`. 
- Replace legacy `localStorage`-based recent-order handling with `sessionStorage` in `src/pages/OrderStatus.tsx`, add parsing/validation helpers, and migrate recent legacy tokens into session storage while cleaning up `localStorage`. 
- Add a new document `docs/prioritized-implementation-plan.md` outlining P0/P1/P2 tasks and sequencing, focusing on security/reliability/performance without UI changes. 

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) against the modified code and no type errors were reported. 
- Performed a local dev build (`yarn build`) and application startup smoke checks which completed without build-time errors. 
- Executed the existing automated unit test suite (`yarn test`) and the tests passed.

### Motivation
- Evitar crashes do metadata_worker causados por profile do Chrome lockado ou corrompido ao iniciar o Chrome.
- Fornecer um modo padrão com profile persistente para manter login salvo e um fallback automático para profile temporário quando houver falha.

### Description
- Atualiza `services/product_metadata_browser.py` para resolver o diretório de profile com prioridade: `METADATA_CHROME_PROFILE_DIR` (se setada) e, caso contrário, um default fixo `C:\projetos\afiliados-mvp\data\chrome_profile_metadata` usando `_resolve_metadata_profile_dir`.
- Antes de iniciar, lista processos Chrome em execução (`tasklist` / `pgrep -a chrome`) e loga o resultado para diagnóstico usando `_list_running_chrome_processes`.
- Remove automaticamente arquivos/dirs de lock do profile persistente (`SingletonLock`, `SingletonCookie`, `SingletonSocket`) com `_remove_profile_locks` e loga o que foi removido.
- Implementa tentativa em dois estágios: tenta iniciar com o profile persistente e, se ocorrer exceção, cria um profile temporário via `tempfile.mkdtemp` e reinicia o driver; logs claros indicam cada passo e a exceção original é logada.
- Ao usar profile temporário, imprime para o terminal: `Faça login novamente no Mercado Livre pois este profile é temporário`.
- Mudança isolada apenas em `services/product_metadata_browser.py`; não altera `remote_worker.py` nem o fluxo de geração de link.

body:
## Summary

**Phase 04: Session Indexer**
**Goal:** Every Claude Code and Codex session on the machine is indexed into SQLite and attributed to a project where possible.
**Status:** Verified: 12/12 must-haves passed

This phase adds metadata-only Claude Code and Codex session indexing end to end: SQLite session schema and repositories, tolerant JSONL metadata parsers, byte-offset incremental parsing with live partial handling, fixed-root Tauri indexing commands/events, rebuild-cache rematching, portfolio session aggregates, project card sparklines, unmatched-session rail data, and a manual indexing progress UI.

## Changes

### Plan 04-01: Session Repository Foundation
- Added metadata-only `sessions` and `session_index_state` tables with query indexes.
- Added transactional repository helpers for upsert, offset state, rematching, and portfolio aggregates.
- Added repository and migration tests.

### Plan 04-02: Parser, Streaming, and Attribution
- Added Claude and Codex metadata parsers over `serde_json::Value`.
- Added complete-line JSONL streaming with byte-offset accounting and live-partial tolerance.
- Added project attribution from parsed `cwd` and Claude encoded path fallback.
- Fixed incremental appended-file handling by merging deltas into existing session rows.

### Plan 04-03: Tauri Command and Events
- Added `index_sessions` command over fixed `~/.claude/projects` and `~/.codex/sessions` roots.
- Added metadata-only `SessionIndexEvent` progress events.
- Registered command metadata, generated permission, and release capability.
- Rematches unmatched sessions after cache rebuilds.

### Plan 04-04: Portfolio UI
- Exposed session totals, token totals, seven-day sparklines, and unmatched session summaries in portfolio DTOs.
- Added typed frontend `indexSessions` IPC and progress panel.
- Rendered project card session sparklines and unmatched-session right rail.

## Requirements Addressed

- SESS-01: Claude Code session metadata indexing
- SESS-02: Codex session metadata indexing
- SESS-03: Partial JSONL tolerance and byte-offset incremental parsing
- SESS-04: Claude project attribution by encoded directory path
- SESS-05: Codex `cwd` attribution and unmatched/global retention
- SESS-06: SQLite session persistence and query indexes
- PORT-02: Seven-day session sparkline on portfolio cards

## Verification

- [x] Phase verification passed: `.planning/phases/04-session-indexer/04-VERIFICATION.md`
- [x] Code review clean: `.planning/phases/04-session-indexer/04-REVIEW.md`
- [x] `cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`
- [x] `npm test -- --run`
- [x] Schema drift check clean

## Key Decisions

- Session rows remain metadata-only; no prompt, transcript, content, tool-call JSON, or FTS columns.
- Offset state advances in the same transaction as session upserts.
- Live trailing partial JSONL is reported as `Live session still writing` and left unconsumed.
- Claude path fallback compares encoded directory names against known roots rather than trusting decoded paths as filesystem targets.
- `index_sessions` accepts no frontend path input; roots are derived from app state.
- Session progress events carry source/path/count metadata only.
- Portfolio session stats read from SQLite aggregates, and sparklines use fixed CSS bars rather than a chart dependency.

## Notes

Security enforcement is enabled and no Phase 04 security report exists yet. Run `$gsd-secure-phase 04` before merging if you want the GSD security gate artifact attached to this phase.

author: tonychen06
body:
`Signal.pad` already computes a `padding_mask` for records shorter than `--segment_len`, but the MAE-family pretrain task transform drops it on the floor. As a result, when records are padded, the all-zero padded patches:

1. Get patchified alongside real cardiac signal patches.
2. Get randomly chosen as masked targets by the MAE objective.
3. Contribute trivially-low MSE to the loss (predicting zero from a sep + lead + positional embedding is essentially free).

This biases the loss downward and inflates apparent convergence on any dataset with variable-length records.

This PR plumbs `padding_mask` from the data pipeline through to `forward_loss`, where it's converted to a per-time-patch validity flag (a patch is "padded" if any of its samples is padding) and zeroed out of the random masking mask before the loss reduction.

- `js-base64` → `toUint8Array` для декодирования адреса
- `chain: "solana:mainnet"` в authorize
- Без `QueryClientProvider` (вызывает краш)
- Каждый свап через Seed Vault (биометрия)

**Экраны:**
- **Swap Queue** — "Start Daily Session", очередь с таймером, статус каждого свапа
- **Statistics** — сегодня/всего/газ/объём, средние значения
- **SCR Token** — покупка SCR через Jupiter, баланс SOL/SCR
- **Settings** — свапы/день (50–100), бюджет, уведомления, фоновый режим

**Сервисы:**
- Jupiter API v6 (quote + swap)
- AsyncStorage для настроек и статистики
- expo-notifications для алертов
- expo-background-fetch + task-manager

**Стек:** React Native, Expo SDK 54, TypeScript, @solana-mobile/mobile-wallet-adapter-protocol-web3js v2.2.x, @solana/web3.js v1.x, Jupiter API v6

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Установить на Seeker Phone: `npm install && npx expo prebuild && npx expo run:android`
- [ ] Проверить подключение Seed Vault (кнопка "Connect Wallet")

- [ ] Проверить что каждый свап запрашивает биометрию через Seed Vault
- [ ] Проверить что рандомизация работает (разные суммы, пары, задержки)

### Notes

- Приложение требует устройство Seeker Phone с Seed Vault для подписи транзакций
- TypeScript компиляция проходит без ошибок (`npx tsc --noEmit`)

body:
﻿## What

Adds three files under `convex/domains/agents/lessons/` that close the learning loop for the `agentLessons` table introduced in A-PR-A.1:

### 1. `captureLesson.ts`

One `internalMutation` per lesson type so callers cannot mix fields incorrectly:

- `captureSemanticLesson` — post-rollback (mistake/correct/artifact pattern)
- `captureInfrastructureLesson` — post-failover; **folds duplicates** by incrementing `count` when `(threadId, fromModel, toModel)` already exists
- `captureBudgetLesson` — post-cap (taskCategory + estimated tokens remaining)
- `captureSpiralLesson` — post-loop (mistakePattern + correctPattern + toolName)
- `deprecateLesson` and `pinLesson` for the LessonsPanel UI in A-PR-B.7

### 2. `getRelevantLessons.ts`

`internalQuery` returning the top-K relevant lessons for a thread.

- Pinned lessons bypass the K cap
- Scoring: tool match (+1000), infrastructure `count` (capped +100), success bonus (+5), recency penalty (up to −60)
- HONEST_STATUS: returns `[]` when no lessons exist; skips deprecated and expired silently
- Plus `listAllLessonsForThread` for the audit panel

### 3. `systemPromptBuilder.ts`

Pure utility (no Convex, no I/O) rendering an array of lessons into a markdown system-prompt prefix:

- Groups by type (`semantic` → `spiral` → `infrastructure` → `budget`)
- 📌 emoji prefix for pinned lessons
- 8 KB byte ceiling with non-pinned tail-drop when over budget; pins kept regardless
- `injectLessonsIntoSystemPrompt` helper for the agent runtime to concatenate before the model's existing prompt

## Why

A-PR-A.1 added the schema. This PR adds the read/write/render trio so the agent runtime can:
1. **Capture** lessons after every rollback / failover / spiral / budget event.
2. **Query** the most relevant lessons before each turn.
3. **Inject** them verbatim into the system prompt so the model literally cannot ignore the captured pattern without explicit deprecation.

Without this trio, the `agentLessons` schema is dead weight.

## Scope discipline

- Per-thread isolation in v1; cross-thread guardrails deferred.
- No callers wire this in yet — the rollback action (A-PR-A.3) and model router (B-PR4) get capture wiring in a follow-up.
- The agent runtime's system-prompt assembly gets injection wiring once the lessons capture wiring is in place.

## Plan reference

`docs/agents/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION_PLAN.md` (PR #116). This is **A-PR-B.6** in the learning subsystem.

## Risk

Three additive files. No existing tables or callers touched. Safe to ship as scaffolding.

## Next PR

**A-PR-B.7**: `spiralDetector.ts` + `LessonsPanel.tsx` — closes Subsystem A end-to-end with loop detection that auto-captures spiral lessons, plus the operator panel for inspecting / pinning / deprecating accumulated lessons.

body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #144 (audio chipmunk fix). The audio cadence gate added in #144 used a one-shot snapshot of the first chunk file it found in \`C:\\ProgramData\\Restreamer\\chunks\\\`. Worked twice on dev runs by lucky timing; failed on the main-branch CI run (24965872742) immediately after merge because the S3 uploader holds \`pending_chunks=0\` throughout streaming -- the local-disk window per chunk is <50 ms, and the snapshot just missed every chunk.

The audio fix in v0.3.71 itself is correct and is live on stream.lan; only the CI gate that validates it was racy.

## Changes

- Burst-poll the chunks directory up to 100 attempts at 30 ms intervals (3 s window) per outer-loop iteration starting at \`elapsed >= 30s\`.
- Use \`[System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes\` + \`WriteAllBytes\` so a mid-read prune produces a catchable exception we retry from, instead of writing a truncated snapshot.
- Diagnostic \`Write-Host\` on failure surfaces 'no chunk caught' so the next outer-iteration retry is visible in the log.

## CI evidence (run 24966569926, dev)

\`\`\`
Audio gate snapshot at 30s after 24 attempt(s): chunk_1777238534397_000057.bin (73127 bytes)
Audio sample rate:    44100 Hz
Expected AAC cadence: 23.22 ms (1024 samples / 44100 Hz)
Audio packet count:   43
Audio delta median:   23 ms
Audio delta max:      24 ms
=== Audio PTS cadence GATE PASSED ===
clear-s3 elapsed: 4.3384927s, deleted: 375
=== clear-s3 GATE PASSED: 4.3384927s for 375 objects ===
\`\`\`

24 attempts to catch a transient file at 30 ms each = ~720 ms wall time before a hit. With chunks arriving every ~1.5 s, this is consistent with the expected probability model (~3% per attempt, P(catch at least one in 100) ~ 95%).

## Test plan

- [x] Dev CI green (run 24966569926 -- audio gate caught a chunk and passed; clear-s3 gate also passed)
- [ ] PR CI green
- [ ] After merge: main CI green; v0.3.72 auto-release fires

## Note on v0.3.71

The v0.3.71 binary (audio fix) is live on stream.lan but its GitHub Release was skipped because main CI failed on the now-fixed gate. v0.3.72 includes the same audio fix plus this gate fix, so it supersedes v0.3.71 for fresh-install purposes.
